title: ESPN, Joe Buck strike new deal worth more than $100 million
summary: Fortunately for Joe Buck (and for ESPN), Disney doesn't apply the same rules the Steelers do to redoing contracts after football season has started.
full_text: Fortunately for Joe Buck (and for ESPN), Disney doesn't apply the same rules the Steelers do to redoing contracts after football season has started. Andrew Marchand of The Athletic reports that ESPN and Buck have agreed to a new deal that pays out more than $100 million. In all, the six-year extension is worth roughly $108 million. That's an average of $18 million per year. His current deal pays out $15 million annually. The contract runs through 2032, beyond the expiration of ESPN's current deal with the NFL. Which essentially confirms (as if there was any doubt) that ESPN will emerge from the coming game of broadcast-rights musical chairs with a seat at the table. As Marchand notes, Troy Aikman does not yet have a new deal. Buck and Aikman left Fox together for ESPN in 2022, and there were suggestions last month that they could be a package deal . Aikman's five-year, $90 million contract runs through the Super Bowl, which ESPN/ABC will televise. Aikman was already at $18 million per year. With Buck matching it, Aikman surely will be looking to get to at least $20 million. To go along with whatever he's currently getting as a consultant for the Dolphins.
author: Mike Florio

title: Todd Monken responds to Mike Tomlin: It's not Browns being Browns, it's Browns playing poorly for one week
summary: During the pregame show for Sunday night's matchup between the Cowboys and Giants, new NBC analyst Mike Tomlin quoted one of his former players when talking about Cleveland's ugly 34-10 loss to Jacksonville.
full_text: During the pregame show for Sunday night's matchup between the Cowboys and Giants, new NBC analyst Mike Tomlin quoted one of his former players when talking about Cleveland's ugly 34-10 loss to Jacksonville. "In the words of my friend JuJu Smith-Schuster," Tomlin said, "the Browns is the Browns." Smith-Schuster made those words famous back in 2020, ironically before the Browns then pounded the Tomlin-led Steelers in the wild card round. But the saying has stuck in part because the Browns have had just one winning season since — and even that ended with an ugly postseason loss. Asked about Tomlin’s comments in his Monday video conference, first-year head coach Todd Monken seemed to take some exception to them. “Well, again, everybody’s afforded their opinions. That’s what you do when you go from coaching to television,” Monken said. “ We have to own that . We have to own that. We didn’t play very well. I don’t see it that way, Browns being Browns. I don’t see it that way. Every week is different, every team is different. We just didn’t play well. That’s one week. That’s not Browns being Browns, that’s Browns being poorly on one week. “So, again, everybody’s afforded their opinion. And the only way to change people’s opinion is to play better. That’s a fact. We don’t want to be considered an also-ran, then we have to play better. We have to coach better, and we have to play better.” At this point, Monken is right — the only way the Browns can change their perception is by winning. We’ll see if they can at least be competitive against the Buccaneers on Sunday, though that will be unlikely if Deshaun Watson does not play any better at quarterback.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Senate advances the Protect College Sports Act
summary: ESPN has gotten its apparent wish.
full_text: ESPN has gotten its apparent wish. Partially, for now. The Senate has passed the Protect College Sports Act, by a vote of 74-24. It's a procedural move and not yet a full vote of the Senate. The vote comes three days after ESPN put Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas), one of the bill's sponsors, on its flagship college football show to advocate for the passage of the act, without a contemporaneous opposing point of view. And while Stephen A. Smith has apparently chastised me for suggesting that everyone at ESPN supports the Protect College Sports Act, I don't believe that. It was not my intent to put everyone at ESPN in the same bucket, and I apologize if I created that impression. My point was and is that ESPN's corporate position seems to be that it supports the bill, as evidenced by the fact that two of its most prominent college football analysts (Nick Saban and Pat McAfee) have argued for its passage on GameDay without any real pushback by other panelists, by Disney's reported lobbying for the bill, and by the misguided decision to platform Cruz without offering a voice representing the other side. Here's a thought — they could have let Smith interview Cruz. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) also opposes the Protect College Sports Act. I'll be interviewing him on Thursday morning, for a special edition of #PFTPM. I'd love to chop it up with Stephen A., too. We agree on plenty of things. On the things we disagree, there's a chance that, through open and honest discourse, we'd better understand each other's points of view. The country currently needs a lot more of that. The country does not need a federal law that "saves" college sports, in my opinion. College sports are doing just fine, and the system should be required to clean up its own mess without a federal bailout that artificially limits the compensation and freedom of the people who generate the vast majority of the revenue, while leaving unrestricted the ability of coaches to hopscotch the map in chase of their next bag of cash.
author: Mike Florio

title: Patriots, Mack Hollins agreed to make his 2026 incentives harder to earn
summary: It's going to be a little harder for Patriots receiver Mack Hollins to boost his shoe budget.
full_text: '' It's going to be a little harder for Patriots receiver Mack Hollins to boost his shoe budget. The fact that he doesn’t seem to ever wear them makes that less of a problem. Via Spotrac, the Patriots and Hollins agreed to a 2026 revision that converts some of the potential payments into not-likely-to-be-earned incentives. The move shifts money from the 2026 salary cap to 2027, if the incentives are reached. Previously, Hollins was due to get $300,000 for catching 30 passes, another $300,000 for catching 40, and another $400,000 for catching 50. The new version moves the magic numbers to 47, 50, and 55, respectively. Last year, Hollins caught 46 passes. Which unlocked $600,000 in extra pay. And which made $600,000 of the incentive package "likely to be earned" in 2026, with those dollars counting against the 2026 cap. The new deal was finalized on September 1. Given that Hollins apparently got nothing in return for the adjustment, the leverage to get him to agree would have been a not-so-subtle suggestion that he'd be released before Week 1, when his $2.9 million base salary would have become guaranteed as termination pay. (He also has $750,000 in per-game active roster bonuses.) It's odd to think the Patriots were considering cutting Hollins. Albert Breer of SI.com recently reported that at least one contending team expressed interest in trading for Hollins, and the Patriots declined . Hollins could have forced the issue, become a free agent, and signed with that team (or any other). The likely problem was the timing. Hollins would have been scrambling for a job, at a time when rosters were set. The team that had been interested in trading for him may have addressed its needs elsewhere. And, even if someone would have given Hollins the same terms he had with the Patriots, Hollins would have had to embrace a new city, new team, new coaching staff, new everything only days away from Week 1. The good news for Hollins is that the A.J. Brown injury will give Hollins more opportunities to get toward 47, 50, and/or 55 receptions. In Week 1, Hollins had four catches. That projects to 68 for the season, which would get him the full $1 million — and which would make all of it count against the 2027 cap.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jaguars place B.J. Green on IR, sign Jack Kiser to 53-man roster
summary: The Jaguars have made a few moves on Wednesday morning.
full_text: The Jaguars have made a few moves on Wednesday morning. Jacksonville announced the club has placed defensive end B.J. Green on injured reserve, signed linebacker Jack Kiser to the 53-man roster, and signe defensive end BJ Ojulari to the practice squad. Green is dealing with an elbow injury. He was only able to play a handful of snaps against the Browns on Sunday. He'll now be out for at least the next four weeks. Kiser, a fourth-round pick in 2025, appeared in 14 games for Jacksonville last season, mainly playing on special teams. Ojulari has appeared in 25 games since the Cardinals selected him in the second round of the 2023 draft. He’s registered 5.0 career sacks.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Keenan Allen formally charged with two misdemeanors from August arrest
summary: Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen has been formally charged with a pair of misdemeanors related to his August arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence.
full_text: Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen has been formally charged with a pair of misdemeanors related to his August arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence. According to multiple reports, Allen has been formally charged with with operating a vehicle with an alcohol concentration equivalent (ACE) of 0.15 or more and operating a vehicle while intoxicated. The former charge is a Class A misdemeanor which carries a possible jail sentence of up to one year and a fine of no more than $5000. The other charge can result in a jail term of no more than 60 days and a fine of no more than $500. Colts General Manager Chris Ballard said that any team discipline would be handled internally. Allen also faces possible league discipline, which is typically a three-game suspension for alcohol-related offenses. Nathan Brown of the Indianapolis Star notes that the collective bargaining agreement allows for enhanced penalties given Allen's ACE level. Allen played in last Sunday's loss to the Ravens and had six catches for 32 yards.
author: Josh Alper

title: Could Carson Wentz play his way into the Vikings' QB1 job?
summary: Wentz performed well in Week 1. If it continues, the Vikings could stick with the hot hand.
full_text: Most casual observers of the NFL were surprised to see quarterback Carson Wentz enter Sunday's game for the Vikings after Kyler Murray suffered a concussion on the third drive of the game. There's another potential surprise in the pipeline. If Wentz keeps playing well and winning, he could end up hanging onto the job even after Murray is cleared to return. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network floated that idea on Tuesday night. And it would be a stunner; Wentz was never in the competition to start, if the competition between Murray and J.J. McCarthy was even a real competition. (It likely wasn't.) Last year, when Wentz was playing in place of McCarthy, who suffered an ankle sprain in Week 2, there was a sense that Wentz could keep the job even after McCarthy was ready to play. The key factor in that was simple — Wentz and receiver Justin Jefferson had a more effective in-game connection than McCarthy and Jefferson. A season-ending injury to Wentz's left shoulder, through which he played for multiple weeks, ended that debate. This year, a fresh debate could emerge — if Murray can't return for Sunday's game against the Bears and if Wentz can engineer an upset at Soldier Field. Rapoport calls the possibility an "excellent problem." Still, the best problem is no problem at all. It won't be easy to manage Murray if he believes he lost his job over a concussion suffered on the third drive of the opening game of the season. In the end, however, it's all about winning games. If Wentz keeps winning, maybe he'll keep playing. Either way, the Vikings have a pair of top-two draft picks who grew up rooting for the team. Murray, for now, isn't healthy enough to play. Wentz is. He'll get an opportunity to extend his run if he can continue to run the offense in a way that helps Minnesota score more points than the other team. Which, in a numbers-driven league, continues to be the only statistic that matters.
author: Mike Florio

title: DeMeco Ryans on Texans defense: I don't believe in hype, this isn't 2025, we have to earn it
summary: Leading up to the 2026 season, there was plenty of talk about how good the Texans defense could be — that the unit could help lead Houston to a deep postseason run.
full_text: Leading up to the 2026 season, there was plenty of talk about how good the Texans defense could be — that the unit could help lead Houston to a deep postseason run. But then Week 1 happened, with the Texans letting up 409 yards and 36 points in the loss to the Bills. Buffalo does have one of the league’s best quarterbacks in Josh Allen and continuity on offense with former coordinator Joe Brady getting promoted to head coach. So the Bills have the potential to do that to many teams. Still, it was a disappointing opening for a team that finished No. 1 in yards allowed and No. 2 in points allowed last year. So did the Texans buy into the offseason hype too much? Did they consume the proverbial rat poison? “I don't know,” head coach DeMeco Ryans said in his Monday press conference, via transcript from the team. “You have to ask those guys about the hype. I don't believe in hype. You've heard me stand here many times and talk about people talking about how great the defense was. Yeah, that was 2025. You don't just line up, and it's 2026, and just because you were good last year, you got to go out and make the plays. We made plays. “The difference in this game on Sunday, versus the time we played the guys last year, we took the ball away three times. We go into this game, we don't take the ball away at all. We turn the ball over two times and we don't play smart defensively. We're not where we're supposed to be. We know the quarterback is going to scramble out to our left — if we don't stay out to our left and the quarterback runs for a touchdown, they're going to make plays.” Ryans added that whatever Houston does this year, it’s not about how good the unit has been in the past. “You have to put your stamp each and every year on who you're going to be,” Ryans said. “This is a new team. This isn't 2025. You have to go earn it. That's every year in the league, you have to go prove yourself. You can talk about it all you want to, how good you want to be, what are you going to do. You have to go out and make plays. “That's always been my message. My message never changes. Talk never matters. When the ball is snapped, what are you doing?” The Texans will be challenged defensively once again in Week 2, as the Bengals will be in town to face the club at 1 p.m. ET.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Bills and Texans each fumbled twice, Bills recovered all four on way to 36-31 win
summary: Bills coach Joe Brady cited the importance of O'Cyrus Torrence recovering James Cook's fumble on the game-winning drive.
full_text: The Bills' 36-31 win over the Texans could have gone the other way if some fumbled footballs had bounced a little differently. Both teams fumbled twice in the game, and the Bills recovered all four fumbles. In a one-possession game that was decided when the Bills recovered C.J. Stroud's second fumble with nine seconds left, any one of those fumbles landing in a Texan's hands could have altered the outcome. All four fumbles going the other way almost certainly would have given the Texans the win. Another crucial fumble recovery came when Bills running back James Cook put the ball on the ground with three minutes left in the fourth quarter and the Bills trailing 31-30. If the Texans had recovered that, they might have been able to run out the clock and win the game. Instead, Bills offensive lineman O'Cyrus Torrence recovered the fumble and the Bills scored the game-winning touchdown later in that drive. Bills head coach Joe Brady noted that the hustle of Torrence, whom the team calls Cyborg or Cybo, was crucial to the win. "We put the ball on the ground there," Brady said. "If our offensive line isn't doing the little things we ask and run to the football, and Cybo doesn't recover that football, and we end up losing that game, a lot of people will point to the fact that we fumbled. And we did fumble. It can't be just because we won the football game that, 'Oh, that didn't happen, we had no turnovers.'" Brady said Cook was mad at himself for fumbling and that the Bills aren't overlooking how fortunate they were on fumble recoveries. "He was pissed. I talked to him on the plane. He knows how important he is to our football team," Brady said of Cook. "He understands that when he has the ball he has all of our jobs on the line. He was not happy after that. Even through the win, we've got to clean that up." Brady knows the Bills can't count on recovering 100 percent of fumbles every week.
author: Michael David Smith

author: Mike Florio

title: Dan Campbell: It's special to be part of first game at new Bills stadium
summary: The Bills will be playing their first regular season game at the new Highmark Stadium on Thursday night and the Lions drew the spot as the guests of honor for opening night.
full_text: The Bills will be playing their first regular season game at the new Highmark Stadium on Thursday night and the Lions drew the spot as the guests of honor for opening night. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said on Tuesday that his message to the team's players about getting the opportunity to be part of the festivities is to "drink it in [and] enjoy this." He also said players will need to take care to avoid being overwhelmed by the situation. "This will be one of those places it'll be loud. Their fanbase is outstanding ," Campbell said, via the team's website. "They are a lot like our fanbase, man. They love it and they show up and they're loud and they're all in and now you're in a new stadium. It's a new environment and this is the first one in that place — the christening. It'll be special. I'm telling our guys to embrace it. Keep your composure. Don't forget it's one play at a time. Stay focused on your job and keep your head about you, but man, enjoy it." Buffalo would be a tough place to play on a short week in any circumstances, but the atmosphere will be even more heightened for this Lions visit.
author: Josh Alper

title: Charvarius Ward embraces Guardian Cap in hopes of avoiding another concussion
summary: After the 2025 season, Colts cornerback Charvarius Ward said that, if he gets another concussion, he'll "probably retire."
full_text: ' After the 2025 season, Colts cornerback Charvarius Ward said that, if he gets another concussion, he'll " probably retire ." To avoid that, he decided to try a Guardian Cap during the Week 1 game against the Ravens. "I was scared to get knocked out again for real," Ward said earlier this week, via James Boyd of The Athletic . "So I just put a Guardian Cap on. I warmed up with it, and it felt good . . . I just kept it on all game. So I might as well keep it for the season . It's not gonna hurt me." The real question is whether it helps. "I don’t know if it made a difference or not," Ward said. "I got a headache right now. I don't think it's a concussion, but it is what it is. It's football, man. You're gonna get dinged up . . . I know what I signed up for." The full benefits of the Guardian Cap aren't known. It helps with low-impact hits to the helmet. For bigger blows, will it make a difference? One thing no helmet can do is prevent the brain from bouncing against the skull when the head quickly decelerates. Which is one way to get a concussion. The NFL has a somewhat complicated relationship with the Guardian Cap. When the device was first adopted for use in practice, the league prevented players from wearing them during games. That position has changed; there are now one or two players in most games who can be seen wearing one. The league is keenly aware of the aesthetics of the Guardian Cap. They're bulky. They diminish the appearance of the helmet. Even the new model, which doesn't require a cover for placement of logos and stripes, doesn't look the same as the helmet. As helmets improve, the argument is that they are as effective as prior technology plus a Guardian Cap. But, still, the Guardian Cap will always provide an additional layer of cushioning. And it's impossible to tell a player who wants to wear one that he can't do it. Even if it doesn't help that much. Even if it can create a false sense of security. Even if it doesn't look great on TV. At this point, if it helps a player like Ward break the tie between continuing his career and not playing, it needs to be among the available pieces of protective equipment for a game that is inherently hazardous to the human brain.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles restructure Nolan Smith's contract
summary: The Eagles have created some cap space for this season and next season.
full_text: The Eagles have created some cap space for this season and next season. The team has restructured the contract of linebacker Nolan Smith. Spotrac reports that converting $1.24 million of his 2026 salary created $992,000 in cap space for the rest of this season. Smith also had $12.5 million of his salary for 2027 — the Eagles exercised their fifth-year option on his rookie deal — converted to a bonus. That move opened up $10 million in cap space for next season. The Eagles may or may not have their eye on making an immediate addition to the roster, but the restructuring gives the that option and the extra cap space in 2027 can help General Manager Howie Roseman structure things in a way that keeps the Eagles in compliance with the cap now and in the future.
author: Josh Alper

title: Bills DL T.J. Sanders misses practice with an illness
summary: Bills defensive lineman T.J.
full_text: '' Bills defensive lineman T.J. Sanders did not play in Week 1 due to a knee injury and a different issue kept him off the field on Tuesday. Sanders did not participate in practice because of an illness that led the team to send him home. Sanders had been listed as a limited participant in practice on Monday. author: Josh Alper

title: Broncos seem to be nervous about a potential Drew Brees tampering case
summary: On Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported that the Broncos talked to quarterback Drew Brees about joining the team for the AFC Championship, without acknowledging that Brees's status on the Saints' reserve-retired list made the move impossible.
full_text: On Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported that the Broncos talked to quarterback Drew Brees about joining the team for the AFC Championship, without acknowledging that Brees's status on the Saints' reserve-retired list made the move impossible . What is possible, based on Schefter's report, is a tampering case against the Broncos. Schefter reported that former Broncos offensive coordinator Joe Lombardi and former Broncos offensive assistant Pete Carmichael spoke to Brees about a potential unretirement. Brees has since told Ed Werder that the former Saints assistants contacted Brees about the possibility. On Tuesday, Broncos coach Sean Payton offered a different version regarding who called whom. "Drew had reached out, I think, right after the championship or right after the playoff win against Buffalo," Payton told reporters. "I think he called Pete, probably texted Pete or Joe, those guys. None of it even came to my attention. So, when the story came up in Canton, I kept thinking they were just talking about the COVID season. Even in the COVID season when he and I discussed possibly coming back for a Monday night game, he had trouble throwing it. So, I don’t think really anything really came of it. I think in Drew’s mind, there’s that competitor in him. So, I was kind of out of the loop. I don’t think it’s a big story, but nonetheless, certainly one that once they described it to me, it just never got to my level, I guess. He had reached out to Pete, I think, and then Joe.” Payton is smart. Very smart. The last thing he needs is the league office thinking the Broncos reached out to a player who is technically under contract with the Saints, without permission from the Saints. Even if the Saints don't file a tampering complaint, the league can act without one. For example, the NFL whacked the Dolphins in 2022 for tampering after it stumbled over evidence that Miami had tampered with Payton and Tom Brady while investigating an unrelated matter. And while it technically doesn't matter if Lombardi and/or Carmichael contacted Brees or Brees contacted them, the situation has a different vibe if someone from the Broncos made the first move without first realizing that Brees wasn't and isn't a free agent. Time will tell if the league does anything about it. The Broncos' effort to recast the interaction as being initiated by Brees suggests that, at some level, the Broncos are concerned about coming under the inconsistent and unpredictable scrutiny of Big Shield.
author: Mike Florio

title: Commanders to sign OL Lucas Patrick
summary: The Commanders are adding a veteran offensive lineman to the roster ahead of their Week 2 game in Dallas.
full_text: The Commanders are adding a veteran offensive lineman to the roster ahead of their Week 2 game in Dallas. According to multiple reports, they are signing Lucas Patrick. Patrick was in camp with the Giants and missed time with a knee injury before being released at the end of the summer. Patrick played in six games for the Bengals in 2025 and appeared in 107 games for the Packers, Bears and Saints earlier in his career. He has made 65 career starts while seeing time at guard and center. The Commanders add experienced depth with the move. Nick Allegretti started at center in Week 1 with Chris Paul and Sam Cosmi next to him at the guard spots.
author: Josh Alper

title: Joe Brady: No concerns about Highmark Stadium field for Thursday night
summary: The condition of the playing field at the new Highmark Stadium became a talking point after the Bills played their first preseason game at the building this summer.
full_text: The condition of the playing field at the new Highmark Stadium became a talking point after the Bills played their first preseason game at the building this summer. Some players aired concerns about the size and frequency of divots that came up during the course of play, which led the Bills to replace the field ahead of Thursday night's inaugural regular season game against the Lions. The Bills worked out at the stadium on Tuesday and head coach Joe Brady said that the team will not go into the game with reservations about the condition of the field. “I really don't have many concerns with it,” Brady said, via Jay Skurski of the Buffalo News . “There wasn't a lot of concerns with it the first go around with it in terms of there was stuff that was moving. I credit our leadership that I understand that they want to have the best surface out there and be able to make the decision and kind of go with it. But, yeah there’ll be no concerns come Thursday. Our guys are excited just to be on grass.” Linebacker Greg Rousseau agreed with Brady's closing statement and said he believes "it'll be smooth" based on Tuesday's experience. The Bills will be hoping that's the case so they can avoid the playing surface overshadowing anything about the game itself in the aftermath of the home opener.
author: Josh Alper

title: Ben Johnson suggests he wanted Bears to score 60 points at Carolina
summary: The Bears scored 59 points on Sunday at Carolina.
full_text: The Bears scored 59 points on Sunday at Carolina. Just one point short of a whopping 60 points. In a Monday interview of coach Ben Johnson on ESPN 1000, Jeff Joniak said this about the 59-37 win over the Panthers: "At that point I was hoping for 60. I was thinking a two-point try at some point." Johnson paused, smiled, and said, " I don’t think you were the only one ." It's on brand for Johnson. He wants to score a lot of points. He wants to blow teams out. Whenever, wherever, however. Having a shot at getting to 60 is rare. For the 2026 Bears, it may not be. And there's a good chance that, the next time his team is in striking distance of the number, maybe they will try to get there.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jacoby Brissett leads the NFL in passing yards since becoming the Cardinals' starter
summary: Brissett's 277 passing yards on Sunday helped the Cardinals beat the Chargers.
full_text: In Week 6 of last season, Jacoby Brissett started for the Cardinals for the first time in place of an injured Kyler Murray. What Brissett has done since then is something no one would have expected: Brissett has led the NFL in passing yards. After his 277-yard game in Sunday's win over the Chargers, Brissett now has 3,643 passing yards in 13 games since becoming the Cardinals' starter. That's the most of any quarterback in the league during that time. Brissett ranks ahead of Jared Goff (3,583 yards), Dak Prescott (3,371 yards) and Matthew Stafford (3,359 yards), who are the quarterbacks with the next-most passing yards since Week 6 of last season. Although the Cardinals were not a good football team down the stretch last year, Brissett has played well, completing 65.6 percent of his passes, with 24 touchdowns and eight interceptions. Brissett won't have an easy task on Sunday, with the Seahawks coming to Arizona, but after the Cardinals' upset of the Chargers on Sunday, this Cardinals team may be better than people think, with a quarterback who's better than people think.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Arch Manning apologizes for "insensitive comment" about AI video from Saturday's game
summary: Saturday was a good day for Texas quarterback Arch Manning.
full_text: Saturday was a good day for Texas quarterback Arch Manning. Monday was not. On Tuesday, he moved to rectify an unforced error. Via ESPN, Manning apologized for making an " insensitive comment " about an AI video that showed Texas coach Steve Sarkisian violently slapping ESPN sideline reporter Holly Rowe. At a Monday press conference, Manning was asked if he'd seen any fan clips from the comeback win over Ohio State. "I've seen a few AI edits of stuff , but that's about it," Manning said. "I saw an AI edit of Sark's interview. Have y'all seen that one? That's a good one. Of him slapping Holly Rowe? It's hilarious." The remark sparked a backlash, given the jarring video of Sarkisian hitting Rowe. Manning posted his apology on social media. "In my press conference yesterday, I made an insensitive comment about an AI video," Manning said. "There is nothing funny about it. It's easy to say I didn't mean it, but I know my words and actions were hurtful to a lot of people. I do not take that lightly and am deeply sorry for that. "I specifically want to apologize to Holly Rowe for what she has personally had to deal with because of my comments. I have a ton of respect for her and appreciate her showing me grace in this moment. I need to do better and will be more thoughtful going forward." Rowe accepted Manning's apology. The unedited video was bizarre in its own right. Sarkisian waited to be interviewed by Rowe and stormed away before she could ask a question.
author: Mike Florio

title: Victim in Josh Jacobs case files motion to permanently seal video
summary: Latest move could make it harder for NFL to see the video.
full_text: Previously, lawyers representing Packers running back Josh Jacobs filed a motion seeking to keep evidence in his criminal case from being released to the public. The victim in the case has now done the same thing. But while the current order is temporary in nature, the new motion filed on behalf of Jacobs's former girlfriend seeks to have the evidence in the case — including a key video — permanently sealed. Via Rob Demovsky of ESPN, her lawyers said Tuesday that the motion "is consistent with our client's desire to protect her privacy ." The motion complicates the NFL's effort to obtain the video. On Sunday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network said that the league is " trying all sorts of legal maneuvers " to get the video. One fairly direct maneuver would be to file an opposition to the motion, with a request for a limited opportunity to inspect the video subject to the requirements of a strict and comprehensive confidentiality order. And the league should ask Jacobs to join in the effort. Common sense suggests that the harder Jacobs tries to keep the league from seeing the video, the worse to his ongoing career it may be. If the league decides to take an aggressive approach to the situation, the league could tell Jacobs that he'll remain on paid leave until the league processes his disciplinary case — and that the case won't be processed until the NFL sees the video.
author: Mike Florio

title: Chargers to sign WR Marquez Valdes-Scantling to practice squad
summary: The Chargers are signing wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports.
full_text: The Chargers are signing wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling to their practice squad, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN reports. Valdes-Scantling, 31, spent training camp with the Cowboys, but they released him on cutdown day. The Chargers needed help at the position after injuries to wide receivers Ladd McConkey (rib), KeAndre Lambert-Smith (hamstring) and Derius Derives (undisclosed). Lambert-Smith landed on injured reserve Tuesday. The Chargers replaced Lambert-Smith on the active roster by signing wide receiver Gary Jennings from the practice squad. The Packers selected Valdes-Scantling in the fifth round in 2018, and he spent his first four seasons in Green Bay. He has also played for the Chiefs, Bills, Saints, 49ers and Steelers. Valdes-Scantling has totaled 219 receptions for 3,686 yards and 21 touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Commanders LB Frankie Luvu has minor groin strain
summary: Commanders linebacker Frankie Luvu has a minor groin strain, according to multiple reports.
full_text: Commanders linebacker Frankie Luvu has a minor groin strain, according to multiple reports. His availability for Sunday's game against the Cowboys remains uncertain, but it is not expected to be a long-term injury. Luvu totaled four tackles and a sack on 29 snaps before his injury. Leo Chenal replaced him, and rookie Sonny Styles took over the green-dot duties. Tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring), safety Tyler Owens (ankle) and linebacker Jordan Magee (hamstring) also left Sunday's game with injuries. Coach Dan Quinn did not provide injury updates Monday. The Commanders worked out seven players on Tuesday, including four linebackers and two tight ends.
author: Charean Williams

title: LB Kenneth Murray to join Texans' practice squad
summary: Linebacker Kenneth Murray has found a job.
full_text: Linebacker Kenneth Murray has found a job. The former first-round draft pick is joining the Texans' practice squad, Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports. The Texans needed help at the position after they placed Henry To'oTo'o on injured reserve. Murray, a Houston native, visited the Texans on Tuesday before agreeing to terms. He worked out for the Giants and Dolphins this offseason, but had remained a free agent since March. Murray started at middle linebacker for the Cowboys last season, finishing with 81 tackles, four tackles for loss, three quarterback hits and two pass breakups. The Chargers made Murray the 23rd overall pick in 2020, and he spent his four seasons with the team. He played one season with the Titans before the Cowboys acquired him in a trade with Tennessee.
author: Charean Williams

title: Chargers put WR KeAndre Lambert-Smith on IR
summary: Wide receiver KeAndre Lambert-Smith injured his hamstring in Sunday's loss to the Cardinals and he's going to be out of action for at least the next month as a result.
full_text: Wide receiver KeAndre Lambert-Smith injured his hamstring in Sunday's loss to the Cardinals and he's going to be out of action for at least the next month as a result. The Chargers placed Lambert-Smith on injured reserve on Tuesday. Lambert-Smith played two snaps on special teams against Arizona. Lambert-Smith was a fifth-round pick last year. He had five catches for 51 yards and a touchdown in 10 games as a rookie. The Chargers filled the open roster spot by signing wide receiver Gary Jennings off of their practice squad. Jennings played in one game for the Dolphins in 2019 and more recently saw action in the UFL. Cornerback Isas Waxter was signed to the practice squad to complete the day's moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles sign WR Britain Covey to 53-man roster
summary: The Eagles officially placed guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve Tuesday and they pulled a player up from the practice squad in a corresponding move.
full_text: The Eagles officially placed guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve Tuesday and they pulled a player up from the practice squad in a corresponding move. Wide receiver Britain Covey has been signed to the 53-man roster in Philadelphia. Covey played in Week 1 as a temporary elevation and returned four punts for 37 yards in the 24-22 win over the Commanders. Covey appeared in 44 other games for the Eagles over the past four seasons. He has a career average of 11.2 yards per punt return. The Eagles also announced that they have signed tight end Josiah Deguara to the practice squad. They still have one open spot on the 53-man roster after placing tight end Eli Stowers on injured reserve last weekend.
author: Josh Alper

title: Giants-Cowboys delivers 25.7 million viewers
summary: The first Sunday of Week 1 ended with the latest installment of the Cowboys-Giants rivalry.
full_text: The first Sunday of Week 1 ended with the latest installment of the Cowboys-Giants rivalry. As expected, it drew a big crowd. The game averaged 25.7 million viewers on NBC and Peacock. It made 2026 the first year since 2015 with both the kickoff game and the Week 1 Sunday night game at 25 million or more. Viewership peaked at 29.0 million in the second quarter, from 9:00 to 9:15 p.m. ET. It was also the most-watched Week 1 Sunday night game since 2015, when the Cowboys hosted the Giants. It was a four-percent bump over last year's Ravens-Bills classic, which Buffalo stormed back to win, 41-40. The Patriots-Seahawks game to open the season on Wednesday night averaged 25.1 million viewers.

title: NFL Week 2 odds, picks: Jets continue to stay frisky, while Baker Mayfield torches former Browns team
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 2 schedule, plus five locks against the spread
full_text:
We are off and running in the 2026 regular season and are coming off an opening weekend where we escaped Week 1 with a stellar record on the whole. For the slate, I went 13-3 on straight-up picks and 9-7 ATS. That was good for the best among CBS Sports experts straight up and tied for second against the spread.
The only unfortunate aspect of my weekend was that some of the locks within my five Locks of the Week were faulty. I was 2-3 ATS on my five best bets, with the Jets ' upset win in Nashville and Jacksonville's throttling of the Browns as the lone covers. The Houston Texans nearly swung the day for us as they had the Buffalo Bills on the ropes, but Josh Allen was simply too much to slay, so we'll look to keep the overall momentum rolling in Week 2 while cleaning things up with my locks.
As we turn our attention to the upcoming slate, we're somewhat going back to the well with a couple of teams, attacking the Browns and buying the Jets with the points.
It seems like Cooper Rush is going to get another start for Atlanta, so we'll gladly fade him after a rough debut with the Falcons in Week 1. Out of every starting quarterback that took the field in Week 1, no one has a worse passer rating than Rush (54.9). There was essentially no vertical passing game as Rush averaged just 3.5 air yards per attempt (31st among QBs). Despite that, he still had an off-target rate of 13.6% (22nd). So, while the Panthers ' defense was pantsed by the Bears in Week 1 to the tune of 59 points allowed, they won't face nearly the firepower under center as they did when squaring up against Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams . Meanwhile, lost in the Bears lighting it up, Bryce Young put together a strong effort, with his .29 EPA per dropback ranking sixth-highest among all quarterbacks in Week 1. The Panthers QB also owns a 4-1 SU and ATS record when he starts against Atlanta.
Projected score: Panthers 24, Falcons 20 The pick: Panthers -1
Listen, this might be the last time in our lives that we'll be able to bet against Deshaun Watson , so we HAVE to take this opportunity while it's still there. The Browns QB looked about as you'd expect him to look in the opening loss to Jacksonville. He didn't seem comfortable in the pocket at all, tossed an interception on his opening possession, and nearly had two more turnovers. Dating to before his Achilles injuries, Watson is 0-6 SU and 1-5 ATS over his last six starts. Meanwhile, the Browns are 1-10 ATS in their last 11 road games when they are a dog of 6-plus points.
While Watson won't provide much resistance for the Bucs defense, old friend Baker Mayfield is likely chomping at the bit to square off against his former team. This will be just the second game against Cleveland since he was traded in the summer of 2022. Mayfield lost his first matchup against the Browns while a member of the Panthers, but has since revitalized his career in Tampa and will likely be looking to run it up with his college of skill-position players. The Bucs are 3-0 SU in home openers with Mayfield.
Projected score: Buccaneers 30, Browns 13 The pick: Buccaneers -8.5
It's hard to call a Week 2 matchup a kitchen-sink game or any team, but I sort of feel that way with the Patriots. They completely collapsed in the fourth quarter and lost a winnable game against the Seahawks in the season opener. After this game on Sunday, they'll begin a two-week road trip where they'll head to Jacksonville and Buffalo. The Patriots shouldn't expect to be favored in either of those matchups, so if they drop this home opener to Pittsburgh, they're looking down the barrel of a potential 0-4 start.
While they did lose A.J. Brown (ankle) to injury, I think New England should be able to outpace the Steelers ' offense. Aaron Rodgers was tied for the fourth-worst EPA per dropback in the NFL in Week 1 as the Pittsburgh offense averaged just 4.1 yards per play against Atlanta. The Patriots boast a far better defense than the Falcons, with All-Pro corner Christian Gonzalez and a pass rush that was surprisingly disruptive in Week 1.
Remember, the Steelers went into Foxborough in Week 3 last year and pulled out a 21-14 win. In that loss, the Patriots turned the ball over five (!) times. Mike Vrabel will almost certainly remind them of that game and push them to right the wrong here.
Drake Maye is also 6-0 SU and 5-1 ATS as a 3-plus point favorite at home in his career.
Projected score: Patriots 24, Steelers 17 The pick: Patriots -5.5
Can you believe it? We're backing the Jets in back-to-back weeks! Did we slip into the Twilight Zone or something? Unlike last week, however, we're not taking them to pull off the outright win (although I was tempted). Instead, we're looking for them to merely cover as they host the Packers in the home opener. While it was against Tennessee, New York looked far improved from last year's squad. Specifically, they got stable quarterback play from Geno Smith , who was the only quarterback in the entire Week 1 slate to not have an off-target throw. Meanwhile, the defense showed signs of life, specifically with No. 2 overall pick David Bailey tallying a sack in his debut.
As we look at Green Bay, I just don't have a lot of faith in the Packers right now as a road favorite. They collapsed against the Vikings , and Jordan Love did not look good in the process. In stark contrast to Smith, Love's off-target rate was the highest among every quarterback in Week 1 (23.8%). On top of throwing an interception against Minnesota, the Vikings dropped two others, so it was nearly an even more disastrous day for the Packers' quarterback.
They may win because they have a smidge more talent, but it'll be within the number.
Projected score: Packers 24, Jets 21 The pick: Jets +3.5
Maybe it's a trap, but I don't care. I'll fade Cam Ward and the Titans until they give me a reason not to. Ward ranked 26th in the league in Week 1 in EPA per dropback as well as off-target rate in a loss to New York at home. He was sacked three times in the opener, and will now face an Eagles front that will continue to apply pressure. Tennessee scored just 10 points in Week 1, which was the fewest point total in a season opener at home in franchise history. It's hard to imagine this unit suddenly finding success against a superior defense that took it to them on Sunday.
Meanwhile, Breece Hall averaged 4.6 yards per carry while piling up 102 yards and a touchdown on the ground against Robert Saleh's defense in Week 1, and I expect Saquon Barkley to carry the baton with a similar showing in Week 2. This should be a double-digit win by Philadelphia.

title: Cowboys' Caleb Downs explains why historically bad Week 1 defense is 'very fixable'
summary: Dallas produced one of the NFL's worst defensive performances since the start of 2025, but its first-round rookie says the mistakes are correctable
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys entered the 2026 season full of hope for a new era of defense. After firing defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus , Dallas hired 34-year-old, longtime Vic Fangio staffer Christian Parker, and also revamped its roster. Nearly half, 46.2%, per the Dallas Morning News , of the snaps taken on Dallas' defense in 2025 are no longer on the team.
However, the on-field performance was more of the same in a 28-20 road loss to the New York Giants . New York converted 82% of its third downs, with one of those stops being the game-ending knee down. That figure was New York's best third-down conversion rate in a single game since 1978.
Based on defensive expected points added (EPA)/ per drive in TruMedia, the Cowboys delivered the worst effort by any team in Week 1, and it was worse than all of their defensive games last year. Of the 576 defensive performances since the start of the 2025 season, it ranked 574th. Their seven defensive possessions yielded four touchdowns, one takeaway via fumble recovery, a punt and the game ending.
So how did the Cowboys' latest stinker happen after all that change?
"To lose contain on a guy like Jaxson (Dart) that is that athletic, and it was multiple guys at multiple times. ... We have Jayden [Daniels and the Washington Commanders ] this week, and then you guys have maybe heard of Lamar Jackson [and the Baltimore Ravens ] coming in a couple weeks. So we certainly have to get better with our discipline," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "The other thing that I will say, looking at the game, that we need to be better in is our communication on defense. ... Communication is two parts. It's the person that gives [the call], and the person that receives it has to acknowledge it. Some of the things that we did in the red zone late where we didn't have anybody accounting for [running back Devin] Singletary, who is a pretty dynamic player. Those were communication issues. That can't happen because those are self-inflicted wounds that get you beat."
In an otherwise forgettable night, the debut of 11th overall pick Caleb Downs was a positive one. The ex-Ohio State safety racked up seven total tackles, one sack and one forced fumble. Dart targeted Downs once and completed a pass for five yards on the rookie's 29 coverage snaps, per TruMedia. In college, Downs was relied on to help with on-field communication, and he didn't put the blame on Parker, a first-time defensive coordinator, not getting the call in fast enough.
"I think it's just first-game execution honestly," Downs told CBS Sports related to Week 1 communication. "I don't necessarily think it's not getting a call or anything like that. I think it's just making sure we're detailed in our work and doing our jobs at the highest level more so than anything else. Just executing our job is the biggest thing."
While Schottenheimer had plenty to gripe about with his defense after Week 1, Downs wasn't one of them. He's already in love with his ability to harass the quarterback, something he did with a strip sack of Dart with 2:36 left in the first half. Unfortunately for the Cowboys, New York jumped on the football as it did on three of the four fumbles Dallas forced.
"I think Caleb played really, really well," Schottenheimer said. "Jaxson Dart never saw him on the blitz. He gets a free run and the ball goes spiraling through the air, and the 320-pound guard [Jon Runyan Jr.] catches it and rumbles for five yards. That's kind of how the night went for us. I think that's one of the positives of what we did on defense: we attacked the ball. We had four forced fumbles. ... Caleb is a guy that can move around, but we like him down near the line of scrimmage."
Caleb Downs with a HUGE hit on Jaxson Dart 😤 DALvsNYG on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6x4h1EbLxb
Early in the game, Downs functioned as a safety in Dallas' base defense and then closer to the line as a nickel corner/hybrid linebacker near the line of scrimmage in sub-packages. That's how former NFL coach Matt Patricia, now Ohio State's defensive coordinator, used him as a chess piece up and down the field.
"Yeah, a lot similar to college, being able to move around," Downs said. "So being able to play, whether it's nickel, being able to play safety and then third down, being able to play dime as well. I think just being able to make plays wherever you're at, that's the biggest thing. So I have confidence in my ability, and that's what I'm going to go out and do."
Dallas' plan at deep safety with Malik Hooker sidelined for what they hope is only a couple of weeks with a forearm fracture is to have seven-year veteran P.J. Locke fill in at that spot so that Downs can be freed up to play more of his hybrid role along the line of scrimmage.
"I think I can play the run game really well. Play the pass game, whatever it is, whether it's man or dropping zones," Downs said. "I'm an extra corner or extra linebacker. Whatever you need."
The Cowboys trust Downs to handle whatever they throw at him because of the way he attacks watching film and preparing himself to play each and every week.
"Man, [I] probably sound like a broken record. The way he prepares, the way he practices is not like, I don't want to say any. It's not like most rookies I've been around. It's different. There's a different mindset," Schottenheimer said entering Week 1. "There's a different competitive fire in this kid. He craves coaching. He cannot get coached enough. And I think at the end of the day, that's why he's such a good player. I think you look at him and just the way he's always played the game, he plays it with instincts. ... He works his butt off at studying the X and the O's part of it. So unique young man, very special talent."
Downs and Parker are the two new faces of the Cowboys' defense, along with four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . They walked off the bus together at MetLife Stadium Sunday night, and Downs sees symmetry in their career trajectories.
"We're going through the same journey at the same time," Downs said. "It's my first season, and it's his first season calling the plays and being the defensive coordinator. So I think there's a lot of similarities there, and we're just trying to succeed at what we do, and that's the biggest thing."
After their deflating primetime defeat, Parker pulled Downs aside immediately after landing back home to talk about what needs to change entering Week 2 against the Washington Commanders.
"When we got off the plane for a couple minutes, just talking about some of the things we needed to correct for this coming week and really just basic defense," Downs said. "How we need to adjust and do certain things. Just talking about this coming week and how we're going to prepare a little bit differently."
Downs' tone when describing that chat oozed with confidence. Why? Because there is a belief that the issue that plagued them in Week 1 can be course-corrected shortly.
"Everything that we made mistakes on is very fixable," Downs said. "Defense is pretty simple. At the end of the day, it's not like we're playing rocket science. It's just we got to do our jobs when we're on the field, and that's the biggest thing."
Schottenheimer had a similarly productive chat both after the game and on Monday back home at The Star, Dallas' team facility. He came away from that conversation feeling convinced he made the right choice to hire Parker.
"He and I were on the same page with that, which is a good thing," Schottenheimer said. "And then this morning he was amazing with the staff and having hard conversations and real conversations. "And this is not just the players, this is us as a staff. That's a leader. That's a leader of men. ... I'm around him every day. ... I have no question Christian Parker is the right guy for this job. He's an outstanding coach. He will learn from this, just like our young players are going to learn from this. We're going to play our young players this…

title: Ranking the five best 2026 NFL Draft classes after Week 1: Chiefs rookies shine brightest
summary: These five teams' rookies produced the most during Week 1 of the NFL season
full_text:
They say you can't evaluate a draft class until after three seasons. Unfortunately, it's 2026, and no one has that much patience anymore, so how about we do it after one week? As always, the caveat is: this is one game. This is not the end-all, be-all. But with most things, it's better to look good early on than bad.
These are the top-five draft classes after the first week of the season.
Highlight: Peter Woods rare athleticism Lowlight: Mansoor Delane's shoulder injury
There were whispers about Brett Veach having another masterclass draft last April, and they've now turned into roars. Peter Woods was already making special plays as a pass-rusher and in the run game. He also chased down a running back from behind on a flat route. His addition will allow Steve Spagnuolo to be more measured with how many snaps they give to 32-year-old Chris Jones going forward.
Peter Woods with one of the most athletic recoveries vs. a double team you'll ever see from a DT pic.twitter.com/CdMDIiJ7CB
Top-10 corner Mansoor Delane unfortunately left the game after three snaps with a shoulder injury, but the injury occurred on a play where he ran a dig route for Courtland Sutton and picked off a pass.
Mansoor Delane Every Snap in NFL Debut vs Broncos pic.twitter.com/0rrFJYFzhS
Then there was second-round edge rusher R Mason Thomas , who had a crucial sack in a two-minute drill before the half, where he teleported underneath Mike McGlinchey with a spin move.
Rookie R Mason Thomas with the spin move right into a sack 💪 DENvsKC on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mVVJ07s2NB
Oh, and then Day 3 running back Emmett Johnson made as many people miss on two catches Monday night (six) as Isiah Pacheco and Kareem Hunt on 37 combined catches last season. It's hard to swing and hit harder than the Chiefs did with their first three picks, at least in Monday night's win.
Highlight: Austin Barber locking down right guard Lowlight: KC Concepcion's ball security
Lost in the ugliness of the Browns quarterback position was the fact that the Browns look like they've clocked yet another impressive draft haul. The Browns have four starters on offense from the 2026 draft class in Spencer Fano , Austin Barber, KC Concepcion, and Denzel Boston , with Emmanuel McNeil-Warren filling in for 14 snaps defensively. While they weren't as obviously slam dunks as the Chiefs, there were big-time flashes for all of the offensive starters.
Concepcion, in particular, already looks like the Browns' best playmaker. His ability to separate was on full display.
KC Concepcion consistently shows strength & fluidity when running routes. Being able to stem inside, get vertical to the proper depth, and roll into this deep sail route all while a defender on the hip isn’t easy. pic.twitter.com/rdEsYTGOJi
While he didn't have any drops that he was known for in college, Concepcion did have an ugly fumble, which was also a problem for him in school, with four fumbles on 185 career receptions.
The most surprising standout was third-rounder Barber. A career tackle at Florida, Barber kicked inside and flipped to the right side for the Browns. He was incredibly clean for a rookie in his first career start. PFF had him as the highest-graded rookie offensive lineman of the week. While there were more concerns on tape than that grade may suggest, Barber looked like he'll be a long-term starter at the position for Cleveland.
Highlight: Vega Ioane's run game dominance Lowlight: Zion Young's 12 forgettable snaps
The Ravens are the only team on this list that didn't have multiple first-rounders. That didn't stop them from getting a big impact from their rookie class, however. The big reason why is first-rounder Vega Ioane. He was the single best rookie I saw on tape in Week 1. He was dominant in the run game at right guard against the Colts , and while there was a trio of reps he'd want back in pass protection, there were others where he paved the way for Lamar Jackson's scrambles. Considering the state of the Ravens' right guard position a year ago, this draft pick could not have had better early returns.
Vega Ioane was the closest thing I saw to a Pro-Bowler in the rookie class Week 1. A few reps he'd want back in pass pro, but sheer dominance otherwise pic.twitter.com/2cau8PLgNY
The Ravens also got meaningful contributions from third-round receiver Ja'Kobi Lane and fourth-round tight end Matthew Hibner , who played 27 and 23 snaps, respectively. Hibner looked like a very capable TE2, while Lane looked like he'll be a red zone favorite for Lamar Jackson. Lane saw three targets inside the opposing 20-yard line, with one touchdown called back by a penalty.
Highlight: Most rookie starters in the NFL Lowlight: Most rookie starters shouldn't have been starting
No team in the NFL hit reset harder this season than the Miami Dolphins . All told, they had 368 of a possible 1,353 snaps Sunday (27.2%) come from rookies - the most in the NFL. Given that, they have every reason to be elated about what they saw Sunday. Kadyn Proctor was the biggest standout with some truly elite reps in the run game. His power for a 21-year-old is special and translated vs. grown men.
Proctor with a couple pancakes & a knockdown on the 2nd level. Solid debut. Anchor looked pretty strong. Got slipped once across his face against a wide alignment. Another favorable matchup next week against SF's IDL. pic.twitter.com/eF0cvfGBX4
While I think Dolphins' other first-rounder Chris Johnson will be a fine player in time, he had an up-and-down Week 1 with a couple of pass breakups, but a couple of big plays as well. I felt similarly about second-round linebacker Jacob Rodriguez as well. While he struggled to get off the blocks consistently, you saw the play speed flash in space on numerous occasions.
The final rookie worth a mention was third-round receiver Caleb Douglas , who led all rookies with five catches for 94 yards Sunday. In a very underpowered receiving room, Douglas played with a comfort level well beyond that of a rookie.
Dolphins rookie WR Caleb Douglas moved me in week 1. Feed him more targets pic.twitter.com/nm72ms8EJ1
Highlight: Francis Mauigoa's stout pass pro Lowlight: Colton Hood only sees six snaps
Giants fans may see this as a slight, but to me, they check in fifth because I'd expect the only team with two top-10 picks to get an impact out of its rookie class. Arvell Reese was an obvious upgrade for their run defense, while Francis Mauigoa solidified their right guard spot.
There were reps from both, where you saw the high-end talent, but both looked like rookies at times, too.
Wake up with rookie Guard #65 Francis Mauigoa pic.twitter.com/VcNdfBNCCO
The cherry on top of this draft class is third-rounder Malachi Fields , who's already playing a very important role for Matt Nagy's offense. That is doing the dirty work. Fields looks like he'll be a value add in the run game with his ability to dig out box defenders from reduced splits.
Malachi Fields blocking pic.twitter.com/nXtfKRaPFi
author: Mike Renner

title: Predicting the entire NFL playoff bracket after Week 1, including a surprise Super Bowl winner
summary: A wild opening week reshaped our projected playoff bracket, with the Patriots missing out
full_text:
It might sound crazy to try and predict the entire NFL playoff field after just one week of action, but we specialize in crazy.
Week 1 turned the NFL upside down, and you can mostly blame the two teams in Los Angeles for that. The Rams were the Super Bowl favorite going into the season, but right now, it's hard to  envision them even winning their division after they got blasted 27-7 by the 49ers in Australia. And then we have the Chargers . They usually wait until the playoffs to let their fan base down, but this year, they did it in Week 1 with a stunning 26-14 loss to the Cardinals .
As if that's not enough, EVERY team in the NFC South is 0-1, making that possibly the most unpredictable division in the NFL this year. Actually, I take that back; nothing is unpredictable for us here, and that's because we have our resident analytics expert, Stephen Oh, who simulated the rest of the season to see how things will end up playing out. For those of you who are not familiar with Oh's work, let me just say this: If AI was human, it would be Oh.
They say don't overreact to Week 1, but our simulation has run the numbers and reacted accordingly. With that in mind, let's get to the projections.
Before the season started, the Chiefs were kind of a question mark, but that's not the case anymore after their dominant 31-10 win over the Broncos on Monday night. Our projection model is now feeling confident that the AFC West will go through Kansas City this year.
If this projection holds up, that means we'll have two new playoff teams in the AFC with the Bengals and Chiefs getting in. The biggest surprise here might be that the reigning AFC champion Patriots are projected to miss the postseason.
In the NFC, the computer has three teams in the NFC West making the playoffs. Before the season started, our computer surprisingly projected the Seahawks to win the NFC West over the Rams, which looks like a smart pick right now after the way Week 1 played out. Despite their ugly loss in Week 1, the Rams are still projected to make the playoffs, but just barely. Oh, and did I mention that we have a surprise winner coming out of the NFC South? Because we have a surprise winner coming out of the NFC South.
It's almost impossible to predict who will win the NFC South, but the computer likes Atlanta. The Falcons lost to the Steelers 20-13 in Week 1, but it's a game they certainly could have won if they hadn't been forced to start a third-string QB and didn't miss two field goals.
In the NFC North, the Bears' 59-point outburst wasn't enough to put them at the top of the division. The computer still thinks the Lions are in the driver's seat.
Now that we know who's in the playoffs, let's see who's going to make it to Super Bowl LXI.
And now, we're down to our final eight teams.
Things are getting interesting. We're down to four teams, and two of them -- the Bills and Lions -- have never won a Super Bowl.
If our projection is correct, we're going to be getting a battle of the birds in the Super Bowl.
NOTE: The Seahawks have said that Sam Darnold's injury isn't serious, so the computer is assuming that Darnold will be out for a short period of time. If it turns into a longer absence, that could certainly change our projections.
author: John Breech

title: Super Bowl stock report for Week 2: 49ers are healthy and formidable, Chargers dig deeper hole
summary: We assess the NFL title race after Week 1 and identify three upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture
full_text:
You cannot win the Super Bowl in Week 1. But you can't lose it, either. You certainly can put the right or wrong foot forward on the path to the championship. Swamping the preseason favorite in Australia like the San Francisco 49ers did is about the best start possible, while losing to a team in the mix for the No. 1 draft pick a la the Los Angeles Chargers will instill zero confidence in one's ability to compete for the Vince Lombardi Trophy.
Week 1 is ripe for overreactions . Some takeaways will age poorly. What if they carry over into Week 2, though? What if the 49ers continue their hot start and take further command of the NFC West? What if the Chargers drop another game to a perceived bottom-dweller? The conversations about their respective trajectories will only grow stronger.
Each week this season, we will take a snapshot of the Super Bowl race and determine which teams are trending up, which are trending down, and which upcoming games will shake up the title race.
Here is the Super Bowl stock report heading into Week 2.
Odds via DraftKings , +2000 or better
Maybe they are not fully healthy, but even with Alfred Collins on injured reserve, Mykel Williams on the PUP list and De'Zhaun Stribling set to miss at least a month , the 49ers are far closer to full strength now than they were at essentially any point in 2025. The issue with this team has never been talent but rather the ability to keep it on the field. For now, at least, the 49ers have enough tools in their belt.
The 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia was not just a wire-to-wire beatdown. It was also a statement to the entire NFC. The assumption is that the team that emerges as the NFC West champion will represent the entire conference in the Super Bowl. After one week, the 49ers look like the strongest team in football's most loaded division . That is saying a lot, considering the reigning Super Bowl champions and a Rams team that just about everyone thought would cruise to the postseason.
San Francisco's defense allowed just the third-lowest EPA per play of any team in the league in Week 1, and it did so against an offense that boasts the reigning MVP. On the other side of the ball, Mike Evans ' arrival as a new weapon for Brock Purdy , Deebo Samuel's return as a proven playmaker in this offense and Kaelon Black's emergence as a capable running mate for Christian McCaffrey helped the 49ers carve up what is supposed to be one of the league's stingiest defenses.
What was supposed to be the third-best team in its own division has the makings of a squad that could get back to the Super Bowl for the third time under Kyle Shanahan.
When the NFL released the 2026 schedule, it set the Chargers up for an absolute gauntlet. Based on last year's win totals, the Chargers face the ninth-toughest slate of anyone in the league. It was vitally important for them to take advantage of two home games against projected bottom-dwellers before embarking on perhaps the most brutal eight-game stretch the league has to offer.
But they lost to the Arizona Cardinals . By 12 points. At SoFi Stadium. With two turnovers. The Cardinals never trailed in a game they went on to win, 26-14. Maybe Arizona is much better than everyone thought, and perhaps the Chargers are far worse than expected. Both things could be true.
The biggest problem for Jim Harbaugh right now is that every win in the first half of the season matters. With a schedule so grueling, he needs his team to at least tread water until December in order to have a chance at making it out of a competitive AFC West. Losing to a team that might be in the running for the No. 1 overall pick is not the right way to start.
The John Harbaugh effect is already working its magic in New York. In the Giants ' 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys , they displayed a heightened element of toughness on both sides of the ball, showed off a clearly improved Jaxson Dart and uncorked a new weapon in tight end Isaiah Likely , who might be the kind of X-factor that takes this offense to another level.
To be frank, the Cowboys defense might just still be terrible. That should not discount the Giants' performance too much, though. Harbaugh is as proven of a winner as nearly anyone else on the sidelines in this league and has a bevy of young talent at his disposal, and he made excellent use of it in the win -- caliber of opponent aside.
Plus, it was not just the offense that thrived on "Sunday Night Football." The Giants limited the potent Dallas offense to 20 points while containing Javonte Williams to a modest 41 yards and bottling up CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to the tune of a combined 72. It was a multifaceted, victorious effort by the home team in Harbaugh's debut, and one that suggested the Giants might already be closer to the top of the NFC than the bottom.
The most entertaining matchup of Week 2 is the one that opens the slate. The new Highmark Stadium will be rocking in its inaugural regular-season game. That is one of the three contests with the greatest Super Bowl implications this week.
Scoreboard operator, get ready for a busy day. The Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions both had their Week 1 games decided in the 30s, and that will likely be a trend for them all year, with two of the NFL's most talent-laden offenses and defenses that, though it was just one game, seem as shaky as they did a year ago. Both enter this Thursday night battle at 1-0, and once the contest is done, one team will boast two wins over postseason contenders right out of the gate.
The mighty Houston Texans defense could not have drawn two tougher matchups to open the year. It failed its first test in the loss to the Bills and now faces another one with Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase coming to town. There is no reason to believe that the NFL's most powerful defense is all of a sudden anything less than elite, but a second consecutive head-scratcher to open the year would cause at least a little bit of doubt to creep in. On the other side, the reworked Cincinnati Bengals defense has an opportunity against C.J. Stroud to prove that last week's promising effort was no fluke.
There is a lot to be learned about the Jacksonville Jaguars ' upcoming trip to the Mile High City. Are they really as good as they looked against the Cleveland Browns , or was their opponent just as bad as they come? And for the Denver Broncos, are there legitimate concerns, or did their Monday night loss say more about the Kansas City Chiefs being back than anything else? It is a step up in competition for the Jaguars and a spot where the Broncos need to get right. An 0-2 hole for Denver would raise a few early-season alarms as they seek a return to the AFC title game.
author: Carter Bahns

title: From walk-on at North Texas to promising NFL Draft prospect: What early season says about QB Drew Mestemaker
summary: After a 426-yard breakout performance against Oregon, former North Texas transfer Drew Mestemaker is rapidly rising in early 2027 NFL Draft evaluations
full_text:
The college football and NFL Draft communities alike are enamored with a former walk-on quarterback from Austin, Texas. No, this is not a repackaged story on Baker Mayfield, but rather Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker.
CBS Sports' Shehan Jeyarajah wrote an excellent story detailing the Texas native's journey from earning district recognition as both a safety and punter, but never taking a varsity snap at quarterback to now being one of the hottest names at the quarterback position ahead of the 2027 NFL Draft.
Mestemaker's Cowboys have had an unorthodox start to the season; first falling to in-state Tulsa and then knocking off No. 6 Oregon. Each game provided evidence of both the player's strengths and weaknesses. What does the scouting report say about his draft prospects? I solicited the opinion of retired old man soccer star and CBS Sports NFL Draft analyst Ryan Wilson for his thoughts on the quarterback captivating audiences.
"Coming into the season, I was just working from the assumption that Drew Mestemaker would return to school for the 2027 season. Now … maybe not?
"That was my point of reference when I watched him over the summer; he was coming off a huge 2025 season at North Texas, but he had only 13 career starts, hadn't faced a Power 4 opponent and still looked like a quarterback who would probably benefit from another year of development. I had him as my QB9 back in August and while there was plenty to like -- he could work through reads from a clean pocket and consistently showed good touch on intermediate throws -- I also had questions about the arm strength, not always playing on time and occasionally locking onto his first read and forcing the issue.
"Over the summer, I came up with the First-Round Readiness Score (let's call it FRED) to measure a quarterback's current development against the traits and production of past first-rounders. Let's just say the model was considerably more bullish on Mestemaker than my notes . His combination of production, efficiency and early career development gave him one of the strongest scores in the class, behind only Julian Sayin and Jayden Maiava -- and well ahead of Oregon's Dante Moore and Texas' Arch Manning.
"FRED was essentially telling me that I might be underselling how far along he already was," Wilson said.
Speaking to my personal summer process, Mestemaker was a top 50 overall prospect, but clustered in Tier 2 behind Arch Manning, Moore and South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers.
First and foremost, the NFL game is changing. There is less of an emphasis on a quarterback's ability to run the football and more of an emphasis on operating on time and making quick, accurate decisions as a passer from the pocket. Mestemaker has the foot speed to get chunk yardage on the ground, as was seen against Oregon, but is more of a straight-line sprinter than a sudden athlete who will put defenders in compromised positions in space.
His pocket presence was a bit up and down last season but he stood tall in the face of pressure. Mestemaker makes quick decisions and throws with touch, anticipation to allow pass catchers the opportunity to make plays post-catch.
One of the biggest question marks had been how he would handle the transition to Power 4 competition. In two years with the Mean Green, his only exposure to that level of competition had been three pass attempts against Texas Tech in a 66-21 loss.
Fast forward to September when he made his first two starts at Oklahoma State alongside 53 other incoming transfers, including 15 former teammates from North Texas.
"Mestemaker's Oklahoma State debut against Tulsa didn't do much to change my mind. He had some rough moments, struggled to push the ball downfield and looked like a quarterback still adjusting to a new offense. No real surprise and also no reason to panic.
Then Oregon happened," Wilson continued.
"In his first start against a Power 4 team, Mestemaker finished with 426 total yards and outplayed Moore by a wide margin. And some of the things I wanted to see from him showed up in that game. His arm looked stronger than it did last season. He ripped intermediate field-size throws on time, showed great touch and timing on deep balls in the face of pressure and looked a lot like Josh Allen, his favorite player growing up, when he decided to run.
"His footwork from a clean pocket was especially encouraging. He also showed he could play on the move, throwing with pace and accuracy, and Oklahoma State trusted him with the ball on a third-down QB keeper to seal the win.
"There are still reasons to exercise patience. Oregon's defense was, to put it politely, awful. Mestemaker can panic when the first read disappears, and he'll still miss easy throws when his feet aren't set or stare down a target long enough to bring underneath defenders into the play.
So this isn't suddenly a QB1 conversation . But the question has changed, for sure. Before the season, I was wondering whether Mestemaker, who is just 20 years old, would show enough to make himself a legitimate 2028 prospect. Two games in, it's fair to wonder if he might force his way into the 2027 QB conversation."
Through two games, Mestemaker has been pressured on 32.3% of dropbacks, according to TruMedia. On average, he is being pressured once for every three drop backs. There was a discomfort evident against Tulsa. He consistently had pressure in his armpit and was unnecessarily fading away from throws. There were a number of errant throws that were a byproduct of poor footwork and not opening his hips to the throw.
Against Oregon, he displayed better pocket presence as well as the arm strength and decisiveness to rip the ball over the middle of the field. When forced out of the pocket, he struggles to reset his feet.
CBS Sports' Mike Renner has him as the No. 9 overall prospect . Although I am not yet personally as high on the player, there is cautious optimism that he will factor into first-round conversations if he continues on this trajectory.
The Ducks represented arguably the stiffest competition on Oklahoma State's schedule. They have just one more ranked meeting at No. 22 Houston before traveling to Lubbock to play No. 13 Texas Tech Nov. 14.
