title: The Giants showed they can be ‘dangerous’, will the Rams?
summary: Matthew Stafford referred to the New York Giants as a “dangerous” football team, and he further explained that every team in the NFL has a chance to be dangerous. The logic that any team can be dangerous makes sense as every team is made up of the best talent in the world. So, by extension, […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 13: Isaiah Likely #9, Jaxson Dart #6 and Malik Nabers #1 of the New York Giants pose for a photo after the game against the Dallas Cowboys at MetLife Stadium on September 13, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images Matthew Stafford referred to the New York Giant s as a “dangerous” football team, and he further explained that every team in the NFL has a chance to be dangerous. The logic that any team can be dangerous makes sense as every team is made up of the best talent in the world. So, by extension, the Los Angeles Rams can be dangerous too, right? One would think, but it’s hard not to be a little concerned or maybe more than a little concerned given how disappointing they were in Week 1. Now, Myles Garrett is out too. For the Giants, we just saw them be very dangerous over a touted Dallas Cowboys team on Sunday Night Football. The Giants showed they had the goods in Week 1. They’ll look to do it again in Week 2. It’s not all doom and gloom, it’s one week. But the Rams haven’t shown, so far, that they have the goods to be a dangerous team for four quarters in 2026. Will they find that gear on Monday night? Tune in, find out. Matthew Stafford shares early thoughts on ‘dangerous’ Giants (ramswire) “Obviously, the young quarterback, Jaxson Dart, I thought played really well, played within himself, made some plays with his feet,” he added. “They’re a dangerous team. I think every team in the NFL, it’s what people out there forget, year in and year out going through training camps and watching preseason, think they can pick who’s gonna win every game. And that’s why we play them. You put the ball down, you go play the games. And I thought the Giants did a heck of a job the other night. I thought it was cool on the weekend of September 11th, 25 years later, for the Giants in New York City to get a win, felt right and felt great to have the NFL have something like that happen and those guys play well.” View Link NFL power rankings Week 2: There’s a new No. 1 after Rams tumble (usatoday) “ Seattle Seahawks (2): Should’ve known they’d demand and command the respect of a reigning champion that deserves the No. 1 slot until proven otherwise. Did the ‘Hawks look spectacular while winning their Super Bowl rematch with the Patriots, despite losing QB Sam Darnold five plays in to a hip injury? Nope. Did they show their typical grit and dominant defense while again vanquishing a quality opponent? Yep. And plenty of upward mobility, as they’ll tell you. “We’ll improve our operation,” said coach Mike Macdonald after the win. “(W)e can get so much better very quickly.” Good bet they will.” How did former Rams OLB Jared Verse play in his Browns debut? (ramswire) “Similar to Garrett’s first game with the Rams, Verse’s debut with the Browns was disappointing. He finished the game with four tackles, one of which went for a loss, but zero sacks or quarterback hits. According to Pro Football Focus, Verse didn’t record a single pressure and also missed one tackle.” Why Richard Sherman is concerned about Rams’ defense, and it has nothing to do with Myles Garrett injury (clutchpoints) “The corners you got are great corners, but they have played in (Steve Spagnuolo’s) system their whole career, and you don’t run to Spags’ defense…You don’t use a Corvette to Uber. You get in a Corvette, you’re racing…you pay them their money, let him do what he was doing,” he said, per Kevin Clark on X, formerly Twitter. Sherman wasn’t the only one to question how the Rams utilized new cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson in their season opener, as Brock Purdy and the 49ers’ offense seemed to have no issues moving the ball down the field throughout the evening.“ Matthew Stafford downplays Rams’ big injury as ‘little bump in the road’ before four-game gauntlet (nypost) ““This is just a blip in the radar, a little bump in the road,” Stafford said on the “Let’s Go!” podcast, predicting Garrett would work diligently to return quickly. Stafford understands the expectations attached to a blockbuster acquisition, having arrived under similar pressure in 2021. He also emphasized that Garrett is “a human being, too” and said the entire team must compensate for his absence.“ Another baby girl is joining the Rams ‘Ramily’ after star player’s heartwarming Instagram announcement (nypost) “ Terrance Ferguson’s second NFL season may have started quietly, but away from the football field, the Los Angeles Rams tight end just received much bigger news. Ferguson and his wife, Sophia, announced Tuesday that they are expecting their first child, a baby girl, in early 2027. title: Are Rams putting their new corners in the best position to succeed?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams made two of the biggest offseason acquisitions in Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. McDuffie was brought in via a blockbuster trade. Watson was an out of character free agent investment by LA. But why would the Rams acquire two premium corners if they were going to run a defense designed for […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - AUGUST 22: Los Angeles Rams cornerback Trent McDuffie (22) during the NFL preseason game between New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams on August 22, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, CA. (Photo by Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Los Angeles Rams made two of the biggest offseason acquisitions in Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. McDuffie was brought in via a blockbuster trade. Watson was an out of character free agent investment by LA. But why would the Rams acquire two premium corners if they were going to run a defense designed for the players they wanted to replace? That’s exactly what happened in Week 1 in the stunning loss against the San Francisco 49ers. Whether the issue persists is something worth monitoring. Rams vs Chiefs 2025: Coverage Breakdowns Rams zone coverage ranking: 8th at 76.3% Chiefs zone coverage ranking: 24th at 66.3% Rams zone coverage rate vs 49ers: 77.8% Los Angeles ranked in the top 10 in terms of the teams who most often utilized zone coverage according to data from SumerSports. The Chiefs ranked in the bottom 10 of the NFL. These are two distinct approaches to defense, and it was reasonable to expect a shift from LA. Zone coverage can be the great equalizer. You can take heady players who are maybe less physically talented and maximize their production. Zone is more apt for takeaways and allows defenders to keep their eyes on the quarterback. Playing man coverage often requires the horses to do so. Simply put, the Rams did not have them last year. They should now. They shouldn’t continue to play a defense that is designed for the players they were intent on replacing. Counterpoints: Why 49ers were a bad example There are several key reasons why you wouldn’t want to play man coverage against the 49ers: Brock Purdy is athletic enough to gash you Christian McCaffrey is a unique receiving threat The SF offense is designed for YAC Purdy finished with 29 yards on five carries with a long of 18 despite how much zone coverage Los Angeles presented. Asking corners to turn their backs in man coverage proves this was probably a bad matchup. Also, the biggest threat against San Francisco is not that passes are completed—it’s what happens thereafter. The 49ers are built to turn 10-yard catches into explosive gains. Zone coverage is the better method to mitigate this risk than man. But the counterpoints don’t tell the whole story While the 49ers might have been a bad team to deploy a new-look defense against, the single matchup doesn’t completely dismiss the idea that the Rams’ defensive scheme needs to change. McDuffie and Watson are capable of playing sticky man coverage. This would help a talented pass rush, especially after Myles Garrett’s eventual return from injured reserve. The coverage mix is worth keeping an eye on over the coming weeks. We may not get true answers on who the defense wants to be until after they are healthy and back at full force.

title: Sean McVay & Rams W-L record following a 49ers loss
summary: The Los Angeles Rams opened the 2026 season with a disappointing loss to the San Francisco 49ers, leaving Sean McVay and his team with plenty to evaluate heading into Week 2. While the result was not what the Rams wanted, McVay frequently emphasizes one important message following adversity: “controlling their response”. That response will be […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams opened the 2026 season with a disappointing loss to the San Francisco 49ers, leaving Sean McVay and his team with plenty to evaluate heading into Week 2. While the result was not what the Rams wanted, McVay frequently emphasizes one important message following adversity: “ controlling their response ”. That response will be especially important for a Rams team that has high expectations entering the season. McVay and his coaching staff must find ways to correct the mistakes from Week 1 while making sure the loss does not carry over into Monday night’s matchup against the New York Giants. For the players, the challenge is equally simple: learn from the mistakes, move forward and respond with urgency. I was curious to know how Sean McVay was motivated following a loss to his rival, Kyle Shanahan and the San Francisco 49ers. Since both coaches were hired by their respective teams in 2017, here is how McVay has responded after losing to Shanahan. 2017: Week 17 | 34-13 loss vs. 49ers Next Game: 26-13 (playoff) loss to Falcons After choosing to rest their starters in the regular season finale, the Rams could not get their offense moving against Matt Ryan and the Falcons. 2019: Week 6 | 20-7 loss vs. 49ers Next Game: 37-10 win over Falcons The Rams went into Atlanta and dominated. This was the first game that Jalen Ramsey played in horns. 2019: Week 16 | 34-31 loss @ 49ers Next Game: 31-24 win over Cardinals The Rams were knocked out of the playoff race after their Week 16 to the 49ers and there was not much to play for in the regular season finale other than having a winning season. Sean McVay made sure of that. 2020: Week 6 | 24-16 loss @ 49ers Next Game: 24-10 win over Bears The Rams faced Nick Foles and the Bears in primetime. The offense was able to slow down Khalil Mack off the edge in order to get back in the win column. 2020: Week 12 | 23-20 loss vs. 49ers Next Game: 38-28 win over Cardinals Troy Hill had a pick 6 and the Rams scored 21 points in the 4th quarter to clip the birds yet again. 2021: Week 10 | 31-10 loss @ 49ers Next Game: 36-28 loss to Packers After storming out to a 7-1 record, the Rams then lost to the Titans, 49ers, and then Packers. A lot of people thought the Rams were frauds but the 3 game skid led to a 5 game win streak. 2021: Week 18 | 27-24 (OT) loss vs. 49ers Next Game: 34-11 (playoff) win over Cardinals The Rams were pissed for having lost Week 18 to the 49ers. They still secured the NFC West division crown but they became the 4th seed in the NFC. As it turned out they stomped the Cardinals in the Wild Card round. 2022: Week 4 | 24-9 loss @ 49ers Next Game: 22-10 loss to Cowboys Aaron Donald registered two sacks but that was enough to beat Cooper Rush and the Cowboys… 2022: Week 8 | 31-14 loss vs. 49ers Next Game: 16-13 loss to Buccaneers The 2022 was a disaster but none was more unsettling than watching the team hand a game to Tom Brady and the Buccaneers after seemingly having the game secured towards the end of the 4th quarter. 2023: Week 2 | 30-23 loss vs. 49ers Next Game: 19-16 loss to Bengals Apparently Tutu Atwell stepped out bounds… I still will never understand how that call was reversed. 2025: Week 5 | 26-23 (OT) loss vs. 49ers Next Game: 17-3 win over Ravens Puka Nacua was injured midway through the 2nd quarter but the Rams defense held Tyler Huntley and the Ravens offense to just 3 points. After this game, the Rams offense made the switch to using 13 personnel more frequently. In 11 losses to San Francisco, Sean McVay and the Rams are 6-5* in the ensuing games. The 2017 loss to San Francisco was purely out of a decision to rest their starters before the playoffs. At least its more likely than not that the Rams will pick up a win against the New York Giants this week after losing to the 49ers in Week 1 at Melbourne, Australia.

title: Rams Super Bowl chances hinge on 3rd down success
summary: The Los Angeles Rams have played 86 regular-season games from Week 1 of 2021 through Week 1 of 2026. A lot of their success as a offense has been their ability to keep pressure on opposing defenses by moving the chains. Eventually, defenses bust their coverage and the Rams find their way in the end […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams have played 86 regular-season games from Week 1 of 2021 through Week 1 of 2026. A lot of their success as a offense has been their ability to keep pressure on opposing defenses by moving the chains. Eventually, defenses bust their coverage and the Rams find their way in the end zone. Over the last 5 seasons, the Rams season-level third-down rates were: 2021: 44.6% 2022: 39.3% 2023: 41.7% 2024: 36.1% 2025: 37.1% It’s no surprise that the Rams 2021 numbers were so strong as they parlayed that into a Super Bowl championship. The 2022 season saw the team fall drastically because of injuries across the board. The 2023 Rams went from a slow start to strong finish. The 2024 team was remembered for being offensively sluggish. And the 2025 offense, while carried by MVP Matthew Stafford tried to limit its third down frequency by winning on first and second downs. Last year, the Seattle Seahawks were 16th in the league in 3rd down conversion rate with 39.59%. For the sake of this analytical breakdown, I chose 40% as the measurement that the Rams need to be at to find their footing on offense in the 2026 season. 5 YEAR BREAKDOWN… Rams overall record when they convert 40% or more on 3rd down: 30-13 Rams overall record when they convert 39% or less on 3rd down: 19-24 The Rams a significantly different team over the last 5 years when they win 3rd downs at a respectable clip. They are nearly a .700 winning team. On the flip side, when they don’t move the chains as well, they are inconsistent and a sub. 500 team. 2026 Rams when they convert 40% or more on 3rd down: ? 2026 Rams when they convert 39% or less on 3rd down: 0-1 2025 Rams when they convert 40% or more on third down: 7-3 2025 Rams when they convert 39% or less on third down: 5-2 2024 Rams when they convert 40% or more on third down: 6-3 2024 Rams when they convert 39% or less on third down: 4-4 2023 Rams when they convert 40% or more on third down: 5-3 2023 Rams when they convert 39% or less on third down: 5-4 2022 Rams when they convert 40% or more on third down: 3-2 2022 Rams when they convert 39% or less on third down: 2-10 2021 Rams when they convert 40% or more on third down: 9-2 2021 Rams when they convert 39% or less on third down: 3-3 SUPER BOWL SIGNIFICANCE As the Rams move on from their 2026 season opener, a game in which they looked like a sub .500 team because of their sluggish performance on offense, they will need to find consistency winning on “money downs”. In these last 5 NFL seasons, the AFC and NFC representative each year both finished in the top half of the league for third down conversion percentage. 2021 – Los Angeles Rams (44.66 / 6th) , Cincinnati Bengals (40.08% / 15th) 2022 – Philadelphia Eagles (47.58% / 3rd), Kansas City Chiefs (48.90% / 2nd) 2023 – San Francisco 49ers (47.49% / 4th), Kansas City Chiefs (43.32% / 6th) 2024 – Philadelphia Eagles (40.28% / 10th) , Kansas City Chiefs (47.31% / 3rd) 2025 – Seattle Seahawks (39.59% / 16th) , New England Patriots (40.63% / 13th) As it stands right now, albeit a one game sample size, the Rams are 26th in the league (22.22%). If Los Angeles wants to see a Lombardi Trophy return home, they MUST find a way to be successful on third downs week-to-week.

title: Rams Week 2 power rankings round-up: LA drops from top spot
summary: After a very surprising showing in a Week 1 loss to the 49ers, it’s no surprise the Rams have slipped in almost every power ranking. The lone exception was Complex.com’s Matt Burke, who kept at L.A. at the top spot despite the loss and injury to Myles Garrett. Most writers seem to have adopted a […]
full_text: After a very surprising showing in a Week 1 loss to the 49ers , it’s no surprise the Rams have slipped in almost every power ranking. The lone exception was Complex.com’s Matt Burke, who kept at L.A. at the top spot despite the loss and injury to Myles Garrett. Most writers seem to have adopted a wait-and-see attitude before punishing the Rams any further. If they lose to the Giants this week, they will plummet. This sample of eight sites seems to represent the consensus and the average ranking of these eight prognosticators is just over five, which seems about right. Pete Prisco : Dropped from 2 to 5 “So much for the idea they were just going to waltz to the Super Bowl. They have issues on both sides of the ball that were exposed by the 49ers.” Fox Sports Ralph Vacchiano : Dropped from 1 to 5 “The big debate is how far they should plummet because of their opening flop? It could turn out to be a travel-induced anomaly. But if the Rams lose to the Giants on Sunday, you’ll find them in the high teens next week.” NFL.com Nick Shook : Dropped from 1 to 7 “Is it a bit dramatic of me to drop the Rams six spots after a season-opening loss ? You could make that case. But the offseason darlings certainly haven’t done themselves any favors in the last week, appearing unprepared and somewhat fatigued.“ Mike Florio PFT : Dropped from 2 to 11 Mike Florio went the furthest in dropping the Rams, all the way from 2 to 11. Seriously? A bit of an overreaction, perhaps. USA Today Nate Davis : Dropped from 1 to 5 ‘This was likely an anomalous defeat, if a reminder that the Lombardi Trophy is guaranteed to no team.’ SI Conor Orr : Dropped from 1 to 7 “The Rams laid an egg in Australia but the circumstances are such that I’m allowing a pass until we see the team at something closer to optimal.“ Complex Matt Burke : No change, stayed at 1 “The Rams’ team travel director could be on the unemployment line soon as LA’s decision to arrive in Melbourne, Australia just 28 hours before kickoff against the 49ers proved to be costly. New acquisition Myles Garrett is set to miss at least four games as he is undergoing arthroscopic knee surgery. But for now, they are still number one in the rankings.“ NFL Trade Rumors Ethan Woodie : Dropped from 1 to 2 He dropped the Rams one spot due to the Myles Garrett injury. This week’s result against the surprising Giants should move the needle somewhat. The question is which direction.

title: Make your Week 2 NFL picks
summary: Week 1 of the NFL season is in the books and Week 2 is upon us. After a high-scoring opening weekend, there are plenty of questions waiting to be answered. The biggest matchups include the Bills hosting the Lions, the Bengals traveling to Houston to face the Texans, and the Jaguars traveling to Mile High […]
full_text: East Rutherford, NJ December 31, 2023 -- The Giants defense with Jihad Ward and Kayvon Thibodeaux of the Giants sack Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford in the second half. The Los Angeles Rams edged the New York Giants 26-25 on December 31, 2023 at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Week 1 of the NFL season is in the books and Week 2 is upon us. After a high-scoring opening weekend, there are plenty of questions waiting to be answered. The biggest matchups include the Bills hosting the Lions, the Bengals traveling to Houston to face the Texans, and the Jaguars traveling to Mile High to face the Broncos. Monday Night Football features the Los Angeles Rams (0-1) hosting the New York Giants (1-0) at SoFi Stadium. Three of the biggest disappointments from Week 1 were the Los Angeles Rams, Los Angeles Chargers and Green Bay Packers, while the Minnesota Vikings, Arizona Cardinals, and New York Giants emerged as some of the biggest surprises. After going 9-7 with my Week 1 picks , I’m looking to build on that start as we dive into another exciting slate of NFL action. If you want to submit your Week 2 NFL picks: CLICK HERE Week 2 Picks: Detroit Lions @ Buffalo Bills — Thurs., 8:15 p.m. ET Both teams scored 30+ points in Week 1 and the same could happen again in Week 2 as both teams are still trying to find their defenses. My Pick: Bills 37-30 Carolina Panthers @ Atlanta Falcons — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET If the Panthers can bottle up Bijan Robinson, then they should be able to go into Atlanta and secure a Week 2 road win. My Pick: Panthers 29-24 Minnesota Vikings @ Chicago Bears — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET How Brian Flores gameplans for Caleb Williams and Ben Johnson will be interesting. I will take the hot hand though of Ben Johnson. My Pick: Bears 30-21 Philadelphia Eagles @ Tennessee Titans — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET The Eagles snuck out of Week 1 with a win over the hapless Commanders. Jalen Hurts is still a one dimensional quarterback. They get an easy road game in Tennessee. My Pick: Eagles 34-17 Pittsburgh Steelers @ New England Patriots — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET The Patriots have had 10 days off to get ready for the Steelers and should be able to come up with solution with AJ Brown’s absence. My Pick: Patriots 20-17 Green Bay Packers @ New York Jets — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET The Packers blew a pretty important Week 1 divisional game. Week 2 features an east coast contest against Aaron Glenn’s Jets. My Pick: Packers 30-20 Cleveland Browns @ Tampa Bay Buccaneers — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET Baker Mayfield revenge game? Baker Mayfield bounce back game? Mayfield earned a huge payday and then turned in a dud in Week 1; fumbling the ball three times. My Pick: Buccaneers 28-17 New Orleans Saints @ Baltimore Ravens — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET Tyler Shough is showing signs of improvement and growth in year two. But the combination of Lamar Jackson and Derrick Henry is going to be too much for the Saints to handle outside of their dome. My Pick: Ravens 41-20 Cincinnati Bengals @ Houston Texans — Sun., 1:00 p.m. ET The Texans get another elite quarterback early – who came up with their schedule? I have to believe that Demeco Ryans buttons up Burrow who is less mobile/twitchy than Josh Allen. My Pick: Texans 23-17 Jacksonville Jaguars @ Denver Broncos — Sun., 4:05 p.m. ET Trevor Lawrence vs. Bo Nix. Jacksonville will have an extra day to prepare but they will also have to fly across the country. I like Denver at home in afternoon game. My Pick: Broncos 23-16 Las Vegas Raiders @ Los Angeles Chargers — Sun., 4:05 p.m. ET The Chargers were one of the biggest disappointments in Week 1. Justin Herbert only throwing for 209 yards was shocking to say the least. Could Jim Harbaugh’s seat be getting hot? My Pick: Chargers 28-21 Washington Commanders @ Dallas Cowboys — Sun., 4:25 p.m. ET The Commanders battled in Philadelphia but their are some glaring weaknesses. New offensive coordinator, a bad offensive line, and lack of offensive weapons make life for Jayden Daniels difficult. The Cowboys should bounce back in Week 2. My Pick: Cowboys 31-21 Seattle Seahawks @ Arizona Cardinals — Sun., 4:25 p.m. ET The Seahawks will roll with Drew Lock as Sam Darnold recovers from his hip injury. If the Cardinals can shut down Justin Herbert, there is a chance they can pull off an upset. Mike LaFleur could be able to scheme up enough offense. My Pick: Cardinals 16-13 Miami Dolphins @ San Francisco 49ers — Sun., 4:25 p.m. ET Just when you think the 49ers are irrelevant, they find a way to be considered Super Bowl contenders. They have arguably the most NFL experience at key positions: Brock Purdy, Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, Deebo Samuel, Trent Williams, Nick Bosa, and Fred Warner. The 49ers could be a problem all season. My Pick: 49ers 33-10 Indianapolis Colts @ Kansas City Chiefs — Sun., 8:20 p.m. ET Patrick Mahomes. Sunday Night Football. Give me the Chiefs. My Pick: Chiefs 24-20 New York Giants @ Los Angeles Rams — Mon., 8:15 p.m. ET I am very worried about this game for the Rams. The offense was anemic in Week 1. The offense lacks a complimentary piece to Puka Nacua. The defense is now without Myles Garrett for the next four weeks at minimum. The Giants have a new offensive identity under Harbaugh where they can run the ball with the bruising force of Cam Skattebo. Not to mention Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers are issues in the passing game. The Rams need to be ready to play on Monday Night but I am skeptical… My Pick: Giants 27-24

title: Will Aaron Donald suit up for Rams on Monday?
summary: Will Aaron Donald make his 2026 debut on Monday Night Football against the New York Giants? The Rams may need him. With Myles Garrett out, and the entire team looking middle of the pack (at best) against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, the Rams may need Donald to help them get back in […]
full_text: Will Aaron Donald make his 2026 debut on Monday Night Football against the New York Giants? The Rams may need him. With Myles Garrett out, and the entire team looking middle of the pack (at best) against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 1, the Rams may need Donald to help them get back in the win column. It’s not time to panic, but it is time to seriously realize that if the Rams do not start stacking wins now, or at the very least show some improvement in Week 2, this season could get away from them quicker than they had ever considered. It’s Tuesday, time will tell who all will be officially active on Monday night. Could Donald be one of the Rams to come out of the tunnel? Stay tuned. Rams HC Sean McVay noncommittal on Aaron Donald’s Week 2 status (ramswire) “ Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay isn’t tipping his hand on whether Aaron Donald will suit up for Monday Night Football against the New York Giants , saying the Rams simply haven’t made a decision yet. “He’s going to continue to work his process,” McVay said, “and we’ll see what that looks like.” Sean McVay offers positive updates on 3 Rams injuries (ramswire) “McVay called the updates on safety Kam Curl , inside linebacker Nate Landman , inside linebacker Omar Speights and tight end Davis Allen “positive,” suggesting the Rams could get some of their key contributors back sooner rather than later. Curl exited Thursday’s game in the second half with an ankle injury. While he was officially listed as questionable to return, McVay said the veteran safety “is good,” downplaying the injury as ankle soreness. Curl has quickly become one of the most important pieces of the Rams defense, starting all 17 games last season while playing 99% of the defensive snaps. He signed a $36 million contract extension this offseason. Jaylen McCollough replaced Curl after going down, who had two tackles before exiting.“ 4 things Rams learned from Sunday’s games: Are LaFleur’s Cardinals…good? (ramswire) “As always in the opening weekend of the season, there were plenty of surprises and new developments across the league. Here are four things the Rams learned about their foes in the NFC, including a couple of impressive upcoming opponents in the Cardinals and Giants. Cardinals won’t be the easy out many people expected them to be The Cardinals’ projected win total was set at 3.5 before the season started. After just one game, they’re already a quarter of the way toward eclipsing that number set by oddsmakers. They beat the Chargers convincingly on Sunday, 26-14, in Mike LaFleur’s head coaching debut. And they were on the road in L.A., too.“ Did Browns Know More Than Rams Ahead of Myles Garrett Trade? Why Deal Timing Was Perfect (heavy.com) “Garrett earned his second Defensive Player of the Year award in 2025 after tallying 23 sacks and breaking the NFL’s single-season mark in that category. He wanted a raise heading into his age-31 campaign and didn’t make sense for Cleveland’s timeline, given the Browns don’t appear likely to have a true franchise QB before 2027, which probably means it will be at least 2028 before the team can seriously contend. The Browns executed a deal with the Los Angeles Rams , after which Garrett missed considerable time during the spring and summer with knee issues that included swelling. Now, after one wildly underwhelming performance in a blowout loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia, Garrett is going to miss at least four weeks due to surgery.“ Reeling Rams defense can’t afford to underestimate Jaxson Dart and the Giants (ramblinfan) “While 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy picked apart the Rams, the Giants’ Jaxson Dart dominated the Cowboys secondary in similar fashion, completing 23-of-29 passes for 230 yards and three touchdowns. He was cooly efficient en route to averaging an impressive 0.73 EPA per play, wasting little energy in leading his offense to a touchdown in every quarter. And now the LA defense, which is already reeling , must step up and stop him in Week 2. Rams defense won’t be overconfident vs Giants in Week 2 Whatever exposed the Rams so badly, those factors have been scrubbed for Week 2. They are no longer anointed as default winners. The roster is no longer seen as bursting with insurmountable superstars, many of whom either struggled in the season opener , are injured entering Week 2 (i.e., Myles Garrett),or both.“ Texas A&M Legend Myles Garrett’s Injury Situation Takes New Turn (sports.yahoo) “ Myles Garrett ‘s highly anticipated debut with the Los Angeles Rams did not go according to plan, and now the former Texas A&M star is facing a significant absence after undergoing knee surgery. Garrett was dealing with the knee issue throughout the summer, limiting his participation during training camp and the preseason. However, the Rams believed the veteran defensive end would be able to manage the injury and contribute once the regular season arrived.“ Rams tumble in Week 2 power rankings: Is LA a top-5 team? (ramswire) “ 5. Los Angeles Rams (1): Woof. At least you couldn’t blame the special teams for this loss? But the Rams scored their fewest points of the Matthew Stafford era, while WR Puka Nacua had more tackles (1) than ballyhooed offseason acquisition Myles Garrett, who will be out at least the next month – apparently he should’ve stayed in L.A. with Aaron Donald. This was likely an anomalous defeat, if a reminder that the Lombardi Trophy is guaranteed to no team.“ Rams undecided if Donald will play vs. Giants (nbcsports) “Donald was kept off the Week 1 roster for last week’s opener against the 49ers, and the Rams did receive a two-game roster exemption for Donald after he agreed to return. Speaking on Monday, McVay said Donald will “continue to work his process” and that the team will see how things look from there. With the Rams losing Myles Garrett (knee) for at least the next four games, it’s safe to assume they would like to get Donald on the field sooner rather than later. – Zachary Krueger ” Broncos-Chiefs on ‘Monday Night Football’: What We Learned from Kansas City’s 31-10 win (nfl.com) “ Davis’ Denver offense stymied. As Patrick Mahomes made his much-ballyhooed return after tearing his ACL and LCL last season, his former Texas Tech teammate Davis Webb was making his debut as the Broncos play-caller and offensive coordinator. Monday went much better for Mahomes. Webb and Broncos QB Bo Nix , in his first game since breaking his ankle in the Divisional Round, never found any consistent success. Kenneth Walker’s 191 total yards for the Chiefs bested the Broncos’ 176. Nix looked sharper earlier passing than Mahomes, but it made no matter as the game wore on with Denver shockingly held to nine first downs and its ground game non-existent. J.K. Dobbins was the leading ground gainer with a meager 36 yards, while Nix’s 19-yard TD toss to Evan Engram to tie the game in the first quarter was really the last splash of any kind had by Webb’s offense. After the Chiefs vaulted ahead, 21-7, on a stellar 60-yard gallop by Walker in the third quarter, Mahomes was picked off by Brandon Jones on the Chiefs’ ensuing drive. Set up at the KC 5-yard line, Nix and the offense went backward and settled for a 31-yard field goal by Wil Lutz — Denver’s last points of the game. With such high expectations and such a disastrous debut for Webb and the offense, one has to wonder how long head coach Sean Payton will wait until snatching the offensive reins back.“ NFL ties Week 1 scoring record for Super Bowl era (nfl.com) “Thanks to the Kansas City Chiefs and Denver Broncos combining for 41 points on Monday night, the opening slate of games for the 2026 season has officially tied the 2012 season’s record for the most Week 1 points scored (791) during the Super Bowl era. Entering Monday’s AFC West showdown, teams had averaged 50.0 combined points per game, per NFL Research, with the Week 1 finale bringing the average down to 49.4.“ Comment of the Day: “McVay, I like you as a coach,…

title: Ashton Jeanty starts 2nd season in a big way
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1 and what to look for Sunday at the Los Angeles Chargers: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 73 percent of the snaps in Week 1. He averaged […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2025 draft class fared in a 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1 and what to look for Sunday at the Los Angeles Chargers: Ashton Jeanty: The No. 6 overall draft pick played 73 percent of the snaps in Week 1. He averaged 77 percent play time as a rookie. He made a big impact. He had 29 touches on 68 offensive plays and accounted for 147 of the Raiders’ 290 scrimmage yards. He is a focal point of the offense. Jack Bech: The second-round pick logged the third most snap totals of the Raiders’ receivers. He played 39 percent of the snaps in Week 1. He played more than seven times last season. Bech had three cathces for 23 yards and a touchdown against Miami. Like all of the Raiders’ receivers, Bech needs to find a way to produce more. Darien Porter: After beating rookies Jermod McCoy and Zeke Masses for the starting job, the third-round pick played every snap in Week 1 until he left with an injured foot. Caleb Rogers: The third-round pick didn’t play on offense after losing a camp battle to Jackson Powers-Johnson at right guard. Rogers did play six plays on special teams. Charles Grant: The offensive lineman, taken in the third round, also only played six snaps on special teams. Dont’e Thornton: The wide receiver, taken in the fourth round, will be on the injured reserve for, at least, three more weeks. Tonka Hemingway: The fourth-round pick played 57 percent of the defensive snaps, the most of any defensive tackle and he played 12 snaps on special teams. He had four tackles (three assisted) against the Dolphins. JJ Pegues: The defensive tackle, taken in the sixth round, was inactive in Week 1, a healthy scratch. He was active in nine of 17 games as a rookie. Cody Lindenberg: The seventh-round pick was also a healthy scratch in Week 1. It was a bit of a surprise. He was active every games and was a core special teamer as a rookie.

title: Las Vegas Raiders slide in some NFL Power Rankings despite win against Miami Dolphins
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders took care of business in Week 1, beating the Miami Dolphins 27-13. However, this was one of the few games the Raiders were expected to win heading into the season, so it’s no surprise that they didn’t climb up most NFL Power Rankings in the Week 2 roundup. That being said, […]
full_text: (Photo by Candice Ward/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders took care of business in Week 1 , beating the Miami Dolphins 27-13 . However, this was one of the few games the Raiders were expected to win heading into the season, so it’s no surprise that they didn’t climb up most NFL Power Rankings in the Week 2 roundup. That being said, a couple of outlets had Las Vegas falling despite the two-possession victory. Sports Illustrated 28. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 27 The Raiders beat the worst team in the NFL in the season opener. The good? We saw a revival from talent that was drafted highly in the 2025 draft and was all but abandoned by the previous regime. The bad news? They are getting a hella pissed off Chargers team coming off the most embarrassing loss of the inaugural weekend. — Conor Orr I’m having a hard time wrapping my head around how the Raiders fell in Orr’s rankings when the only explanation is centered around a game that hasn’t happened yet. Don’t get me wrong, beating the Dolphins isn’t a significant accomplishment. However, how are you saying that the talent the team drafted last year is finally starting to show through while suggesting the coaching staff has improved, and still have the team drop in the rankings? Las Vegas should at least stay the same, in my opinion. For reference, Orr had the Chargers dropping from 10 to 17 after losing to the Cardinals, who leapfrogged the Raiders (30 to 26). Arizona’s ascension is likely the reason for Vegas’ drop, but that’s not clear or stated in the analysis. ESPN 28. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 27 Non-QB newcomer debut: Edge Kwity Paye The Raiders have been searching for a secondary pass rusher to support All-Pro Maxx Crosby. Paye, who signed a three-year deal in free agency, showed Sunday that he could fill that role with two sacks, five pressures and five quarterback hits. Under first-time defensive coordinator Rob Leonard, the Raiders want to be aggressive and make life uncomfortable for opposing quarterbacks. If Paye continues to have performances similar to the one he had in Week 1, the outlook for Las Vegas could be a lot different this season. — Ryan McFadden Another drop for the Raiders! Apparently, the worst thing to happen to the Silver and Black in Week 1 was the Cardinals pulling off the biggest upset of the weekend! I do appreciate McFadden’s analysis, though. Paye did a pretty good job in the complementary role next to Crosby . The free-agent signing didn’t have many quick wins as a pass-rusher, but he did clean up a lot of plays, which is something the Raiders’ defense was missing last year. If that trend continues, I’m going to be pushing for Paye’s nickname to be ‘The Custodian’. NFL.com 29. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 29 The Raiders received the most favorable draw for Klint Kubiak’s head-coaching debut and handled business, overcoming two turnovers to build a two-score lead that was threatened but ultimately held through the final whistle. Most encouraging: Ashton Jeanty finally delivered a game that matched the expectations he brought with him from Boise State. — Nick Shook It’s funny, Shook has the Raiders ranked lower than anyone else here, but I can at least wrap my head around it since he didn’t have them falling. Granted, it’s not like he could have Vegas much lower. But at least he’s consistent, and fair is far. The Raiders didn’t exactly face the 1972 Dolphins on Sunday. And on the note about Jeanty, it’s amazing what can happen when he has a competent offensive line in front of him. Shoutout to Rick Dennison. The Athletic 27. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 27 What we learned: This season may be different Trepidation is warranted after the Raiders won their opener last season, too, before finishing 3-14. But as our Sam Warren wrote, there are legitimate reasons to think this season could be different under Klint Kubiak. They pulled off the win without tight end Brock Bowers, who could return from injury for Week 2. — Chad Graff, Josh Kendall Warren’s article referenced above dives into how starting 1-0 this year feels different than last season, which ended up being a 3-14 campaign. The improved offensive line was a big reason for that, on top of the improved defense. For the latter, one of the biggest differences I noticed was that the Raiders were constantly pursuing the football, with several defenders around the ball carrier. Las Vegas still had some tackling issues, with Pro Football Focus having them on the hook for 10 misses as a team. However, that wasn’t nearly as impactful with defenders in position to clean up plays and have their teammates’ backs. To me, little things like that are a sign of a culture change, which bodes well for Kubiak and Rob Leonard as leaders. Bleacher Report 24. Las Vegas Raiders Last Week: 26 Fans shouldn’t overreact to a two-touchdown win over a Miami Dolphins team that has one of the NFL’s most underwhelming rosters, especially at home. However, the Las Vegas Raiders looked more like a cohesive team than they did at almost any point last season. It’s too early to declare Klink Kubiak as Las Vegas’ answer at head coach. However, his team was well-prepared for Week 1 and operated like a team that can probably pull off a few upsets in 2026. However, Kirk Cousins (2 INTs) will need to be more careful with the football to keep Las Vegas in the win column and to quiet calls for rookie Fernando Mendoza. — Kristopher Knox Knox kind of picked up where I left off in the section above, noting how the Raiders were more cohesive than last year’s team. That doesn’t say much, seeing as they were so bad in 2025, but it is a step in the right direction and worth celebrating. Also, Knox is on the mark with his analysis of Cousins. Three touchdowns are great, but 5.3 yards per attempt and more interceptions (two) than completions (one) when throwing 10 or more yards past the line of scrimmage isn’t a sustainable winning formula. The 38-year-0ld’s age and injury history are showing when he tries/has to push the ball down the field. He can get the benefit of the doubt without having Bowers out wide, but Cousins’ arm is something to monitor moving forward. Kirk Cousins' passing chart from @NextGenStats Passes 10+ down the field: 1/7, 21 yards, 2 INTs #Raiders pic.twitter.com/ScJOVPMCFl — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 14, 2026

title: Kwity Paye makes loud statement in Las Vegas Raiders debut against Miami Dolphins
summary: The Las Vegas Raiders’ defense was pretty dominant in the 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins. The Raiders’ pass rush was especially impressive, sacking Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis five times and recording 27 pressures as a team, per Pro Football Focus. Maxx Crosby, Las Vegas’s well-known rusher, was his typical self with 1.5 […]
full_text: (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Las Vegas Raiders’ defense was pretty dominant in the 27-13 Week 1 win over the Miami Dolphins . The Raiders’ pass rush was especially impressive, sacking Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis five times and recording 27 pressures as a team, per Pro Football Focus . Maxx Crosby, Las Vegas’s well-known rusher, was his typical self with 1.5 sacks and tying for the defense’s most pressures with eight. However, he wasn’t alone, as Kwity Paye was also impressive. The free-agent signing made his Raiders debut on Sunday and managed to tie for the team lead with six total tackles . Additionally, he led the Silver and Black with two sacks and four quarterback hits while matching Crosby with eight pressures, which is tied for the third-most across the NFL at the position (pre- Monday Night Football ). Here’s the kicker: Paye only had 24 pass-rush snaps, meaning he got pressure on a third of his opportunities. The former Indianapolis Colt didn’t get many opportunities to rack up a large volume of stats against the run with Vegas holding a lead for the majority of the contest. However, he was an efficient run defender, notching a pair of defensive stops on just six snaps against the run, per PFF . With all of this in mind, let’s flip on the tape and breakdown the performance. Well-timed blitz by Rob Leonard -Sends the boundary CB off the edge to influence the handoff vs. triple option -RB runs right into Kwity Paye as the unblocked defender for a TFL -Taron Johnson also gets in the backfield on the nickel blitz #Raiders pic.twitter.com/NpOqb8KxCc — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 14, 2026 One reason that Paye was so productive against the Dolphins is that defensive coordinator Rob Leonard called an excellent game. The Dolphins come out in 11 personnel but motion into a 21 personnel formation by motioning the tight end on the line of scrimmage and a wide receiver into the backfield as the H-back in the offset I-formation from the pistol. Miami’s goal is to keep the defense in nickel personnel by leaving three receivers on the field and shifting into a look that they can run a triple option out of. However, Las Vegas has the perfect counter. Whether it was called in the huddle or something the Raiders checked to pre-snap, Leonard has a well-timed blitz to defend the option. The boundary cornerback (Darien Porter) comes off the edge, which influences the quarterback to hand the ball off to the running back and immediately takes away two of the offense’s “options”: the quarterback and pitch man/wide receiver in the backfield. Meanwhile, Paye is supposed to be the defender the quarterback is reading, meaning he’s unblocked. He does a great job of recognizing the play design to avoid getting too far upfield and stays close to the line of scrimmage, squeezing inside on the heel line of the offensive line. That puts him in a perfect position to meet the running back in the backfield for a TFL, with some assistance from nickelback Taron Johnson, who blitzes off the other edge and beats the slot receiver’s block to get penetration. So, this is a scheme-assisted tackle for Paye with a great play call from Leonard. But the edge defender executes his assignment well to be in a perfect spot to make the play. Kwity Paye at 5-tech Nice job getting skinny to split the combo block and escape the G to get a clean-up tackle for a 1-yard gain #Raiders pic.twitter.com/s4zBPe803l — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 14, 2026 One way that Paye filled up the stat sheet on Sunday was by making several “clean-up” tackles, like the one above. Something he brings to the defensive line is alignment versatility. The Raiders match this two-tight end or double-wing-esque look (before the motion) from the Dolphins by putting Johnson in the box and getting into an odd front with off-ball linebacker Quay Walker on the edge. As a result, Paye slides inside a bit to play as a 5-technique defensive end rather than a standup outside linebacker or wide defensive end. That also means he’s going to take on a combo block from the left tackle and guard against Miami’s outside zone toss call. In other words, he’s being asked to execute an assignment that edge defenders don’t see much because they’re the end man on the line of scrimmage and won’t have to take on many combo blocks, at least not with two offensive linemen. So, Paye does give up some ground after initial contact. However, he does a good job of attacking the man he’s lined up across from (the left tackle) and then turning his shoulders when he starts to feel pressure from the guard to get skinny and split the offensive linemen. When the tackle works up to the second level, that’s where the versatile defensive lineman comes in, escaping from the guard and making the play for a one-yard gain after Jeremy Chinn misses. #Raiders used Kwity Paye as an interior pass rusher on a lot of 3rd downs vs. MIA Here's one of his best pass rushes, selling the vertical rush and using his quickness to win across the G's face #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/cLVToQFo2B — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 14, 2026 Along similar lines, the Raiders used Paye as an interior pass-rusher on a lot of third downs or obvious passing situations. That’s a good way to get him, Maxx Crosby and Malcolm Koonce on the field at the same time, like the play above. Additionally, it helps take advantage of Paye’s lateral movement skills and quickness by giving him matchups against guards. He lines up as a 5-technique again and pushes upfield with his first couple of steps to help sell the vertical rush. That combination gets the left guard to widen, and with the center working in the opposite direction/to Crosby’s side, there’s a big pass-rush lane in the weak-side A-gap. That’s where the five-year veteran’s quickness and lateral movement skills come into play, as he beats the guard across the guard’s face to get pressure. The one tweak that Paye can do here is finishing his pass-rush move with a chop or an arm over rather than a rip. The former would allow him to knock the guard’s inside hand/arm down and get a clean win to have a better chance at finishing with a sack. But regardless, he flushes the quarterback out of the pocket and forces the quarterback to scramble on third and long, leading to a punt. Simulated pressure from Rob Leonard leads to Kwity Paye rushing on the edge, where Paye gets push to collapse the pocket and help set up a Maxx Crosby sack #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/RqWQBPBGGu — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 14, 2026 This time, Leonard dials up a simulated pressure out of a double A-gap look, where Koonce and Walker drop into coverage while Paye, Nakobe Dean, Jonah Laulu and Crosby make up the four-man rush. Paye and Koonce are in the same alignments as the previous play; the latter is just in a two-point stance instead of having his hand in the ground this time. So, it’s a similar look for the offensive line. However, when Koonce drops into coverage, Paye works wide to end up rushing on the edge despite starting the rep as a 5-technique. That keeps the offensive line on their toes and gives them something to think about when those two defenders line up next to each other moving forward. Post-snap, Paye gets outside so that he can keep Willis (a running quarterback) in the pocket and rushes with power to be in a position to escape if the quarterback steps up or tries to scramble around the edge. It takes a second since he has to transition from inside to outside and then from upfield to into the quarterback, but Paye gets a nice surge to push through the right tackle’s inside shoulder and collapse the pocket. Then, when Willis tries to step up, he’s in position to slow Willis down and give Crosby enough time to finish with a sack. Here's the play: -3 DL away from Crosby influences C to open left -Dean on LOS keeps RG inside for Crosby 1-on-1 -Walker on a creaper blitz while Dean drops -Nose slants to…

title: Treydan Stukes makes presence felt in Week 1
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1 and what to look for Sunday at the Los Angeles Chargers: Fernando Mendoza:The No. 1 overall pick served as Kirk […]
full_text: (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 27-13 win over the Miami Dolphins in Week 1 and what to look for Sunday at the Los Angeles Chargers: Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick served as Kirk Cousins backup. he did not play. He was seen taking many notes on the sideline. Treydan Stukes: The Raiders’ second-round pick played all 56 defensive snaps at safety and he played 46 percent of the snaps on special teams. He delivered after earning the starting job over veteran Isaiah Pola-Mao in training camp after a slow start. He had six tackles and he had an interception. What a nice start to his career. Trey Zuhn: The third-round pick didn’t play on offensive, but the versatile offensive lineman did play on six special-teams plays. Jermod McCoy: The fourth-round pick was active, but did not play on defense or on special teams. The Raiders are easing him back from a 2024 knee injury. Mike Washington: The fourth-round pick had 41 rushing yards on seven carries, including a 18-yard run. He played on 13 offensive plays. Expect that number to grow depending on the game plan. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was a healthy scratch. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick came in late in the fourth quarter when starter Darien Porter left the game with a foot injury. He played the 10 final snaps of the game. He was tested on his first NFL play and broke up a pass. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick played seven offensive snaps and two on special teams. He had one catch for eight yards on two targets and he had had minus-8 yards on one carry. He did have a 23-yard punt return he nearly broke for a touchdown. I could see his role growing soon.

title: Strategerie (maybe not a real word)
summary: I am so excited to be a small part of the Fins’ universe. I love reading the Phinsider columns with our great writers and the great comments from our readers(you all are strong!). Keep ‘em coming. Before I start the column proper, I am watching the Chiefs-Broncos butt-whipping, I mean game, and I just saw […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Head Coach Jeff Hafley of the Miami Dolphins stands on the field after an NFL football game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images I am so excited to be a small part of the Fins’ universe. I love reading the Phinsider columns with our great writers and the great comments from our readers(you all are strong!). Keep ‘em coming. Before I start the column proper, I am watching the Chiefs-Broncos butt-whipping, I mean game, and I just saw Jaylen Waddle drop a perfectly thrown pass from Bo Nix. It had a bit of Grey Poupon on it but it should have been caught. I think we will make out good on that trade. I just read Chris-Early’s column. Wow! That “Wow!” wasn’t just an ordinary “Wow”, it was a “Wow!” with a factorial “!” behind it. In mathematics, a Wow! (factorial) is far superior to an ordinary “Wow.” I get fired up when people put out strong opinions! The Chiefs are pulling out a page from Dennis Erickson’s UM versatile offensive playbook. I went to Auburn, FAU and UCLA but I do root for the Canes. Back in 1992, FSU came into the Orange Bowl to take on the high-flying high-octane passing attack Hurricanes. FSU expected UM to throw the ball a million times but Dennis Erickson saw some weaknesses in FSU’s run defense and ran the ball for 222 yards and ultimately won on the “Wide Right” kick. This change of pace is something that the Dolphins should aspire to but we are not there yet. Does Hafley and company have the “strategerie” to try things like this down the road? I say that because I didn’t see much “strategerie” on Sunday. Say what you want but Coach Hafley seemed like he threw the Dolphins into an underwater maze and left them to their own devices. I didn’t see any obvious coaching changes e.g. all out blitzes, max protect, reverses, counters, sixth offense lineman etc etc etc. I am not gonna harp on that because I saw Andy Reid let Mahomes get killed in two Super Bowls because the Chiefs didn’t have the foresight to have serviceable tackles. I thought Andy Reid would have ran double-tight end or use a sixth blocker (even Mike McDaniel figured that out). Something. Anything to change the momentum of those two Super Bowls. I watched Coach Shula and Tom Olivadotti not figure out to switch defensive fronts and let Tim Tyndale rush for 498 yards (almost) in Shula’s last game ever. Thank God the moronic Bills lost the next week to Pittsburgh! So Hafley was content to not make any noticeable changes or if he did, nothing happened. Mike McDaniel could have done that too. Where is Hafley’s mark as a coach? The fans need to see something positive, something to build on. Even in Shula’s down years, he would pull out one unexpected victory. Repeating myself a bit; I didn’t see anything special from the coaching staff. Speaking of special, there was very little in the special teams. Pathetic is a better word. Is this the coaching upgrade that we were promised? What possible excuse do you use for not being able to stop long kickoff returns? Twice? The camera showed some bewildered coach, acting bewildered. Twice. The bad second coverage was virtually an instant replay of the first bad coverage. I am unsure if he is the special teams’ coach but I already had Keith Armstrong flashbacks. How do we not get special teams right? Special teams (outside of finding a reliable kicker and punter) should be the EASIEST thing to fix. This is how John Harbaugh made his bones. This special team issue is a symptom of something wrong. Maybe I will have to eat some crow? Glad to do it. I am an experienced crow eater!

title: Dolphins Week 1 review: Thoughts and reactions from Raiders loss
summary: For the first time in 16 years, I do not have NFL Sunday Ticket.  The good news is that NFL+ has a condensed version of the game, so I can skip a lot of the talk and in-between play stuff that the normal podcast.  I can watch kickoff to final whistle in about 45 minutes.  […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Malik Willis #2 of the Miami Dolphins leads teammates onto the field before the NFL game against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The Raiders defeated the Dolphins 27-13. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the first time in 16 years, I do not have NFL Sunday Ticket. The good news is that NFL+ has a condensed version of the game, so I can skip a lot of the talk and in-between play stuff that the normal podcast. I can watch kickoff to final whistle in about 45 minutes. The bad news is that I can’t watch live via that source. I say all of this to preface the fact I watched the game LATE Sunday night, and that process will not likely change this season. With weekends being what they are for me, all my immediate takes will be from the perspective of watching the game late and trying to remember everything I saw. So if things seem off, perhaps that’s why. Perhaps . Anyway, here we go. Youth and experience was front and center This has been THE major talking point all offseason and we all knew coming into this season that rookies were going to play a major factor. This Miami Dolphins team is loaded with players who have not played many NFL snaps on both sides of the ball. Profootballreference.com has the snap counts and starters from the game on their site. On offense, Miami started 3 rookies: Caleb Douglas, Will Kacmarek, and Kadyn Proctor. On defense, Miami started 3 rookies: Jacob Rodriguez, Chris Johnson, and Michael Taaffe. The Douglas, Kacmarek, and Proctor played 51, 14, and 56 snaps respectively, with 56 being all the offensive snaps. Rodriguez, Johnson, and Taaffe played 68, 68, and 51 snaps respectively, with 68 being all the defensive snaps. Other rookies like Chris Bell, Kevin Coleman Jr., and DJ Herman saw significant snaps. But it wasn’t just the rookies. There were several starters who have limited playing time at the pro level. Starting safety Zayne Anderson played 53 snaps yesterday, which represents over 25% of his career total. Malik Willis, whom I highlighted as an “experienced rookie” played 56 snaps, which represents about 10% of his career total. Jordan Phillips, Jason Marshall Jr., Dante Trader Jr., and Zeek Biggers are all second-year players who played significant snaps against Las Vegas that all have less than 500 NFL snaps in their careers. That’s a long-winded way of saying the Dolphins are about as wet behind the ears as they can be across the board. That is going to lead to sloppy play from everyone. There are going to be missed assignments. There is going to be miscommunication. I saw more than one occasion where the offensive line looked more confused than the defense. There is going to be a lot of splintery wood to sand down before this looks like what we want it to be. That doesn’t make it any easier to watch, but it does add some perspective when you realize that of 22 starters, only 8 had more than 1000 career snaps entering this contest. Coaching is a concern I read something somewhere that this game was only like the 6th time in NFL history that 2 rookie head coaches faced off against one another. Maybe that’s true; maybe it’s not. What I can say is that one set of coaches looked like they knew what they were doing and the other did not. The Raiders are not a good team and they know that. They have limited weapons and an older QB that is only there as a bridge for their rookie. That coaching staff knew that and did what any good coaching staff would do: protect their QB and let their one top playmaker carry the load. And by protect their QB, I mean get the ball out of his hands and don’t let him do stupid stuff. One might look at Cousins’s stat line and see 21-30 and 3 TDs. But he only threw for 160 yards on those 30 attempts. A high completion percentage and low YPA means what class? That’s right… Captain Kirk was Captain Checkdown. I don’t blame them one bit. They were smart to lean on the running game. They were smart to target a rookie cornerback – and Cousins is savvy enough to do that. When Cousins did look downfield, it was usually bad. He had a few completions. He also completed a few to the Dolphins. Cousins wasn’t particularly good this game despite his stat line looking somewhat nice. That team just played smarter and looked better coached. To counter that, the Dolphins didn’t sell out to stop the run. Or maybe they did. I don’t remember. It was late. But I would have had 8 in the box at all times and forced Cousins and limited pass catchers to beat me. Only one WR on the Raiders had a YPC average over 10 and that was because he caught the one decent downfield throw from Cousins. But no… the Raiders ran over the Dolphins and ran over them some more. It was a disappointing showing from a defensive calling standpoint. Now, I will give Hafley a slight break… typically offensive head coaches have an advantage over defensive head coaches starting out. But Hafley will need to improve. If he is going to sink or swim with rookies and green players, he might as well go all out with them. On the flip side (hat tip to WZB), Miami’s offense was like that annoying card player at the poker table that goes all-in every hand. Everything was a run or deep pass. I saw a screen pass or two, but that was it. No checkdowns, no easy passes, no “drive starters.” I recall the Raiders having several plays where Cousins threw a quick out for a 4-5 yard gain at most. Where was that for Miami? That’s how you protect your quarterback. That’s how you stay on schedule and maintain proper down and distance. I get the game script got out of hand late, but the play calling was very suspect (also hat tip to JUK – I was preparing this before I read his post, so make sure you read it ). This and that Caleb Douglas may be for real. I’m going to be a little hesitant because the Raiders don’t exactly have a shutdown secondary. But a “reach” in his debut game going 5-94 on 7 targets is nothing to write off. He should only improve. Sully may have struck gold here. Kadyn Procter looked ok out there. Perhaps an All-22 review is in order. I saw a player who missed several assignments, which is a communication issue. That’s not necessarily a rookie mistake, but the 1st team OL has been the same from day one. That’s something that should be mitigated by now. I also saw Achane get dropped for a loss because Proctor got obliterated. A 360 lbs. OL should NOT get pushed THAT far back on a run play. That is simply unacceptable. But he also had some good run blocks and held up decent in pass pro. OL reviews really require All-22 film and the condensed replay doesn’t rewind the easiest (on the TV anyway), but from what I could see, he had good and bad moments. Malik Washington can be a reliable target for Willis, but if he is used the right way. McDaniel had him running sweeps and behind the LOS kinda stuff and that’s good. But Slowik has a 6’4” and 6’2” receiver at his disposal and he’s running deep sideline routes to a 5’8” WR? Come on now. This comes back to the play-calling. Putting Washington in position to catch the underneath stuff and use RAC skills will best fit what he can do AND give Willis the needed “easy pass” option. Malik Willis was… ok. I don’t think he played poorly overall, but there were some issues that need to be addressed. Aside from the playcalling aspect, he took some bad sacks. Before fans jump on the “oh noes, the OL sucks again”, this is very likely ALWAYS going to be a part of Willis’ game. He is going to hold the ball longer than we have seen under the previous regime. Yes, some of it was poor blocking. Let’s give the Raiders some credit. They have one of the game’s best pass rushers in Crosby and edge rushers Kwity Paye and Malcolm Koonce are solid players. But Willis is going to take sacks that his predecessor never would because of how he plays. Play-calling can also help with the sack numbers. Getting the ball…

summary: Don’t you dare think I can’t see you rolling your eyes at your screen right now… Yes, despite the fact that the Miami Dolphins lost to the Las Vegas Raiders by a score of 27-13 on Sunday, marking a disappointing debut for new head coach Jeff Hafley, we will be naming a Most Valuable ‘Phin […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - SEPTEMBER 13: Caleb Douglas #7 of the Miami Dolphins runs after a catch against Jeremy Chinn #11 of the Las Vegas Raiders in the second quarter of a game at Allegiant Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Don’t you dare think I can’t see you rolling your eyes at your screen right now… Yes, despite the fact that the Miami Dolphins lost to the Las Vegas Raiders by a score of 27-13 on Sunday, marking a disappointing debut for new head coach Jeff Hafley, we will be naming a Most Valuable ‘Phin for that contest. And yes, despite the fact that the 2026 season has the potential to be one of the most frustrating years of Dolphins football in recent memory, we will be picking an MVP each and every week this season. If that bothers you, don’t click. It’s really that simple. However, for those who are viewing the 2026 season through the right lens, we will be finding silver linings and highlighting players who are impressing despite the organization’s current struggles in an effort to put some attention on the positives this year — however few of those may exist. Miami Dolphins Week One MVP – WR Caleb Douglas In his professional debut, Douglas had an historic performance — nabbing five balls for 94 yards. His receiving yards total was the most for any Dolphins rookie receiver in his first NFL game, but was also tied with Tyreek Hill (2022) for the most receiving yards for any receiver in their first game with the team in the franchise’s history. For a player who many thought was overdrafted when he was selected by new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft, Douglas’ debut was a delightful one to witness for Dolphins fans. Let’s hope that he can continue to progress forward as the season rolls on, and his counterpart, Chris Bell, can begin to contribute in meaningful ways as well. Quarterback Malik Willis and the organization as a whole would be significantly better for it. MVP TRACKER Week One – WR Caleb Douglas

title: Notes on Vikings Win Over the Packers
summary: The Minnesota Vikings came away with probably the most unusual win over the Green Bay Packers in the history of the division rivalry. It was unique in that the Vikings were down 12 points with twenty minutes to play but finished win a 17-point victory, and because the Vikings won by 17 points despite gaining […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Aaron Jones Sr. #33 of the Minnesota Vikings celebrates with fans after his rushing touchdown against the Green Bay Packers in the fourth quarter of a game at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings came away with probably the most unusual win over the Green Bay Packers in the history of the division rivalry. It was unique in that the Vikings were down 12 points with twenty minutes to play but finished win a 17-point victory, and because the Vikings won by 17 points despite gaining 180 fewer yards than the Packers. As I mentioned in the stock market report, early season games can be unpredictable based on opposition research or lack thereof, as each team can present any number of previously unseen looks/plays. The Packers seemed to have better opposition research on the Vikings than vice-versa, and that seemed to help them early on. Whether the Packers were able to capitalize on continuity of scheme with the Vikings, picking up videos of the Vikings practices, or gaining inside information from Kahlef Haillessie, a former Vikings safety who the Packers added to their practice squad last week, or a combination of all three, the Packers seemed to have the better game plan going into the game. Fortunately the Vikings coaching staff was able to make adjustments as the game progressed, and the players execute better, but the Vikings seemed to be at a disadvantage early on. Whether that continues next week or not remains to be seen. Penalties I’d say that penalties hurt the Packers more than the Vikings, except the Packers knocked out the Vikings starting quarterback Kyler Murray with an unnecessary roughness penalty, which likely cost the Vikings a lot more than 15 yards the rest of the game. Scary scene as Kyler Murray takes a massive hit and stays down after the play. pic.twitter.com/sVqZ7M24e4 — NFL on CBS 🏈 (@NFLonCBS) September 13, 2026 There was also an unnecessary roughness penalty against the Packers on a hit to the head of Justin Jefferson. Packers get flagged for a personal foul for this hit to the back of the head of Justin Jefferson pic.twitter.com/7Zd0CnF0M7 — Rate the Refs (@Rate_the_Refs) September 13, 2026 This was another obvious call where the player could have avoided head contact but chose differently. I would not be surprised if both players are fined at a minimum, and also suspended in a message from the league that it will not tolerate that sort of conduct at a time when concussions and CTE issues are rising. The league sometimes hands out what can be seen as stiffer penalties early in the season when the message value may resonate more and help prevent more incidents the rest of the season. Looking back at the other Packers penalties, none of them were particularly controversial, except the roughing the passer penalty for the player putting his full weight on the quarterback when taking him to the ground. This is the Aaron Rodgers penalty, resulting from Anthony Barr’s sack of Rodgers in 2017 in which he broke his collarbone. That rule has often had controversial enforcement because it is difficult to ascertain whether the defensive player was able to break his fall sufficiently or not and because it is difficult to both sack the quarterback and break your fall at the same time. In any case, the enforcement was consistent- protecting the quarterback. Except a facemask penalty targeting Wentz was missed, and another one against Justin Jefferson. It’s not uncommon to see more penalties early in the season as players get used to playing in real games again and new rules or emphasis by the league are enforced. But the latter wasn’t really the case as the penalties enforced have been on the books for years. It was simply a matter of the Packers either being undisciplined or poor in their technique to the point where it is outside the rules. Vikings Need to be Better It was great for the Vikings to beat the Packers by 17 points. Most will take that sort of win every time, regardless of circumstances. But it is also important to recognize that sort of win is unsustainable. You can’t expect the Vikings to continue to beat teams when they give up 180 more yards than they gain. The Vikings will need to be more explosive offensively than they were against the Packers and give up fewer explosive plays defensively. Those things can happen, but changes will need to be made. First, the Vikings will need to get Kyler Murray back at quarterback to have the potential for a more explosive passing game. Carson Wentz did a great job in relief of Murray on Sunday, all things considered, but he has limitations in the passing game that make it more difficult to be successful with chunk plays. Kyler Murray also needs to settle in and perform at least to the average to above average level he has achieved in the past. He didn’t do that in the eleven plays he had before suffering the concussion. Second, the defense probably needs to hone in on what works best for them. Every matchup is different, and there is a need to avoid being predictable, but one lesson from the Packers game is that interior gap blitzes are more effective than blitzes from the outside. Brian Flores began the game with more blitzing from the outside, which weren’t always as effective. But later in the game he went with more interior gap blitzes with linebackers that were more effective in disrupting Jordan Love. Again every matchup is different, but with Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel rushing off the edge, that may generate sufficient pressure by itself while interior blitzing may bring more value in added pressure up the middle that may disrupt the quarterback’s vision and throwing angle, in addition to generating sacks. On the backend, getting alignment and assignment right is paramount. There were at least a couple blown coverages against the Packers that resulted in explosive plays. That simply can’t happen. Communication is key, but each player is also responsible. Optimizing personnel on the backend is an ongoing task. I’m not sure Josh Metellus, who appeared to be involved in some blown coverages, needs to be out there for 100% of the defensive snaps as he was against the Packers. Theo Jackson also appeared to be out of place or at least late in getting there in the long touchdown pass to Christian Watson. I noticed Jacob Thomas had ten snaps at safety and Jay Ward can certainly play and has plenty of scheme experience. Not sure why he didn’t get any defensive snaps against the Packers- he did play on special teams. Eric Wilson also had a rough game against the Packers and played all but one snap. Ivan Pace Jr. had only ten snaps but performed better- including in coverage- than Wilson. Maybe that snap mix needs to be optimized going forward. In any case, the backend needs to be alignment and assignment sound in a fast moving defense- from a changed call perspective. They can’t count on pressure getting home every time. There is always some trial-and-error and adapting early in the season as the coaching staff discovers what works and what doesn’t, which players are doing well and which are struggling. There are a lot of moving parts. But there is a premium for figuring things out sooner rather than later. Brian Flores addressed some of those things in his Tuesday press conference: LIVE: Defensive Coordinator Brian Flores talks to the media https://t.co/kqO3JUIbWm — Minnesota Vikings (@Vikings) September 15, 2026 Another aspect of the passing game is quarterbacks need to see receivers other than Justin Jefferson. Yes, he is the best and often the primary target, but he’s not always open and other receivers are and don’t get targeted. There were a few times Jordan Addison was open and Wentz either didn’t see him or was too focused on Jefferson. Whatever the case, moving on from Jefferson when he’s covered and targeting other receivers…

title: Daily Norseman Reacts Survey: Are You Worried About the Vikings’ Offense?
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Vikings fans and fans across the country. It’s time for our SB Nation Reacts survey for this week, ladies and gentlemen, and we’ve got a couple of questions for you about our Minnesota […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: Jordan Mason #27 of the Minnesota Vikings runs with the ball for a touchdown during the fourth quarter of the game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Vikings fans and fans across the country. It’s time for our SB Nation Reacts survey for this week, ladies and gentlemen, and we’ve got a couple of questions for you about our Minnesota Vikings after their wild Week 1 victory over the Green Bay Packers. As we will every week this season, we’re going to ask you whether or not you think the Vikings are heading in the right direction. As always, we remind you that “the right direction” can mean different things to different people, so answer that using whatever criteria you see fit. It will be interesting to see how people feel after beating a division rival by three scores to start the season. The other question has to do with the Vikings’ offense and whether or not you’re worried about them after the first game. That may seem like an odd question to ask about a team that put up 39 points, but it’s worth noting that there were a few issues. The Vikings did only manage 239 yards of offense in Sunday’s game and averaged less than four yards per play. Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings combined for the same number of catches on Sunday as you and I combined for on Sunday. . .which is zero. And the offense was, largely, dormant for the better part of three quarters of play before getting to take advantage of some short fields in the fourth quarter. And, of course, there’s the fact that we’re one game into the season and the quarterback situation is already in disarray. So. . .how worried are you? Are you worried at all? Should we be worried? As always, we invite you to make your voice heard in our surveys for this week. You can cast your vote in our polls either here or in the Feed (where our polls will originate each week), and by sounding off in the comments section in either of those spots. With that, feel free to have at it, folks! We’ll have the results of these polls for you sometime before kickoff on Sunday. What is the panic level around the Vikings offense?
