title: NY Giants rookies impress against the Cowboys in Week 1
summary: The New York Giants are riding high after a great win over the Dallas Cowboys to open the season on Sunday Night Football. The win over the Cowboys was just about everything the Giants could have asked for. It was a definitive statement win over a division rival that had been relentlessly gassed up over […]
full_text: New York Giants linebacker Arvell Reese before a play against the Dallas Cowboys. | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New York Giants are riding high after a great win over the Dallas Cowboys to open the season on Sunday Night Football. The win over the Cowboys was just about everything the Giants could have asked for. It was a definitive statement win over a division rival that had been relentlessly gassed up over the previous four months. At the same time, the Giants weren’t perfect and have plenty to work on as they get ready for the Los Angeles Rams on Monday Night Football. Perhaps best of all, the Giants’ young players all stepped up in the win. The Giants are depending heavily on first and second year players to form the core of their team, the Giants’ rookie class certainly looked like they belonged on the field next to their veteran teammates. Let’s take a look at each of the Giants’ rookies who contributed to the win. Arvell Reese The fifth overall pick was on the field for 62 total plays, including 11 penalties, two Cowboys’ kickoffs, and the Giants’ lone punt. Reese was, overall, as advertised. He’s a big, long, and highly athletic linebacker who looked the part surrounded by the Giants’ other big, long, and athletic linebackers. He also showed off his football IQ all game long. Reese is a highly active communicator in the pre-snap phase, and he also appears to process quickly after the ball is snapped. He wastes little time getting to his landmarks, picking up pass catchers in coverage, or coming downhill to play the run. He also clearly understands where his gap responsibilities are, as well as where the defense is trying to funnel the ball. Reese looks smooth and rangy dropping into coverage at the second level, easily getting depth and into his coverage zones. He also did a good job of using his hands to keep blockers from latching on to him and allowing him to navigate traffic in pursuit. We also got to see Reese’s strength and violence as a tackler when the time came to get the ball carrier on the ground. Reese wasn’t quite as flashy as former teammates Sonny Styles and Caleb Downs, but he did finish second to Tremaine Edmunds in total tackles. I’d like to see more splash plays from Reese, and I think we will as the season progresses, but this was an impressive introduction for the linebacker. SiSi Mauigoa is a difference making guard. Watch this raw power on the move once he torques; he tosses Ogbonnia to the deck, allowing Tracy Jr. to cut behind for an extra few yards. pic.twitter.com/3mewi9nYQ4 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 Sisi Mauigoa The big man had a long night, but it was also about as good a debut as you could ask for from the 10th overall pick. Mauigoa was on the field for 78 total snaps, including each of Dominic Zvada’s extra points and eight penalties. I won’t go quite so far as to say that Mauigoa was dominant in his debut, but he was very good in both pass protection and as a run blocker. We knew that Mauigoa is an obviously powerful young man who could distort the line of scrimmage and dig defenders out of gaps in the run game. We also knew that, as a converted tackle, he has great athletic traits for a guard. We got to see both aspects of his game on display against the Cowboys. Mauigoa was easily able to move laterally to mirror interior rushers, get in position to help with center-guard and guard-tackle double teams, and execute both slide protections and outside zone runs. Mauigoa’s power was featured in the downhill run game as well as when he was asked to match up with the likes of Kenny Clark one-on-one. Sisi might not have dominated his opponents, but the right side was rarely a concern for the offense. That’s about as good a thing as you can say for a rookie guard in his first start. #Giants rookie G Francis Mauigoa in his NFL debut: • 36 pass-blocking snaps • 0 pressures allowed • 0 QB hits He's the first rookie since 2018 to record 35+ pass-blocking snaps in Week 1 without allowing a pressure. (via @NextGenStats ) https://t.co/9XK0FvQyFn pic.twitter.com/ecOvTFs5GE — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 14, 2026 Colton Hood Hood didn’t get much work against the Cowboys. The Giants only had their second round pick on the field for 18 plays on Sunday night, the first 11 of which came on special teams. He was a fixture on both the Giants’ kick coverage teams and punt return teams. He did get six snaps on defense, playing when Greg Newsome II or Deonte Banks were off the field. That’s a very small sample size and the Cowboys only targeted Hood twice (one reception). He was generally in good position and was sticky in coverage on his man, including against George Pickens. That said, it’s also appeared as though the game was a bit fast on the reception he gave up. He was too off-balance to make the tackle after the catch on the come-back route, allowing YAC up the sideline. Malachi Fields Fields didn’t get much work as a pass catcher for the Giants. He was targeted four times, catching two passes for a 25 yards, 19 of which came on one catch. Fields was able to get behind the Dallas defense on one of his targets, but Dart overthrew him. It could have been a huge play, but it wasn’t to be. Fields had much more of an impact as a blocker in the run game for the Giants. Greg Roman’s blocking schemes weren’t shy about using condensed sets and using Fields as a blocker on the play side. On some of the plays, they seemed to view him as an extra tight end, and he held up well as such. For instance, the Giants used an uncommon 20-personnel set (two backs, no tight ends) on their second offensive play of the game. It was a curious look that had wide receiver Braxton Berrios line up in the backfield with Devin Singletary while fullback Patrick Ricard line up at tight end next to Andrew Thomas. The Giants asked Fields to release to the second level and pick up linebacker Dee Winters, and he simply took Winters out of the play. ( Fields is the wide receiver on the offensive left wearing red gloves .) The Giants also made use of Fields’ frame as a downfield obstacle, using his routes to help create space for his teammates in various passing concepts. Dominic Zvada Perhaps the best compliment I can give Zvada is that I forgot he was a rookie — as well as long snapper Ben Mann. The special teams operation was as clean as I’ve seen in some time. The Giants didn’t have to ask Zvada to show off his leg strength, but there was never a doubt about his ability to hit extra points. I was particularly impressed by how he handled kickoffs. Zvada was able to consistently drop the ball inside of the Dallas 5-yard line, three times forcing KaVonte Turpin to field the ball from the 1-yard line (2.2-yard line on average). The Giants limited Turpin, one of the NFL’s most dangerous kickoff returners, to 24.4 yards per return and their average starting field position was the 26.4-yard line. Zvada’s accuracy and ability to get distance and hangtime on his kickoffs certainly helped the Giants’ coverage team, while neutralizing Turpin helped create hidden yardage for the defense. Great start for the UDFA rookie.
author: Chris Pflum

title: Tales from the Timeline: NY Giants dominate the Cowboys
summary: The New York Giants opened their 2026 season with a 28-20 upset victory over the Dallas Cowboys. New York’s offense dictated the terms against Dallas’ defense, while Christian Parker’s revamped defensive unit struggled to find answers for Matt Nagy’s scheme. The Giants outgained Dallas by 150 yards and held a commanding 13:20 advantage in time […]
full_text: The New York Giants opened their 2026 season with a 28-20 upset victory over the Dallas Cowboys. New York’s offense dictated the terms against Dallas’ defense, while Christian Parker’s revamped defensive unit struggled to find answers for Matt Nagy’s scheme. The Giants outgained Dallas by 150 yards and held a commanding 13:20 advantage in time of possession. The tape was one of the more enjoyable evaluations I’ve studied. From a philosophical standpoint, little of it was surprising — we knew the Giants wanted to play with heavy personnel and operate more under center. What exceeded my expectations, however, was the degree to which New York successfully established the run, while maintaining efficiency and effectiveness through the air. The Giants consistently created favorable offensive situations, which is one reason why they had four touchdown drives and four drives of 10-plus plays. Dart finished 9 of 11 on third down, and these charts illustrate just how well he performed on Sunday Night Football: Jaxson Dart Final Stats 23/29 (79%) 230 passing yards (7.9 ypa) 10 rushes | 54 rushing yards 3 TDs | 2 sacks | 1 fumble +0.73 EPA/play (98th %ile) 74% success rate (29/39) +10.9% CPOE 8.6 aDOT pic.twitter.com/I39ihnichM — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) September 14, 2026 Jaxson Dart with the best QB performance in Week 1. • EPA/Play: +0.73 (1st) • WPA/Play: +2.2% (1st) Every 5 plays, Dart added 3.5 expected points and 11% win probability for the Giants. pic.twitter.com/01OTeikQyu — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) September 14, 2026 It was an elite performance by Dart, who found solutions early in the game, including on this third-and-4 below: Great job by Jaxson Dart to throw away from defensive leverage on the mesh that opened up Isaiah Likely on third-and-four. Dart was DIALED in and poised throughout the game, as the #Giants offensively dictated to Dallas all night. pic.twitter.com/lWb6caT47j — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 I love how Dart threw away from the defender’s position, allowing Isaiah Likely (9) to catch the football and nearly spin away from the tackle and into the end zone. It’s a mesh concept with Odell Beckham Jr. (13) running the MUSH ( man under ) and Likely running the MOSH ( man over ); Devin Singletary (26) was released to the boundary, which created space in the middle of the field. Dallas had several coverage assignments that were blown throughout the game. There was a miscommunication above, as Dallas’ zone defender attempted to push Likely to a defensive player that I’m not convinced was present. Hooker (24) was too patient to close width on Likely, who surrendered the catch, but Singletary’s flare and Beckham’s drag route also removed two defenders from the area. Dart was elite, too, in the two minute drill: Jaxson Dart finished the first half in an excellent fashion after the Holland INT. Dart went 4/4 with this third down conversation, as well as the touchdown to Likely off the blown Dallas' coverage. pic.twitter.com/xIaKXPZAfX — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 Dart made several high-level throws throughout the game, but the story of the offense was still the Giants’ rushing attack. New York’s first play from scrimmage was this tackle-over formation, which placed Jermaine Eluemunor (71) and Andrew Thomas (78) next to each other on the Cam Skattebo (44) 4-yard gain: The #Giants start the John Harbaugh era off with a tackle-over formation. Jermaine Eluemunor & Andrew Thomas w/ Patrick Ricard on the kick-out. Jon Runyan pulled to create an extra gap toward the field w/ Cam Skattebo picking up 4 yds behind his blocks. 1st OFF play. pic.twitter.com/6UyImb1ePt — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 Matt Nagy and Greg Roman went into their play-calling bag. New York kept a diverse and physical rushing attack that used pre-snap motion to create easier angles of approach for the Giants’ blockers. Skattebo is the perfect back to complement the physical approach utilized by the Giants’ coaching staff: All-22 of Skattebo vs. Overshown, two plays. https://t.co/drHS5ROCUS pic.twitter.com/R006CMGbyk — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 Two additions to the Giants really embody physicality, and those are guard Sisi Mauigoa and fullback Patrick Ricard. Mauigoa was the 10th overall selection in the draft, and Ricard followed Harbaugh to New York. He was the long-time full-back for the Ravens, but is a big-man’s Swiss Army knife, wearing the full-back, H-Back, and TE hats effectively. Ricard’s 37 snaps set the tone and kept the Giants’ offense true to their physical philosophy. Also, Andrew Thomas and Chris Manhertz blocking together is very fun to watch: Chris Manhertz and Andrew Thomas 💪 pic.twitter.com/ZqF34nvFLm — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 Andrew Thomas + Chris Manhertz with SiSi pulling 🫡 pic.twitter.com/SZDeVFAZpv — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 SiSi Mauigoa is a difference making guard. Watch this raw power on the move once he torques; he tosses Ogbonnia to the deck, allowing Tracy Jr. to cut behind for an extra few yards. pic.twitter.com/3mewi9nYQ4 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 UPDATE! Andrew Thomas is still very fun to watch. pic.twitter.com/iCQGjOfJy3 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 I can't overstate Patrick Ricard's impact on this #Giants win. He played 37 snaps and allowed the Giants to blend 21/12/13 personnel in a creative fashion. Nagy + Roman designed excellent run schemes w/ motion, and he was entrusted to handle DEs in protection. What an asset. — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 Guy is on an island against Rashan Gary, handling rip moves and readjusting well to give Dart enough time to fire. pic.twitter.com/UCWs9eLjzD — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 Isaiah Likely was another offseason addition who caught all eight of his targets for 78 yards and two touchdowns. This route below against cornerback Shavon Revel really showcases how smooth and dangerous Likely is as a weapon: Isaiah Likely's deceptive route running 👀 pic.twitter.com/uxbdPH1KLe — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 The second-half Devin Singletary sequence is detailed below: The Singletary sequence wouldn't have happened on previous #Giants teams. However, a blown screen is all too familiar. JMS misses his block, but space was there. Nagy attacked soft leverage w/ Nabers on the next play and then used the attention paid to Nabers to find Singletary… pic.twitter.com/8kjTSBCQb3 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 The Giants dictated the game from start to finish, putting Parker in a position that New York fans haven’t seen in quite some time — the position of having no answers. Defense I was very pleased to see how effective D.J. Reader (98) was for the New York Giants. It didn’t show up in the stat-sheet, but Reader consistently forced Javonte Williams (33) to bounce runs away from their intended destination: The first play of the game last night. DJ Reader stacked the center and stopped the run at the LOS. Reader was the highest-graded run-defense player by PFF in the #Giants win. pic.twitter.com/Qzpt149JlU — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 Nose 👏 tackle 👏 pic.twitter.com/aCavdj2pqm — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 pic.twitter.com/VQhPuzRSD2 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 Much like Reader, the Giants edge defenders didn’t have eye-popping stats, but they were effective and disruptive. Here are positive plays from Abdul Carter, Brian Burns, Chauncey Golston, and Kayvon Thibodeaux: Abdul Carter's explosiveness and control to reorient and close width is something special pic.twitter.com/JK0biNBh8j — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 The tight end has seen better days. pic.twitter.com/6AsWQcjhPp — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 Chauncey Golston fights through two blockers to force Javonte Williams to bounce the run to the opposite side.…

title: NY Giants QB Jaxson Dart was dialed in against the Cowboys
summary: The New York Giants punched the Dallas Cowboys in the mouth en route to a 28-20 Week 1 victory. A smash-mouth, varied rushing attack set the tone for New York, featuring heavy formations and plenty of under-center looks. But the efficient play of second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart was the catalyst behind the Giants’ rare victory […]
full_text: The New York Giants punched the Dallas Cowboys in the mouth en route to a 28-20 Week 1 victory. A smash-mouth, varied rushing attack set the tone for New York, featuring heavy formations and plenty of under-center looks. But the efficient play of second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart was the catalyst behind the Giants’ rare victory over Dallas. Dart finished 23 of 29 ( 79% completion rate ) for 230 passing yards and three passing touchdowns, with 54 yards rushingon 11 carries. New York finished 9/11 on third down, and Dart found answers to Christian Parker’s defense, which, in fairness, had several breakdowns in coverage/assingments. Not only did Dart pass the eye-test, but the numbers back his performance up as well: Jaxson Dart with the best QB performance in Week 1. • EPA/Play: +0.73 (1st) • WPA/Play: +2.2% (1st) Every 5 plays, Dart added 3.5 expected points and 11% win probability for the Giants. pic.twitter.com/01OTeikQyu — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) September 14, 2026 Courtesy of Doug Analytics, Dart’s +0.73 EPA/Play ( Expected Points Added ) ranked first, as well as his WPA/Play ( Win Probability Added ). As Doug states, Dart added 3.5 expected points on every five plays the Giants took — an elite performance by the second-year signal caller. Here’s what NFL Next Gen had to say about Dart’s performance, along with his throwing chart: The Giants punted the football one time against Dallas, and they mounted four touchdown drives, as well as four drives of 10-plus plays. Dart wasn’t exactly slinging the ball all over the yard — he didn’t have to — but he led the offense, made the right checks, was in command for much of the game ( he didn’t account for Caleb Downs on the EMPTY blitz ), and made some high-level throws that allowed the Giants to maintain their time-consuming drives. High-level throws via GIPHY The Giants faced this third-and-4 in the red zone. Stalling out and kicking a field goal was the normal outcome in these situations — last time the Giants opened against Dallas, it was a blocked field goal that Andrew Thomas hurt his hamstring on — but I digress. The Giants align in 11 personnel, shot-gun, 3×1 set with a mesh concept over the middle of the field. Dallas ran a cover-four-match play and Isaiah Likely (9) ran the MOSH ( man over ) Odell Beckham Jr.’s (13) MUSH ( man under ). Daron Bland (26) seemed to be in MEG on the backside No. 1 ( Beckham ), and as the veteran receiver ran the MUSH, linebacker Dee Winters (53) pushed the MOSH ( Likely ) toward Bland and safety Malik Hooker (24). Likely sat inside of Hooker, who was late to receive the push, and Dart did a fantastic job putting the football toward Likely’s inside shoulder — away from Hooker. The middle of the field was cleared out by the drag route from Beckham. I appreciate how the mesh concept was Dart’s second read after he saw match principles when viewing his first read toward Malachi Fields (88) and Darnell Mooney (17). The latter was the No. 2 receiver ( innermost ), and he ran to the flat with Fields running a corner off his vertical stem. With the safety over top, Dallas matched three over two, and Dart came off the look and saw the vacated space in the middle of the field and Hooker’s depth. Precise ball placement and a calm read by Dart led to another third-down conversion on the Giants’ first drive. via GIPHY Up 7-0, just outside mid-field, Dart quickly processed the zone coverage and found Malik Nabers for 7 yards on second-and-9. Nabers ran the hook, and Fields ran the wheel as the No. 2 receiver. Dart had to wait for the curl/flat to expand with Cam Skattebo’s (44) flare route. This put the Giants into a third-and-2 that they failed to convert, which led to their only punt of the game. There was plenty of discussion about Dart’s ability to operate quick game concepts efficiently throughout the off-season; sure, this was from the shotgun, and perhaps not perfect, but it did give New York the opportunity to convert on the following play. via GIPHY Jaxson Dart was such a cool customer on 3rd downs. Giants were faced with 3rd&10 here on their second TD drive. A blown pass protection assignment leads to an immediately free A gap pressure. Dart stands tall in the pocket and delivers a seed on the money outside the numbers 👀 pic.twitter.com/Ej4bQjRctC — Dan Schneier (@DanSchneierNFL) September 14, 2026 Dart extended a drive with this 19yard throw to Likely. Dallas was in Cover-1 and the Giants ran a DAGGER concept to the field. Dart quickly diagnosed man-coverage and attacked the corner route to Likely on the backside. Shavon Revel (28) faced the unfortunate task of guard Likely in space; the tight end manipulated Revel and exploded outside for the first down. Dart was phenomenal under pressure on the play, as the Giants’ offensive line had a rare mishap. Unfortunately, Tyrone Tracy Jr. would fumble plays later. Two-minute drill Dart executed an impressive two-minute drill after Jevon Holland’s interception. Jon Runyan committed a false-start, which put the Giants into this third-and-9: via GIPHY via GIPHY Dart successfully diagnosed the defense during his shotgun drop, prompting him to switch to the backside one (Nabers) and target vulnerabilities in the now-recognized Cover-2 defense. Dart put touch over the top of the flat defender and in front of the bailing-deep- half player. He was mentally and physically dialed in on this play when the lights were brightest in a crucial two-minute drill. He followed this third-and-9 conversion with this far-hash completion to Darnell Mooney (17): via GIPHY Dallas aligned in a Cover-3 strong-side buzz over Likely’s position against a 2×2 set. The deep third defender to the field lost leverage inside to Darnell Mooney’s vertical stem; Mooney exploded toward the sideline when the defender was on the numbers and the curl/flat was enticed to step forward due to the presence of Devin Singletary (26) in the flat. Dart planted and drove the football into Mooney; credit to Mooney for being a professional wide receiver and having soft hands and feet that are spatially aware. Isaiah Likely was 8.8 yards away from the nearest defender when the ball arrived on this touchdown 🫣 DALvsNYG on NBC/Peacock Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/rIenIu8EGo — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) September 14, 2026 Dart finished the two-minute drill by finding a wide-open Isaiah Likely in the back of the end zone. The Cowboys had a blown coverage and Dart quickly recognized that two defenders reacted to Mooney’s whip route underneath. The No. 2 receiver on the previous play was Likely, who caught a whip route underneath. Second half via GIPHY via GIPHY The Giants opened the second half with a 12-play, 74-yard drive. On second-and-9, they picked up 16 yards on a catch that was heavily aided by play action. New York had already established the run, and Dallas failed to adjust, allowing the under-center play-action look to pull the linebackers toward the line of scrimmage. That created space for Dart to layer a touch pass over the top to Malik Nabers. And then there was the Devin Singletary sequence: The Singletary sequence wouldn't have happened on previous #Giants teams. However, a blown screen is all too familiar. JMS misses his block, but space was there. Nagy attacked soft leverage w/ Nabers on the next play and then used the attention paid to Nabers to find Singletary… pic.twitter.com/8kjTSBCQb3 — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) September 14, 2026 The Giants’ coaching staff, Dart, and the entire Giants team just kept exploiting the vulnerable flats, while Dallas stayed at depth and kept multiple pairs of eyes on Nabers. Dart’s rushing Dart rushed for 54 yards on 11 carries. Dart showed vision that was coupled with timely play calls and designs from the Giants’ coaching staff. Dart on the move!!! 💨 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/6DwDC4ZUdk — New York Giants (@Giants) September 14, 2026 via GIPHY Final thoughts Dart shined in the bright lights and is now technically 2-0 against…

title: NFL power rankings, Week 2: NY Giants take massive jump
summary: Sunday night’s impressive victory over the Dallas Cowboys has resulted in the New York Giants taking a massive leap in Week 2 NFL power rankings. The Giants have moved from No. 23 in our aggregated rankings from around the Internet to No. 16, the league’s midpoint. ESPN | No. 18 Week 1 result: Beat the Cowboys 28-20Non-QB […]
full_text: Sunday night’s impressive victory over the Dallas Cowboys has resulted in the New York Giants taking a massive leap in Week 2 NFL power rankings. The Giants have moved from No. 23 in our aggregated rankings from around the Internet to No. 16, the league’s midpoint. ESPN | No. 18 Week 1 result: Beat the Cowboys 28-20 Non-QB newcomer debut: TE Isaiah Likely Likely was quarterback Jaxson Dart’s go-to receiver, catching two third-down passes on the game-ending drive to go along with two touchdowns earlier. Overall, Likely caught all eight targets for 78 yards. The chemistry with Dart throughout training camp carried over to the season, to the point where it’s easy to see Likely having a huge campaign despite never reaching 500 receiving yards in any of his four years with the Ravens. The performance was no surprise to coach John Harbaugh. “I mean, we paid him a lot,” Harbaugh said with a laugh. “That’s what we paid him for, and he did it.” FOX Sports | No. 17 It’s a well-deserved leap in the rankings after John Harbaugh’s debut showed he has a tough, well-rounded and healthy team. When WR Malik Nabers is off his pitch count, this versatile offense is going to cause problems for everyone. Pro Football Network | No. 23 The John Harbaugh era of New York Giants football kicked off in triumphant fashion. They defeated the Cowboys at home, coming away from Sunday night with a key divisional victory. Emotions were high with the Giants’ pregame ceremony honoring those affected by Sept. 11, and New York went home happy. Jaxson Dart got it done through the air and on the ground, throwing for 230 and three passing touchdowns while rushing for 57 yards. The likes of Isaiah Likely and Cam Skattebo were key in the Giants’ victory, and the team’s run defense limited Dallas’ offense to just 3.8 yards per carry. USA Today | No. 14 Don’t want to overrate them this early, but Sunday night’s victory over the Cowboys was no fluke. This was efficient, smashmouth, Harbaugh football, and the rest of the NFC East is officially on notice. Yahoo Sports | No. 14 No team had a better offensive EPA per play through Sunday’s Week 1 games than the Giants. Not even the Bears, who scored 59 points. What stood out was the impact new tight end Isaiah Likely had. He led the Giants with eight catches for 78 yards and two touchdowns. If the Giants’ offense stays mostly healthy, perhaps this can be a surprise playoff team. The Athletic | No. 18 What we learned: They might be for real High expectations around the hiring of John Harbaugh were tempered by what seemed to be just an OK roster. But the Harbaugh era started smashingly, Jaxson Dart looked legit and the defense more than held its own against a good (or so we thought) Dallas offense. Bleacher Report | No. 21 So maybe hiring John Harbaugh was a pretty good idea. Offensively Sunday night, New York was ruthlessly efficient. Jaxson Dart was poised and accurate. Cam Skattebo didn’t have huge numbers, but he got the tough yards when he needed to. Tight end Isaiah Likely was a revelation in his first game with the team. New York was 9-of-11 on third down. That’s nuts. The defense remains a work in progress, but it made just enough plays against one of the NFL’s best offenses a year ago to win the day—and a second straight contest with the Cowboys at Met Life Stadium. It’s still too early to say the Giants are good—the Dallas defense has been awful dating back to 2025. But they were in Week 1, and we’ll find out soon enough how sustainable the improvement is.

title: Eagles-Commanders Film Review: Offense did some good things but must improve
summary: It’s easy to look at the Eagles scoring 24 points, averaging six yards per play, and conclude the offense played well in the first game of the season. Unfortunately, I don’t think it did. The Eagles generated 318 yards, but 180 of them came on four plays. They finished with only 10 first downs, punted […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Saquon Barkley #26 of the Philadelphia Eagles runs against Nick Cross #25 of the Washington Commanders in the second quarter of a game at Lincoln Financial Field on September 13, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s easy to look at the Eagles scoring 24 points, averaging six yards per play, and conclude the offense played well in the first game of the season. Unfortunately, I don’t think it did. The Eagles generated 318 yards, but 180 of them came on four plays. They finished with only 10 first downs, punted seven times, and had six possessions without earning a single first down. They also went three-and-out on three consecutive drives in the third quarter. Elite players made enough elite plays to win the game, but they showed little consistency. We saw this at times last season. The Eagles won games despite the offense failing to establish any rhythm, and the result often disguised the performance. That is not sustainable. However, it is Week 1. Sean Mannion is a brand-new offensive coordinator, and the Eagles are still working out what this offense should look like. I’m not panicking after one game. The important thing is whether Mannion recognizes the problems and adapts. Let’s get into the film. We are back, baby! Offense The contrast between the Eagles’ different personnel groupings was significant in this one. They rushed for 118 yards on 14 attempts from 11 personnel, compared with only 18 yards on 11 attempts from 12 personnel. Those figures include Hurts’ rushing production and are heavily influenced by Barkley’s 42-yard run, so they require some context. Still, Washington consistently matched 12 personnel with its base defense, and the Eagles repeatedly ran into condensed, crowded fronts. We saw this exact issue last year. A lot of teams run well out of condensed formations, but I’ve yet to see the Eagles do it well. This counter run was a bad early sign. Dallas Goedert’s positioning makes the pull predictable, there is no real misdirection, and Washington can attack downhill without hesitation. I hoped we would see more misdirection in the run game. The Eagles ran counter only once, and I was surprised that we didn’t see more duo. The run game was overwhelmingly zone-based, which isn’t a shock considering Mannion’s background, but I’m still a little concerned about how it fits our personnel. Individual execution was a problem, but the structure did not provide enough help at times. Running repeatedly from heavy personnel into stacked boxes is making life unnecessarily difficult. We are back! Eagles Week 1 Offense Thread vs. Washington. 1) I started worrying a little early on when I saw this rep of Counter early on. The Eagles seemed to run into stacked boxes from heavy personnel far too often, and it ended as you would have expected. This was the only… pic.twitter.com/JLs7tYeFpN — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 14, 2026 Right, just a heads up. I posted the original thread online before Landon Dickerson acknowledged that he had been playing hurt and was subsequently placed on injured reserve. My immediate reaction to the film was that his movement looked completely wrong. We now know why. I didn’t want to kill him in the review, but I could have posted 30 clips of him looking bad. It was probably the worst offensive line film I’ve watched from an individual. Dickerson played all 55 offensive snaps despite clearly being unable to move properly. He was charged with four pressures, including a sack. I am not blaming Dickerson for that performance. The coaches deserve criticism for letting an obviously compromised player stay on the field for the entire game. I can’t just ignore Dickerson in this review because his play made it really hard to run the offense. But, just be aware I’m not blaming him for this. You can see the physical limitation here. Dickerson cannot adjust his feet or redirect with the defender. This isn’t normal poor technique from a player losing an isolated rep. His body won’t let him execute the assignment. The guy could barely move. The Eagles put both Dickerson and the rest of the offense in a terrible position by asking him to play through it. 2) We saw signs of what was to come early on. I really don't want to spend the whole thread kicking Landon Dickerson, since he's already faced enough criticism, but it really wasn't good. Like, unplayable levels of not good. Just ignore the end result and watch his movement.… pic.twitter.com/ScWunMtILO — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 14, 2026 This was one of the Eagles’ better outside-zone runs, and it highlights the importance of personnel. Johnny Mundt does an excellent job controlling the edge, allowing Barkley to press the run before getting outside. The issue with Mundt is when he’s on the field, the Eagles’ offense can become predictable. They must find a way to get him involved as a receiver at times. The Eagles do not have many receivers who can consistently move defenders from condensed formations. Makai Lemon and DeVonta Smith aren’t big receivers, so a blocking tight end matters. Mundt creates an edge here that the Eagles struggled to establish on several other outside-zone attempts. I’m still concerned about the Eagles leaning too heavily on outside zone. If it is going to become a foundational concept, they must choose their moments more effectively and connect it to the passing game. After showing Washington this look, I expected to see more play-action bootlegs or movement passes building from the same action. Instead, the run and pass games often felt disconnected. Which was a shame, considering everything we have read about Mannion. 3) Hey, a rare nice rep of outside zone! I'm very concerned about the Eagles living in the outside zone world, but if you are going to use it more, you need to pick your moments better. This works because the safety comes downhill from the opposite side, and they are running… pic.twitter.com/kdsuIbsF5h — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 14, 2026 Here is another example of Dickerson’s injury affecting the offense. Once again, forget the outcome and focus on his lower body. His feet are in no position to make contact, and he cannot generate any power or control because his base has collapsed. 4) I promise I won't post a whole thread of Dickerson's failings, but you can't analyze the offense without looking at his performance. You have plays like this that can't even get going. Again, ignore the result; just focus on the movement and technique. Look at the position… pic.twitter.com/FRIT4eRt9z — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 14, 2026 This is the first of the explosive plays that carried the offense. The under center running game struggled, but the Eagles must keep developing it because it enables throws like this. The Eagles use play action and a three-level stretch concept. Based on the design, the ball should go to Goedert, but Hurts likes the matchup downfield and makes an extremely aggressive throw to Dontayvion Wicks. The velocity and placement are outstanding. Hurts’ deep-ball accuracy remains one of the offense’s cheat codes. Wicks deserves enormous credit, too. He runs the clear-out route, but he runs it hard and stays ready for the football. We have seen far too many clear-out routes over the years where a receiver (who might currently be on the Patriots…) slows down or never expects the pass. Wicks stays engaged throughout the whole rep, locates the ball, and finishes the play for a big gain. If you are running a route, you always have to believe the ball might come your way. This is excellent. (should have posted this before the previous play) 5) Hurts' deep ball accuracy remains the offense's cheat code. The velocity and ball placement are just so good. The under center run game didn't work particularly well, but the Eagles need to keep working it into the offense… pic.twitter.com/E2dl28GTnL — Jonny Page…

title: Eagles roster news: Landon Dickerson to IR among 3 moves
summary: The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced three roster moves on Tuesday afternoon. Here’s an overview: Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. LANDON DICKERSON Dickerson to IR was previously reported on Monday evening. The Eagles’ three-time Pro Bowl left guard admitted that he “was a complete liability” during the team’s Week 1 win over […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - JUNE 10: Philadelphia Eagles guard Landon Dickerson #69 looks on during the Philadelphia Eagles off season minicamp on June 10th, 2026 at the Jefferson Health Training Complex in Philadelphia, PA. (Photo by Terence Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced three roster moves on Tuesday afternoon. Here’s an overview: OG Landon Dickerson was placed on injured reserve. WR Britain Covey was signed from the practice squad to the active roster. TE Josiah Deguara was signed to the practice squad. Let’s sort through this news on a player-by-player basis. LANDON DICKERSON Dickerson to IR was previously reported on Monday evening. The Eagles’ three-time Pro Bowl left guard admitted that he “was a complete liability” during the team’s Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders. Dickerson also added that he got hurt in training camp and he’s hopeful that the time off will help him get fully healthy. By going on IR, he’s automatically ineligible to play in the Eagles’ next four games. The soonest he can return to the active roster is Week 6. One must wonder if this rest will truly allow Dickerson to get back to form. It seems entirely possible that he’s just physically diminished at this point in his career. That’s a very sad and unfortunate thought … but there’s much to suggest that might be the case: Dickerson has an extensive injury history dating back to his college football days. Dickerson struggled in 2025. Speaking shortly after the conclusion of last season, Dickerson did not sound very optimistic about making a full recovery . Dickerson reportedly gave thought to retiring in the offseason. He’s since denied as much … but he reportedly agreed to a revised deal where he took a pay cut and had a year lopped off his contract. Why would he do that if he felt great about his outlook? Dickerson struggled in training camp this summer and looked to be lumbering around at times. Speaking on SportsRadio 94WIP on Tuesday, Nick Sirianni said the Eagles will be missing Dickerson “ for the foreseeable future .” Dickerson himself talked about the benefit of going on IR in order to “have a good stretch at the back end of the season.” Even putting his health aside, which is impossible to do, there’s question about Dickerson’s fit in the Eagles’ new blocking scheme. To be clear, I hope my skepticism is wrong. It would be such a massive deal if he’s able to return to form. I tend to think that the Eagles didn’t want to outright bench Dickerson, who has earned legendary status for sacrificing his body in order for the team to win Super Bowl LIX. I think he might be done and they’re hoping that the replacement plan will work out well so they don’t have to put him back on the field. It remains to be seen how the Eagles will actually replace him. The expectation is that Drew Kendall will take over at left guard … but we’ll see if that’s the case. BRITAIN COVEY The Eagles temporarily elevated Covey from the practice squad in Week 1 to be their punt returner against the Commanders. To no surprise, he was effective in that capacity. Now he’s back on the roster. This development means that the Eagles are currently carrying seven wide receivers on the roster: DeVonta Smith, Dontayvion Wicks, Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown, Elijah Moore, and Covey. Smith, Wicks, and Lemon comprise the top three. Cooper saw limited playing time on offense as a fourth receiver in addition to being a major factor on special teams coverage. Brown was active in Week 1 but played zero snaps while Moore was a healthy scratch. JOSIAH DEGUARA The 29-year-old Deguara was originally a third-round pick (No. 94 overall) by the Green Bay Packers in the 2020 NFL Draft. He notably overlapped with current Eagles tight ends coach and run game coordinator Ryan Mahaffey on the Packers from 2021-2023. Making 12 starts in 77 regular season games, Deguara has logged 66 career targets for 53 receptions, 471 receiving yards, and three touchdowns. His most recent NFL stop prior to this was a three-day stint on the New York Giants’ roster back in late August. With the Eagles recently placing Eli Stowers on injured reserve , the team only had three tight ends on the roster (Dallas Goedert, Johnny Mundt, E.J. Jenkins) and none on the practice squad. Now they have a fourth tight end for practice purposes, at the very least. STILL ONE OPEN ROSTER SPOT Dickerson and Stowers going to IR opened up two roster spots. Signing Covey filled one of those openings. The Birds still have one vacancy remaining.

title: NFL Week 1 overreactions and exaggerations
summary: Last season in Week 1 the Raiders beat the Patriots. They then went completely separate ways, the Patriots going 14-3 and to the Super Bowl, the Raiders to 3-14 and the #1 overall pick. Also that week the Vikings beat the Bears, with JJ McCarthy throwing 3 TDs. The Bears went on to win the […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - SEPTEMBER 13: Caleb Williams #18 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the first quarter against the Carolina Panthers of the game at Bank of America Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Jared C. Tilton/Getty Images) | Getty Images Last season in Week 1 the Raiders beat the Patriots. They then went completely separate ways, the Patriots going 14-3 and to the Super Bowl, the Raiders to 3-14 and the #1 overall pick. Also that week the Vikings beat the Bears, with JJ McCarthy throwing 3 TDs. The Bears went on to win the NFC North, the Vikings finished with the joint worst record in division and JJ McCarthy fell apart. So Week 1 can be an aberration. But we can still overreact. The New Dream Team The Rams are cooked. No team scored fewer points in Week 1 than Sean McVay’s star studded and jet lagged team. The Falcons were on their third string QB, who had back spasms, and the Dolphins, Browns, and Titans participated in football games; all outscored the Super Bowl favorites. Myles Garrett is out for at least four weeks after doing absolutely nothing in the first week. Maybe Aaron Donald, who hasn’t played in two years, could play soon and turn things around. It’s always good to count on retirees in a football game. Regression is mean Drake Maye threw three interceptions and helped the Patriots blow a 10 point lead to Drew Lock. If you’re keeping track at home, that’s now 11 turnovers in five straight games against teams that made the playoffs last year. Next up: another 2025 playoff team! If the Lions are Super Bowl contenders, then so are the Saints Tyler Shough had 410 yards and 3 TDs and Chris Olave had 182 yards on 10 catches as the Lions and Saints traded punches over five quarters. New Orleans got behind 21-0 but stormed back, on the road, to tie the game 24-24 with just over a minute to play and lost on a failed 2 point conversion. If the Saints are mid, then so are the Lions Detroit gave up 410 yards and 3 TDs to Tyler Shough, and needed a failed two point conversion in OT to defeat New Orleans at home after blowing a 21 point lead. Bears and Panthers, oh my If you’re Chicago or Carolina, you’ve got to feel really good about your offense. The Bears had two 100 yard rushers, a staple of a Ben Johnson offense! Bryce Young had 361 yards and 3 TDs, one of the best games of his career! If you’re Chicago or Carolina, you’ve got to feel pretty horrible about your defense. The Panthers giving up 59 points is of course extremely embarrassing and should result in several changes to the lineup. But the Bears gave up 37 points, despite 3 takeaways. It’s more of the same for the Bears, who last year led the league in turnovers but still had just the 23rd scoring defense. Where were you when… The Chargers, who have the greatest QB of all time in Justin Hebert and football genius Mike McDaniel, scored an unbelievable 14 points against the vaunted Arizona Cardinals. McDaniel’s game plan and Herbert’s jersey are on their way to Canton. Packers offense: 22 points in four quarters. Packers defense: 22 points in the fourth quarter. The Greatest Offense There Is, formerly known as the Dallas Cowboys, had two punts and a turnover on their first four possessions. Cam Skattebo’s quest for 300 carries for 2000 yards (at least 117.7 yards per game at 6.7 yards per carry) began with 18 carries for 81 yards (4.5 yards per carry). Congratulations to Dontayvion Wicks and Makai Lemon, who lead the league in yards per reception and negative yards per reception, respectively!

title: Eagles News: Landon Dickerson replacement options
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! With Landon Dickerson expected to go on injured reserve, the Eagles need a new starting left guard. Drew Kendall should and likely will be be the first man up. I know people love Willie Lampkin — and I’m one of them! […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Drew Kendall #66 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the national anthem prior to an NFL preseason football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! With Landon Dickerson expected to go on injured reserve, the Eagles need a new starting left guard. Drew Kendall should and likely will be be the first man up. I know people love Willie Lampkin — and I’m one of them! — but he wasn’t taking first-team reps this summer. It was Kendall filling in at LG whenever Dickerson missed time. Kendall lacks a ton of experience at guard; he only played center in college. But he’s been learning the position since entering the NFL last year. I don’t like the idea of moving Cam Jurgens to left guard and changing two starting spots on the offensive line. How do you think the team should handle this situation? Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles to place guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, will miss at least four games – Inquirer Second-year offensive lineman Drew Kendall is expected to replace Dickerson, unless the Eagles decide on another configuration that could shift center Cam Jurgens to guard. Willie Lampkin is also in play for either job, although Kendall is the likely first interior lineman up. Kendall played center exclusively in college, while Jurgens’ first season as a starter in the NFL was at right guard. Jurgens also struggled against Washington on Sunday. Like Dickerson, he played through injury during the Super Bowl LIX run in 2025 and returned the following season following back surgery. He never looked 100%. Dickerson’s career, dating back to college, has been injury-plagued. He had multiple ACL tears, ankle surgeries, and other ailments during his time at Florida State and Alabama. The Eagles drafted him in the second round despite the medical red flags. He quickly became one of the NFL’s best interior linemen, though, and earned three straight Pro Bowl nods from 2022-24. But the injuries mounted, and while Dickerson missed only a handful of games in his first five seasons, it increasingly affected his performance. The Eagles’ changes to their offensive scheme this offseason were expected to affect Dickerson the most out of the starting five O-linemen. The wide-zone blocking requires more athletic and agile blockers. Eagles place Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, three thoughts on the move – PHLY Eagles I’d expect Drew Kendall to get the nod to start in Dickerson’s place this Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. Eagles general manager Howie Roseman offered a now-telling admission during a news conference last month closing out training camp that, if he’d been given truth serum going into the summer, he’d have said the interior offensive line depth was the thing he was most worried about. Kendall, along with training camp darling Willie Lampkin and sixth-round rookie Micah Morris, each had strong enough camps to quiet that worry for Roseman and Kendall seems the most ready to jump up the depth chart. “If any of you would’ve given me a truth serum and said, ‘What are you looking for in training camp?’ It would be how our interior offensive line depth panned out,” Roseman said. “Those young guys and the growth that they showed, their ability to play in the passing game, in the run game. I mean, really, really excited about those guys, about being able to have those guys, being able to develop those guys, but at the same time, have confidence that if those guys need to play, that they’re ready to play.” How will Eagles replace Landon Dickerson during his IR stint? – NBCSP Drew Kendall to center. Perhaps the loss of Dickerson will make the Eagles shuffle their line. Because Kendall is a more natural center, the Eagles could elect to plug him there and move Cam Jurgens to guard. Jurgens is a two-time Pro Bowl center but was a full-time starter at guard during the 2023 season. Former offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland normally tried to avoid shuffling the line like this because he thought it weakened them at two spots. But Stoutland isn’t their OL coach anymore and Chris Kuper might have different feelings on how to go about finding their best starting five. Landon Dickerson Update – Iggles Blitz This means Drew Kendall becomes the LG. Willie Lampkin is now the top backup interior OL. Jake Majors or John Ojukwu could be promoted from the practice squad for depth. Ojukwu has more experience. Both guys are good scheme fits. Rookie Micah Morris is talented, but I think he’s more of a long term solution than someone they would play right away. Howie Roseman talked this summer about how his big concern in the offseason was interior OL depth. The Eagles had several guys step up and perform well. Now comes the real test. I’m happy that Dickerson and the team took decisive action. If you know he’s not healthy, get him out of there. Give Kendall a chance to show what he can do. Is this the end of Dickerson’s career? It very well could be. Hopefully some time off will help him to heal and he can get back on the field one more time. No one wants to go out on a bad game. Landon Dickerson injury: Eagles guard headed to IR, admits he “was a complete liability” in Week 1 – BGN There were a lot of things to address coming out of the Philadelphia Eagles Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders, but arguably the biggest concern was starting left guard Landon Dickerson. Just one day later, the three-time Pro Bowler is expected to be heading to injured reserve, which means he will miss at least the next four games. NFC East Mixtape Vol. 189: Giants beat Cowboys, Eagles beat Washington – NFC East Mixtape The first week of the NFL season is just about over, and wow do we have some NFC East action to discuss! To start… the New York Giants actually did it. They announced that maybe this time finally is different as they completely dismantled the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. Earlier in the day, the Philadelphia Eagles withstood a rally from the Washington Commanders for more of the same as far as recent history is concerned. How are we feeling about all four teams as we move on into the actual season? RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! NFC Hierarchy/Obituary: Week 2 edition – PhillyVoice 5) Eagles (1-0): The Eagles’ defense kept the Commanders from doing much of anything until the fourth quarter, and Jalen Hurts made enough plays to win the Eagles the game, but 10 first downs was the second-fewest in the NFL Week 1, behind only the Broncos. The Titans had 11. The Dolphins had 13. Even the Browns had 15. And the Eagles played against one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Not good enough. Last week: 3. The Philadelphia Eagles changed offensive coordinators. Their second-half problem remains – The Athletic There were new schemes, new coaches, but ultimately a continuation of a year-old problem. Jalen Hurts’ second-half heroics allow new Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion to solve second-half stalls in the safety of the win column — much like his predecessor did until the stalls eventually did him in. The 2025 Eagles were the only team in coach Nick Sirianni’s tenure to finish a season with a negative second-half scoring margin (-7). The 2026 Eagles own a minus-3 second-half point differential after Week 1. Debuts offer some forgiveness. So do wins. Mannion, a first-time play caller, will look back on a mostly brutal 20-play sequence that portrayed the antithesis of the “aggressive”…

summary: Stout (adjective): Strong, thick Stout (noun): Legendary former Eagles offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland The Eagles’ offensive line struggled against the Commanders in Week 1, and after the game, Jordan Mailata was talking to reporters and might have had a bit of a Freudian slip. “I just think we need to be more stout. More […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PA - DECEMBER 14: Philadelphia Eagles offensive tackle Jordan Mailata (68) chats with Philadelphia Eagles coach Jeff Stoutland during the game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Philadelphia Eagles on December 14, 2025 at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, PA.(Photo by Andy Lewis/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Stout (adjective): Strong, thick Stout (noun): Legendary former Eagles offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland The Eagles’ offensive line struggled against the Commanders in Week 1, and after the game, Jordan Mailata was talking to reporters and might have had a bit of a Freudian slip. “I just think we need to be more stout. More stout on the runs up front. I think everything was — we should’ve been able to pick up everything.” Obviously this was an unintentional double entendre, because the group really does need to be more stout, the adjective. But, they probably could be more Stout, the noun, too, because this veteran offensive line knows better than to make some of the self-inflicting mistakes they did on Sunday. That’s not a knock on Chris Kuper, either, but the standard was set before the new OL coach got to Philly, and their performance in Week 1 didn’t live up to it. Whether the Eagles OL needs to be more stout, or more Stout, they certainly need to play with better fundamentals and do a better job protecting Jalen Hurts. We learned on Monday that Landon Dickerson is headed for IR as he deals with a bone bruise in his knee, so the group will need to step things up even more with Drew Kendall or Willie Lampkin stepping into that role.

title: Nick Sirianni explains why Eagles WR Hollywood Brown didn’t play Week 1
summary: The Eagles are 1-0 as the begin preparing for the Titans in Week 2, but head coach Nick Sirianni spoke with reporters on Monday after having a chance to watch Sunday’s film. He explained why Hollywood Brown didn’t play, and why they have to do better moving forward, as well as why Dallas Goedert is […]
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles answers questions during a press conference after a preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles are 1-0 as the begin preparing for the Titans in Week 2, but head coach Nick Sirianni spoke with reporters on Monday after having a chance to watch Sunday’s film. He explained why Hollywood Brown didn’t play, and why they have to do better moving forward, as well as why Dallas Goedert is so clutch, and what he saw from the running backs against Washington. When asked about certain individual performances, Sirianni kept coming back to this being the first game and everyone having things they need to improve. He spoke in support of Landon Dickerson following a rough performance, but shortly after the press conference, we learned the starting left guard was headed to IR . Here’s what the head coach had to say: On Hollywood Brown’s usage Sirianni said that they were rotating guys on Sunday, and while they know Brown could help them, it just didn’t work out. The head coach emphasized that they want to get the WR the ball because his speed is real, but there are some games in which players get shut out of catches, and some games that they get shut out of reps. “And quite frankly, just from my end, we want to get him in the football game. We’ll make a better effort to do that next time because I know the play making ability that he can bring with his speed but was pleased with how the wide outs played as a whole. Of course, there were things that you want back. They made a lot of plays down the field with different things with their job description. But I do want to see him in that football game and getting reps and contributing to this football team.” On Dallas Goedert’s ability Sirianni had a lot of positive things to say about Dallas Goedert, noting that the tight end has been so consistent throughout his time with the team. “He just has a knack to make plays. He’s been very solid in the run game; thought he was solid yesterday in that as well. I think Dallas has had different versions of his game shine at different times. What I mean by that is yesterday you got to see him catch the ball over the middle in space and get to the right spot, be a big target, make plays and finish. You’ve also seen through Dallas’ career how much of a dangerous runner he is when the ball is in his hands and how hard he is to bring down. You got to see that a little bit yesterday on the third down.” The head coach went on to talk about some of the more impressive moments from Goedert the past few years, highlighting some of his big sideline catches in critical playoff games. When the TE has to win one-on-one matchups, he’s able to do it in various ways on various routes, including some outside receiver routes and particularly in the red zone. Sirianni was sure to point out that Goedert’s success is not a surprise because he works his butt off to take his game to the next level. “He’s a great teammate. He’s consistent. Guys love being around him, so it was good to see him have a good game yesterday. I was pumped for him, and obviously all the things he did to help our football team win last night.” On the RB group Sirianni disregarded the notion that Saquon Barkley’s 42-yard run was just an outlier compared to the rest of the performance, and insisted that the explosive play count just as much as the other ones. “Being committed to the run game, sometimes that’s the way it goes. Not every play can be an explosive play in the run game. You want to make sure you’re staying ahead of the sticks. Now, that doesn’t mean that we ignore the issues that happened on those plays that averaged whatever. Some of them were negative plays, some of them were one-yard gains, some of them were six-yard gains. We’ll take those six-yard gains, but those plays count. When you’re committed to the run game like we are, you reap the benefits of that when you stick with it.” The head coach also talked about Will Shipley being on the field in some critical moments. He explained that sometimes in third-down they don’t want to sub out a guy if they’re trying to go tempo. “I think the best way to say, ‘Hey, why did Will Shipley get carries in those situations?’ Because we trust our backs. We trust every one of those guys. They’ve all shown to be able to make plays in different aspects. Obviously, Saquon’s our lead guy, as you guys know, and we’re really comfortable when Tank [Bigsby] and Will are in there and they’re getting carries and they’re getting protections. We’ve got a lot of faith in that group, and we’ll continue to have faith in that group because they continue to show us the things that they can do on a consistent basis.” On Jalen Hurts’ development “He made plays that only Jalen Hurts is capable of making at times across the entire league. With some of those new things that we were doing, I thought he did a nice job. Now, not a surprise to me. I was talking to somebody – we had 46 days or 47 days in training camp to get ready for that first game. We’re seeing that on a daily basis, that improvement.” He also admitted that they wouldn’t have put in some of the different things they did on Sunday if they didn’t think Hurts could execute at a very high level. On Makai Lemon’s debut “[Makai Lemon has] always done a good job since he’s been here of blocking, doing the right things, being in the right spots. Obviously, the ones that went to him yesterday didn’t equal out to be big yardage gains, but he did little things to help us win the football game that sometimes are unseen and unnoticed. Why that’s really important is while a young player is continuing to get used to the NFL and being able to make an impact, you have to trust that player. We trust him because he’s constantly doing the things without the ball that we need to help us win and that we know is going to help us win. That just builds confidence and allows players to develop, because I’ve been on the other side of that where maybe you didn’t trust the guy and you didn’t want to put him in there and then it was hard to get that guy going. So because of that trust we have in him, I think that’s going to help him continue to develop as a football player as we continue on through the season.”

summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are exploring another option along their offensive line, bringing in veteran offensive tackle Charlie Heck for a tryout Tuesday. Heck, 28, spent the 2026 preseason with the Miami Dolphins […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - DECEMBER 18: Charlie Heck #67 of the Houston Texans get set against the Kansas City Chiefs at NRG Stadium on December 18, 2022 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are exploring another option along their offensive line, bringing in veteran offensive tackle Charlie Heck for a tryout Tuesday. According to Steelers insider Alan Saunders , the Steelers tried out Heck, a former fourth-round pick of the Houston Texans out of North Carolina. Heck, 28, spent the 2026 preseason with the Miami Dolphins before becoming available on the open market. He originally entered the NFL as a fourth-round selection by Houston in the 2020 NFL Draft. The 6-foot-8, 310-pound tackle has appeared in 51 regular-season games during his NFL career, including 27 starts. His experience comes primarily at offensive tackle, giving Pittsburgh another veteran option as it continues to evaluate the depth of its offensive line. The Steelers also hosted tackle Austin Deculus, a 2022 sixth-round pick by Houston, for a tryout, according to KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson . Deculus has six career starts and has appeared in 26 career games. The Steelers have already made significant changes up front this offseason, with new head coach Mike McCarthy installing a different offensive system. Pittsburgh’s transition from Arthur Smith’s wide-zone approach to McCarthy’s more traditional pro-style, gap-oriented scheme has placed additional emphasis on finding players who fit the new system. Heck and Deculus’ workouts do not necessarily mean the Steelers will sign them, but it signals that the team is continuing to examine available veteran options at tackle.

summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers started the Mike McCarthy era on a high note by defeating the Atlanta Falcons at home Sunday afternoon, 20-13. full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Pat Freiermuth #88 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers started the Mike McCarthy era on a high note by defeating the Atlanta Falcons at home Sunday afternoon, 20-13. After a shaky start, it was the Steelers’ defense that stole the show and propelled the team to victory. That included a pick-six from TJ Watt, who looked fresh and revitalized under this new coaching staff. It’s time for our weekly look around the web to see where the Steelers fall in this week’s power rankings. FOX Sports: No. 16 (No. 20 Last Week) “Aaron Rodgers was OK, not great, but he didn’t need to do a lot thanks to a defense that was stifling against a battered Falcons team playing its third-string QB.” – Ralph Vacchiano The Athletic: No. 16 (Last Week No.18) “Yes, the Steelers have a new coach, but this team looked much like it has in recent years. The defense was pretty good. The offense was mostly fine. It’s rarely worth putting too much stock into Week 1, but this Mike McCarthy-led squad looks like another roughly .500 team. We should learn more about the Steelers in Week 2 during their trip to New England.” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall CBS Sports: No.20 (Last Week No. 20) “They beat the Falcons, but it wasn’t pretty. They have to do more on offense, starting this week against the Patriots.” – Pete Prisco Pro Football Talk: No. 17 (Last Week No. 18) “For the second time in three years, T.J. Watt personally delivered a win over the Falcons in Week 1.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No. 23 (Last Week No.21) “Mike McCarthy’s debut as Steelers coach didn’t come with the explosive offense that was his trademark at prior NFL stops. Aaron Rodgers played with more freedom and aggression than he did last season, but the unit struggled to produce points against the Falcons. None of that matters all that much, though, when T.J. Watt is intercepting passes and turning them into defensive touchdowns.” – Nick Shook Yahoo! Sports: No. 20 (Last Week No. 20) “The Steelers got a win but it wasn’t pretty. Facing a Falcons team down to its third quarterback, the Steelers led by just three points in the fourth quarter before T.J. Watt had an interception return for a touchdown. Particularly troubling was the offense, which had the worst success rate in the NFL for Week 1. The run game really struggled, with 2.8 yards per carry. And that’s against a Falcons defense that wasn’t projected to be very good.“ – Frank Schwab USA Today: No. 20 (Last Week No.21) “OLB T.J. Watt appeared revived Sunday after a subpar 2025 season. He (and Joey Porter?) also looked like a player who might be a tremendous target at this season’s trade deadline.” – Nate Davis ESPN: No. 21 (Last Week No. 21) “Even with Falcons do-everything back Bijan Robinson racking up 173 scrimmage yards, it’s hard to point to anyone other than Graham. The Steelers’ pass rush dominated third-string quarterback Cooper Rush, and the buy-in from the Steelers’ veterans was evident. T.J. Watt, who admitted he was stubborn about the idea of moving around in the old scheme, did just that Sunday. Not only did Watt have a pick-six, but he also recorded a sack from each side of the D-line. title: The Seahawks have turned the turnover battle around during 11-game win streak
summary: When the Seattle Seahawks won Super Bowl 60, they became only the 10th team to end the regular season with a negative turnover differential but still hoist the Lombardi Trophy. According to Stathead, no team has ever won more games in a season despite a minus in the turnover column than the 2025 Seahawks. But […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 9: Nehemiah Pritchett #28 of the Seattle Seahawks intercepts a pass during the fourth quarter of an NFL football game against the New England Patriots at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images When the Seattle Seahawks won Super Bowl 60, they became only the 10th team to end the regular season with a negative turnover differential but still hoist the Lombardi Trophy. According to Stathead , no team has ever won more games in a season despite a minus in the turnover column than the 2025 Seahawks. But that’s only part of the story when it comes to Seattle’s tale of two halves. Including last season’s playoffs, the Seahawks have won 11 straight games, tying a franchise record. Outside of their thrilling regular season win over the Los Angeles Rams, they have dominated in the turnover department. Compare that to the preceding 11 games, in which they were still 8-3, and it’s easy to see how the Seahawks have tilted close games in their favor and turned competitive games into blowouts. Seattle Seahawks turnover splits Seattle’s last 22 games Giveaways Takeaways Turnover differential Points off turnovers differential First 11 games of 2025 season 20 13 -7 -28 Current 11-game winning streak 8 22 +14 +86 That’s right. The Seahawks have kept the turnovers down, driven the takeaways up, and they’re scoring off of those takeaways at a very high clip. When they have turned it over during their win streak, they’ve allowed only 10 points off those eight giveaways. The only touchdown off a Seahawks turnover was in the second Rams game, and that was literally a 1-yard drive after a Sam Darnold interception. Of the Seahawks’ 22 takeaways on defense and special teams, 16 have resulted in at least a field goal, including 12 touchdowns. During Seattle’s 8-3 start last season, the losses to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Los Angeles Rams were more or less a story of untimely and costly turnovers. The Buccaneers recovered a Jalen Milroe fumble and scored a touchdown on the ensuing drive, and picked off Sam Darnold late for the winning field goal. Seattle didn’t come remotely close to forcing a turnover. Against the Rams, Darnold threw four interceptions, two of which led to touchdowns, while Seattle’s takeaway off of a Puka Nacua fumble only led to a field goal. That’s -21 points in the points off turnover column in games lost by a combined five points. Even the eight-point win over the Houston Texans could’ve been a blowout if not for a -3 turnover differential, including Darnold losing a fumble in the end zone for a touchdown. In the somewhat sputtering portion of their current 11-game winning streak, the Seahawks have repeatedly come up with turnovers to generate points. Against the Minnesota Vikings, 17 of their 26 points were off Vikings giveaways (mostly off poor Max Brosmer). After a lackluster first half versus the Atlanta Falcons, the Seahawks turned the screws and turned a 6-6 halftime score into a 37-9 blowout in large part to a trio of turnovers, which led to 17 points. Likewise versus the Carolina Panthers, they quickly turned a 3-3 third quarter score into 17-3 thanks to short fields set up by a pair of Carolina turnovers. In the nail-biter of an NFC Championship Game versus the Rams, Xavier Smith’s muffed punt gifted Seattle a short field and a Jake Bobo touchdown, which gave the Seahawks an 11-point lead and essentially provided enough cushion for the Seahawks to hang on for the win. Fast foward to the opening night win over the Patriots, the Jaxon Smith-Njigba tying touchdown is likely not possible without the Nehemiah Pritchett tip-drill interception. Julian Love’s pick off of Drake Maye gave Seattle a short field to kick the (ultimately) game-winning field goal. The final interception by Josh Jobe didn’t need anything other than a subsequent victory formation kneel. JOSH JOBE TOE TAP INT NEvsSEA on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/MrmQx0a3fo — NFL (@NFL) September 10, 2026 And, of course, sometimes the defense does the scoring to seal a Super Bowl victory. PUNCHED OUT BY SPOON. CHENNA TO THE HOUSE. 📺: @SNFonNBC pic.twitter.com/32dYC8vWqN — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) February 9, 2026 After being a significant net negative in turnovers through the first 28 games under Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald, Seattle has found a way to take better care of the ball, while the league’s best defense has turned the screws to “see ball, get ball,” and keep the good times rolling.

title: Seahawks Week 2 power rankings: Seahawks stay on top, Rams slip from national glory
summary: Entering the 2026 season, the national media has been very high on the Seattle Seahawks. This is not surprising as the team just won the Super Bowl, and in a dominant way. Across the NFL landscape, the consensus top two teams appeared to be the Seahawks and their division rival, Los Angeles Rams. However, will […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - SEPTEMBER 09: Jaxon Smith-Njigba #11 of the Seattle Seahawks runs the ball to score a 45 yard touchdown against Kevin Byard #31 of the New England Patriots during the fourth quarter in the game at Lumen Field on September 09, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Steph Chambers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Entering the 2026 season, the national media has been very high on the Seattle Seahawks. This is not surprising as the team just won the Super Bowl, and in a dominant way. Across the NFL landscape, the consensus top two teams appeared to be the Seahawks and their division rival, Los Angeles Rams. However, will the national media keep the Seahawks in a top position with their win over the New England Patriots? Or will the loss of Sam Darnold to a glute injury show them slip in the rankings? Let’s take a look at five national media sites power rankings ( NFL.com , CBS Sports, Bleacher Report (B/R), Pro Football Talk (PFT), and ESPN) to see where they rank Seattle. Starting with the bad news … if you can call it bad. ESPN ranks the Seahawks at number two in the NFL , keeping the same ranking they had entering the season. In this ranking ESPN notes that rookie running back Jadarian Price had a solid debut, while also giving a shoutout to safety, Rodney Thomas II who played for an injured Ty Okada. The only team ranked above Seattle was the Buffalo Bills. Entering the season, both CBS Sports and PFT had the Seahawks ranked as the number one team in the league. Their win over the Patriots did not change this. In their ranking, CBS Sports shows optimism that Seattle can keep winning with backup quarterback, Drew Lock at the helm. On the opposite end of the spectrum, despite keeping the Seahawks ranked at number one, PFT does question how long the team can keep winning with Drew Lock at the helm . Neither NFL.com nor B/R had the Seahawks ranked number one entering the 2026 season. However, after the week one victory over the Patriots, both have moved Seattle into the top spot. The biggest jump was with NFL.com , who originally had the Seahawks ranked number three entering the season. In this week’s ranking, NFL.com moved them up to number one on the list, and highlighted the team’s big second half comeback, led by three fourth-quarter takeaways, and a signature Jaxon Smith-Njigba touchdown . B/R on the other hand moved the Seahawks up from second to first . In this ranking, B/R notes that this team’s victory with Drew Lock at quarterback shows just how dominant of a team they are. An added note that B/R made was that the “Seahawks should’ve been No.1 to start out power rankings.” The team that Seattle took the top spot away from? The Los Angeles Rams – who have now fallen to sixth in BR’s rankings. I know this is a Seahawks power rankings roundup. However, it is sweet to see the Rams fall from national grace. It isn’t just BR who dropped the Rams down a lot in their rankings. ESPN also had the Rams falling from first entering the season to being ranked fourth. NFL.com dropped the Rams from first to seventh. CBS Sports dropped the Rams from second to fifth. And lastly, PFT had the Rams drop all the way from second to 11th. Overall, the Seahawks have to be feeling good after pulling off that come from behind victory with a backup quarterback, first time play-caller, and with it all being week one of the season (and banner night of all nights). The national media feels good about the team as well. Entering the season the average power ranking between the five polled sites was 1.8. This week the average power ranking between the five sites is 1.2. Although it is small, this still shows an upward trend. Despite going into next week with backup, Drew Lock, the Seahawks are still likely going to be favorites against the Arizona Cardinals. However, this is the NFL, and if Seattle is caught slipping, they may very well see a similar fall in rankings as the Rams did this past week.
