title: With Sam Darnold out, who could the Seahawks look to sign as a third quarterback?
summary: With Sam Darnold dealing with a glute injury that will likely sideline him for the “short-term”, the Seattle Seahawks may not need to go looking for other starting quarterback options. However, there have been reports that Darnold may be out a little longer. One report from Mike Florio even mentioned that Darnold could be out […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - NOVEMBER 17: Jake Browning #3 of the Washington Huskies runs with the ball in the first quarter against the Oregon State Beavers during their game at Husky Stadium on November 17, 2018 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Abbie Parr/Getty Images) | Getty Images With Sam Darnold dealing with a glute injury that will likely sideline him for the “short-term” , the Seattle Seahawks may not need to go looking for other starting quarterback options. However, there have been reports that Darnold may be out a little longer. One report from Mike Florio even mentioned that Darnold could be out 4-6 weeks . Regardless of the timeline, Seattle looks to only have two healthy quarterbacks for the time being. That raises the question of whether the Seahawks should look for other quarterback options, not necessarily to start – Drew Lock is likely your best bet there – but rather to add depth to the room. Counting the practice squad, John Schneider has often had three quarterbacks in the room. The third quarterback was usually your practice squad type (Alex McGough, Brett Rypien, Jaren Hall, Holton Ahlers, Sean Mannion, John Rhys Plumlee). More recently the third quarterback, Jalen Milroe, has had to be rostered due to the likelihood of him being plucked off waivers if waived. Now, with Darnold’s injury, could Schneider look to add another quarterback for temporary depth to the room? Perhaps another quarterback could come in and be Drew Lock’s primary backup, in case the Seahawks are not comfortable with Milroe being one snap away from taking legitimate NFL quarterbacks snaps in a game. With that, let’s take a look at a few options the Seahawks could look at for the quarterback position. Jake Retzlaff This first name may not look familiar to many fans, unless you were watching lots of AAC college football over the years. Retzlaff, an undrafted rookie out of Tulane was the biggest quarterback name that was at the Seahawks 2026 Rookie Minicamp . The tryout did not end up in a contract for Retzlaff. However, Seattle often will keep their eyes on the tryout players before bringing them back later in the season if injuries or other circumstances necessitate it. In his final college season at Tulane, Retzlaff completed 61% of his passes his final year at Tulane, throwing for 3,168 yards, 15 touchdowns and 7 interceptions . However, Retzlaff is also a dual threat quarterback, rushing for 634 yards and 16 touchdowns that final season alone. Retzlaff could potentially be a third quarterback option behind Milroe if Seattle feels the need to have another quarterback in the room. Josh Johnson The complete opposite of an undrafted rookie free agent, is Josh Johnson. Johnson is a 19-year NFL veteran quarterback who has played for seemingly half of the NFL, played in the United Football League, the XFL, and was even the first overall pick in the now defunct Alliance of American Football League . One team he has not played for however – the Seahawks. Adding Johnson would be like adding another coach to the quarterback room. Johnson throughout his career has been a backup or third string quarterback who only went into games in emergency situations – remember the 2022 NFC Championship game where Brock Purdy got hurt? Johnson was the quarterback who played in relief of Purdy . More recently Johnson started two games for the Washington Commanders in 2025. In those two games, he completed 63% of his passes, throwing for 372 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions . Johnson is currently on the Cincinnati Bengals practice squad. Meaning the Seahawks would have to sign him to the 53-man roster to get him to the team. The Seahawks making a move like this would be a sign that Darnold’s injury may be longer term than originally thought. However, Johnson would not be a bad veteran option to help backup Lock and potentially Milroe as well. An added fun fact – Johnson is first cousins, and close childhood friends with Marshawn Lynch . Jake Browning A more familiar name to those in the Pacific Northwest is former Washington Huskies quarterback, Jake Browning. Browning signed with the Minnesota Vikings as an undrafted free agent in 2019. His first real game action did not come until 2023 with the Bengals. Browning started seven games that season in place of injured Joe Burrow, going 4-3 during that time. Browning impressed in his limited time. He completed 70.4% of his passes, throwing for 1,936 yards, 12 touchdowns and 7 interceptions . However, since then Browning has not been able to replicate the 2023 season. Last season when Burrow got hurt again, Browning struggled mightily. This led to the Bengals trading for Joe Flacco, positioning Browning on the outs with the organization. Browning signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this offseason, however did not make the roster and is currently a free agent. The Seahawks could look to bring Browning back to the pacific northwest on the practice squad. Despite a lackluster last few years, Browning has real game experience and could be a backup option to Lock if the team is not comfortable with Milroe starting just yet. Brandon Allen One last free agent that could be an option is Brandon Allen, another longtime backup quarterback. However, Allen has one thing the other options above do not. He has worked with Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury in the past. Along with his many NFL stops, Allen was with the San Francisco 49ers in 2023 and 2024. Although Fleury was the tight ends coach with the 49ers at this time, the two surely are familiar with each other more so than others on this list. Allen is currently in his eleventh season in the NFL, but has only started ten games during that time. His most recent start came in 2024 with Fleury and the 49ers. In that game, Allen completed 56.7% of his passes, throwing for 199 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions . More recently, Allen spent 2025 with the Tennessee Titans before signing with the New York Giants this offseason. Allen was cut by the Giants during final roster cuts and is currently free to sign with anyone. Of the options above, there clearly are not that many that create much excitement. Unless Seattle looks to trade for a backup option (Tanner McKee, Anthony Richardson, etc), these are the options the team is left with. The best news the team can have is that Darnold will be back sooner than later, and that any quarterback they need to bring in (if any) are simply for depth, and not with the goal of them playing any meaningful snaps.

title: 49ers considered favorites to win NFC West after Week 1
summary: Through one week, the NFC West is 3-1, with the lone loss being the Los Angeles Rams, who fell to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. While the spread was 3.5-points, not many had faith in the 49ers, myself included, after the Rams added a ton of star talent in the offseason, making them the […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Deebo Samuel Sr. #19 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates scoring a touchdown in the fourth quarter of the NFL football game against Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images Through one week, the NFC West is 3-1, with the lone loss being the Los Angeles Rams, who fell to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. While the spread was 3.5-points, not many had faith in the 49ers, myself included, after the Rams added a ton of star talent in the offseason, making them the odds-on favorites to win the Super Bowl. With the Super Bowl-winning Seattle Seahawks still around with their nucleus of players, they were also considered above the 49ers for both the NFC West and the Super Bowl. But things have quickly shifted after Week 1, when the 49ers beat the Rams 27-7 and showed the potential of what their team can do when healthy. According to ESPN, the 49ers have jumped from third to first in NFC West odds, climbing up to +160 odds to win the division. The Seahawks are shortly behind at +175, and the Rams, who were hovering around +100 to begin the season, are now third at +205 odds. However, that hasn’t changed the big-picture outlook as much. ESPN still has the Rams as the odds-on favorites to win the Super Bowl at +650, while the 49ers are tied for the fifth-best odds with the Kansas City Chiefs at +1400. Ahead of them are the Baltimore Ravens (+900), Buffalo Bills (+950), and Seattle Seahawks (+1100). It’s interesting that oddsmakers don’t see the Rams as the NFC West division winner, but they do still have them as the favorite to win the Super Bowl. The 49ers, however, do have better odds to win the NFC than the Seahawks. Los Angeles is seen as the favorite to make the Super Bowl out of the NFC at +455, while the 49ers jump up to second with +550 odds. The Seahawks are shortly behind at +580, while the Philadelphia Eagles (+710) and Chicago Bears (+800) round out the top five. There have been some early injuries shifting the tune in the NFC West. Los Angeles will be without star pass rusher Myles Garrett for at least the next month after placing him on Injured Reserve. Of course, Aaron Donald has yet to play as well. Sam Darnold is dealing with a hip injury and will also be out, making Drew Lock the starter for the upcoming weeks. The 49ers have dealt with their mass of injuries already, with players like Ricky Pearsall and Alfred Collins set to miss the season, but their core group of stars was all healthy for Week 1. San Francisco will first face the Seahawks on the road in Week 5 after three straight home games against the Miami Dolphins, Arizona Cardinals, and Denver Broncos. That could be the next major game that shifts the division odds one way or another, and could also be around when Sam Darnold returns.

title: 49ers News: Welcome to the Bay, McKinnley Jackson!
summary: The Miami Dolphins are begging to be overlooked. A trap game this early sounds insane, I know, but after coming back from such a long flight and an emotional win… going against an opponent that doesn’t seem like much… let’s not forget that the Dolphins are still an NFL team. The 49ers are going against […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX-DECEMBER 9: McKinnley Jackson #93 of the Cincinnati Bengals looks on during the game at AT&T Stadium on December 9, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are begging to be overlooked. A trap game this early sounds insane, I know, but after coming back from such a long flight and an emotional win… going against an opponent that doesn’t seem like much… let’s not forget that the Dolphins are still an NFL team. The 49ers are going against a young, hungry, mobile QB-led team with nothing to lose and everything to gain from embarrassing the 49ers. They started rallying on the Raiders before the Raiders put them away. WR Caleb Douglas seems like the real deal, so the 49ers secondary can’t be coasting just because they shut down Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Everybody better lock in at practice today. 49ers Week 1 Tape Takeaways: Motion commotion (paywall) “The 49ers looked coordinated in the run game. They went back to their zone-heavy roots, and I wonder if leaning on Dash helped simplify things. It made things easier for the offensive line and made every run look the same (sometimes they were). San Francisco consistently attacked the Rams’ weak linebacker corps. The coordination on help blocks and second-level climbs was outstanding. Colby looked weak at times, and allowed a team-high six run stops (my measure), but he also had great moments. This is, at this moment, a legitimately good offensive line. A healthy Trent Williams and Dom Puni make a massive difference…The 49ers didn’t really go to dime looks until the fourth quarter, once the Rams had all but abandoned their run game and 13 personnel looks. I love it. Raheem Morris used the 49ers’ best DBs, letting Deommodore Lenoir thrive in that Star/Jackal/Apex/positionless position that’s really just a second nickel. We’ll see how much they lean on dime going forward, but I’d be stunned if this was a one-off experiment. It was too effective….Also, I enjoyed how effective the 49ers were at running stunts. They were far cleaner than in the past. It created a lot of effective disruption, and helped limit some of the wear and tear Nick Bosa would face with head-up rushes….Lastly, George Kittle. He doesn’t look near where he was last year before his injury and I wouldn’t expect him to. I say that while also noting that he had some nice blocks on the move. But he can’t really power off his surgically-repaired right leg.” 49ers mailbag: What’s next after De’Zhaun Stribling’s and Alfred Collins’ injuries? (Paywall) “But I still think the bigger need is at defensive end. Though Mykel Williams is technically a defensive end, he’ll be able to play a lot of defensive tackle snaps — especially on obvious passing downs — when he’s back after Week 4. The same goes for Keion White. There are also a lot more quality defensive ends available, a list that includes Haason Reddick, Leonard Floyd and Joey Bosa. Here’s how I’d classify them: If the team wants another Romello Height-like player or is worried it’s not getting enough out of Height, Reddick would be a good solution. He’s a lighter-bodied edge player who’s played in systems similar to the one defensive coordinator Raheem Morris is running this year. If the team wants a dependable, every-down defensive end, Floyd is the answer. He’s familiar to both the 49ers’ brass and Morris. Yes, Floyd turned 34 last week and had only 3.5 sacks last year for Morris’ Falcons. But the 49ers aren’t in a position to look down their noses at 3.5 sacks. Their sack leader last year had four. If the 49ers want a second-half-of-the-season boost, how about Bosa? The team might be worried about how Nick Bosa’s oft-injured older brother might hold up over a 17-game season. But an eight-game season seems reasonable. Joey had five sacks and 54 quarterback pressures for the Bills last year. That’s not elite, but it’s better than what the 49ers have opposite Nick at the moment. Another interesting option is Yetur Gross-Matos, whose recent stint with the 49ers was marred by a knee issue. Gross-Matos didn’t play or practice much, but when he was on the field, he made an impact. His 16.3 percent pass-rush win rate last season was second best on the team behind Bosa’s 20 percent rate. Gross-Matos is currently rehabilitating from that knee injury and isn’t ready to play. That could change by midseason.” Will 49ers’ De’Zhaun Stribling need an ankle procedure? Surgeons explain factors at play (paywall) “To be clear, most deltoid ligament sprains heal on their own. And that could be the case with Stribling. But the nature of the injury is why athletes are sidelined for at least a month — with some recoveries requiring up to six weeks — if surgery isn’t required. Jung and Dr. Nicholas Strasser, a foot and ankle surgeon who is consultant to the Tennessee Titans and Vanderbilt University, explained that the deltoid ligament is a stronger ligament than the two on the outside of the ankle that are associated with low and high ankle sprains. As a result, it requires more force to damage the deltoid. And more force means more trauma to the ankle. …Jung said Stribling would have already had a procedure if he had “gross instability,” but it’s likely premature to say whether rest and rehabilitation will restore whatever instability Stribling is experiencing. Stribling’s stability will be determined by how the fibers in his torn ankle heal. “If they heal a little bit stretched out, or in a way that it just doesn’t have enough support to it, that could lead to surgery,” said Strasser, an assistant professor of orthopedics at Vanderbilt. “Especially because it’s on the inside part of the ankle and you’re often cutting and pushing off that a little bit more. The stress in that area is a little bit more extreme.” If Stribling needs surgery, his recovery would last three to four months, which would sideline him for most or all of the regular season.” 49ers overreactions: Will 2026 NFL season be a touchdown frenzy for Brock Purdy? “Mike Evans and George Kittle are the most-likely players to have 10 or more touchdown catches. Christian McCaffrey and Deebo Samuel are candidates to team up with Purdy for a lot of scoring receptions, too.” 49ers find needed balance in run game with McCaffrey, Black “From midfield, Brendel turned toward coach Kyle Shanahan on the sideline and waved his arms to suggest he wanted to run the ball, run it again and keep running it until the Rams showed they could at least slow it down. “After a few of those good chunk run plays hit, I’m looking right at Kyle, ‘Let’s go,'” Brendel said. “Let’s just keep going. Let’s keep dialing them up.” Shanahan apparently agreed with Brendel’s assessment. The success of those plays only yielded more runs, and by the end of San Francisco’s 27-7 win, it had 30 attempts for a robust 5.8 yards per rush….San Francisco also took advantage of a schematic curveball from the Rams. According to Brendel, the Niners spent the week preparing for plenty of five-man fronts — similar to what Los Angeles threw at them in recent matchups. Brendel was surprised when the Rams not only played four down linemen more frequently but were also often in nickel packages (five defensive backs). “The way that they chose to play us on defense schematically we weren’t really expecting,” Brendel said. “Most teams are a little bit more scared of our wide zone and our run game.” 49ers’ Renardo Green credits experience for his big interception vs. Rams “I knew the way I played it, I knew he (Stafford) didn’t see me, and even if he did, he didn’t think I could get to it,” Green told NBC Sports Bay Area. “He underestimated my abilities and what I could do, and he paid for it. I sunk under it and made a play on the ball….“Once I made it, I was thinking I’m only as good as my next play,” Green said of his mindset after the interception. “So I just moved on. I didn’t get too high. I don’t even know what it looked like. I…

full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers hosted five players for a tryout after tight end Jake Tonges and defensive tackle Alfred Collins suffered injuries. The team already added a defensive tackle to the practice squad on Tuesday . Here are the three tight ends and a pair of defensive tackles the team worked out: TE Lawrence Cager (6’5”, 220) TE Tanner Conner (6’3”, 232) TE Jack Stoll (6’4”, 247) DT Larry Ogunjobi DT Daniel Ekuale Cager, 29, has been in the NFL since 2020, but he hasn’t played a regular-season game since 2023. He spent his NFL tenure with the Jets and the Giants. His most productive season came in 2022, when he caught 13 passes for 118 yards. Conner went undrafted in the 2022 draft. He spent his rookie contract with the Dolphins. Last season, Conner caught nine passes for 91 yards with the Dolphins. Stoll played for the Eagles from 2021 through 2024. He started four games last season with the Saints, catching six passes for 46 yards. During his career, Stoll has 32 starts. At his size and with his experience, Stoll probably has the best shot to make the roster. Kyle’s update, 3:53 p.m. PT: The 49ers signed Stoll to the practice squad, per Mike Garafolo . Ogunjobi is a name just about everybody should know. He’s been in the NFL since 2017. The 32-year-old most recently played for the Bills in 2025. Ogunjobi, 6’3″, 305 pounds, had five tackles for loss last season. If the 32-year-old has anything left in the tank, the Niners will bring him in. Ekuale, 6’3″, 300 pounds, is also 32. His experience pales in comparison to Ogunjobi’s. Ekuale started 16 games for the Patriots in 2024. He has not started more than four games in any other season since entering the NFL in 2019. Ekuale was with the Steelers last year.

full_text: Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers announced they have promoted tight end Brayden Willis to the active roster. He is expected to replace Jake Tonges. Needing an Alfred Collins replacement, the team signed defensive tackle McKinnley Jackson to the practice squad. Jackson, listed at 6’2”, 330 pounds, was drafted by the Bengals in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft. He’s appeared in 22 games, including nine a season ago. This is unlikely to be the last move the 49ers make before returning to practice Wednesday, as the team will likely place De’Zhaun Stribling on Injured Reserve and decide what to do with Tonges’s roster spot. As for Jackson, he came on late in the preseason for the Bengals, but was unlikely to crack their 2-deep. Jackson flashed toward the end of his rookie season for the Bengals, recording a tackle for loss in three of the final four games, as well as a sack. He didn’t generate much pressure, but that’s to be expected of a player of that stature. The 49ers are looking for a defensive tackle who can hold their ground against the run. Jackson has the size to do it.

title: 3 final numbers to take away from the 49ers’ win over the Rams
summary: The San Francisco 49ers started the year off with a convincing win over the Los Angeles Rams last Thursday and have their sights set on a 2-0 start with a win over the Miami Dolphins at Levi’s Stadium on Sunday afternoon. Week 1 games can set the tone for a season or be a full-on […]
full_text: (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers started the year off with a convincing win over the Los Angeles Rams last Thursday and have their sights set on a 2-0 start with a win over the Miami Dolphins at Levi’s Stadium on Sunday afternoon. Week 1 games can set the tone for a season or be a full-on mirage. Deciphering which trends mean something and which can go out the window is an interesting exercise. No matter where you land on the debate, the one thing you always want to be after Week 1 is 1-0. Here are three final numbers to consider from Thursday night’s win: Are the 49ers shifting to more under center formations? According to SumerSports, under center in the NFL saw a sizable increase from 2025 in Week 1, with a 42% UC rate versus 29.2% in 2025. The result? A 32.2% dropback rate from under center is a big jump from 14.6% in 2025, and the UC EPA/DB is up to 0.149, up from 0.103 in 2025. As far as the 49ers go, the offense was under center 57.8% of the time, which is good for 0.20 UC/EPA. Overall, the 49ers’ offensive success rate was 56.2%, rising to 58.3% in late. The 58.3% matches the 49ers’ success rate on dropbacks. The overall offensive EPA sits at 0.17, but the real development could be playing more under center. The 49ers pressure packages The 49ers finished without a sack, but the pass rush and blitz packages were felt on Thursday night. With 14 pressures, seven hurries, and seven QB hits, the 49ers got pressure on 37.5% of the Rams’ dropbacks. Nick Bosa returned and was excellent, but the additions of Osa Odighizuwa and Raheem Morris as defensive coordinator paid instant dividends for a pass rush that was non-existent last season. Predicting a better pass rush wasn’t bold given how poor it was last year, but the sacks will come, and as long as the team continues to disrupt at this level, there will be plenty to go around for the 49ers defensive line. The 49ers offensive line success continues? Speaking of no sacks allowed, the 49ers offensive line was great and allowed pressures on 25% of Purdy’s dropbacks. In fact, the Rams generated “quick pressure” on only 5.7% of the 49ers’ dropbacks. A game plan mixed with quick throws helps, but the offensive line was dominant at times and gave the Rams’ defensive line fits. Here’s to this continuing and finding out whether the Rams’ defensive line was gassed and Myles Garrett was injured, or if the offensive line is taking a stride forward as pass protectors.

title: How 8 former 49ers fared in their Week 1 debuts with their new teams
summary: None of the San Francisco 49ers from a year ago signed lucrative deals like in years past. In fact, most are role players, with only a couple of starters. Still, we’ll track how former 49ers performed throughout the year. There’s no better week to do it than Week 1, when overreactions are rampant. Jauan Jennings […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 13: Kendrick Bourne #17 of the Arizona Cardinals warms up before kickoff against the Los Angeles Chargers during an NFL football game at SoFi Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images None of the San Francisco 49ers from a year ago signed lucrative deals like in years past. In fact, most are role players, with only a couple of starters. Still, we’ll track how former 49ers performed throughout the year. There’s no better week to do it than Week 1, when overreactions are rampant. Jauan Jennings Jennings played 27 passing snaps in his Vikings debut. He was only targeted once across 19 routes. The target came 30 yards downfield. In terms of usage, Jennings ran 68.4% of his routes from the slot. Jennings’ presence was felt in the running game: New Vikings WR Jauan Jennings (14) had 0 catches Sunday on 1 target, but he showed the blocking skills coaches have been talking about on Aaron Jones' TD run. Picture perfect seal of Packers DE Barryn Sorrell (99). pic.twitter.com/fSl6q2qORa — Kevin Seifert (@SeifertESPN) September 14, 2026 Kendrick Bourne Bourne was heavily involved in the Cardinals’ passing attack. Bourne had a higher target share than Mike Evans. He caught all eight targets for 75 yards and had three impact plays, but his average depth of target was five yards. He totaled 40 air yards. He did hold onto his one contested catch and consistently moved the chains for Arizona. Bourne felt like Jacoby Brissett’s security blanket, being in the right place at the right time for his quarterback. Good for Bourne. Spencer Burford Burford starts at left guard for the Raiders. Burford allowed four pressures in 31 pass-blocking snaps. But that makes it sound like he had a bad game, and he didn’t. I watched most of that game, and the Raiders were running wild against the Dolphins. They had 10 rushes for 65 yards behind Burford. He had one clip where he pancaked his defender after moving him a gap over. Remember, it’s essentially Burford’s second season playing the position. I’ll be rooting for him. Brian Robinson Robinson played 18 snaps in his Falcons debut. He’s also Atlanta’s kickoff returner. Robinson returned a kick for 40 yards to begin the third quarter. He had multiple carries in the first quarter. Despite gaining seven and 14 yards on individual carries, Robinson finished the day with 9 total carries for 31 yards. He had a success rate of 33.3% (you want to be in the 40s), with a -1.39 rushing EPA. In fairness to Robinson, his longest run came when he was hit in the backfield. Robinson bounced off the tackle and picked up 14 yards. Three of his runs gained no yards or were losses. Jordan Elliott The 49ers started Elliott and Kalia Davis in 2025. Davis is currently on the Browns’ injured reserve. Elliott played 20 snaps for Robert Saleh’s Titans. He recorded two tackles and a run stop. Interestingly enough, Elliott dropped into coverage and was responsible for a reception. Unsurprisingly, Elliott did not generate a pass rush on nine snaps. Rob Beal Beal, now going by Rob, played 29 snaps total. Fourteen of those came on defense, while the rest came across different special teams units. Beal is in the rotation, as he played as early as the first quarter for the Dolphins. His lone tackle came seven yards downfield, where he tackled Ashton Jeanty. Beal did not record any pressure stats. Skyy Moore Moore played 16 snaps with the Packers. They gave him a reverse in the first quarter, but a penalty negated it. Moore is Green Bay’s returner. He had one target. On 4th & 2, Jordan Love missed Moore with 1:31 remaining. The game was likely over, but Moore looked like he had a step on the defender and could’ve scored. Dee Winters Winters played 39 snaps for Dallas in his debut. Like most Dallas defenders, Winters looked lost. He recorded four tackles and a stop, but also allowed all four of his targets to be completed for 40 yards, good for a quarterback rating of 108.3. Winters was the Cowboys’ fourth-lowest-graded defender, per PFF. I thought Dee Winters had the roughest go among the DAL LBs vs NYG. Too complacent taking on blocks, failed to fall back with post-snap motion multiple times, not on the same page with DBs in coverage multiple times. Missed a tackle. Forgettable debut. #Cowboys . — John Owning (@JohnOwning) September 14, 2026

title: Colin Kaepernick has some things to say about Trent Baalke
summary: One of the many stories still incomplete is what happened during Jim Harbaugh’s tenure with the San Francisco 49ers from 2011-2014. Then it all just disappeared. Harbaugh […]
full_text: (Photo by Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the many stories still incomplete is what happened during Jim Harbaugh’s tenure with the San Francisco 49ers from 2011-2014. The 49ers went to three straight NFC Championship Games and a Super Bowl, riding a ferocious defense and (for two of those championships, anyway) Colin Kaepernick under center. Then it all just disappeared. Harbaugh mutually parted ways with the 49ers, followed by numerous retirements and releases. Kaepernick stayed with the team until he and the 49ers parted ways when Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch came in as head coach and general manager, respectively. So what happened? As time went on and news bits came out, almost everything pointed to Trent Baalke, Lynch’s predecessor. Reports documented a power struggle between Baalke and Harbaugh. It didn’t help that Baalke had the ear of 49ers owner and CEO Jed York. Kaepernick has an autobiography, “The Perilous Fight,” coming out and has been doing some interviews to promote it. One with The San Francisco Standard’s Scott Ostler has a few nuggets about Kaepernick’s time with the 49ers, but this answer about his interactions with Baalke seems to be something that continues to add to the GM’s marred tenure with the team: I don’t think Trent was a fan of mine before I walked in the door. In part because, from my understanding, Harbaugh stood on the table and was like, “We need to draft him.” I think there was a power struggle, or a sense of toes being stepped on. I know Trent didn’t agree with me playing over Alex. Also, coming off the 2013 season, I had talked to Harbaugh about ways that we could get better, talked about going to the combine with him to look at receivers together, trying to turn over every stone to get over this hump to win a championship. Harbaugh’s like, “I love it, let’s do it.” Then I get a call from Trent. He says, “Hey, you shouldn’t be going to the combine with Harbaugh. You need to call him and tell him you’re not going. Also, don’t tell him we had this conversation.” To me, that kind of encapsulates how he operated. Those kinds of things, I would say, are manipulative tactics. I don’t think they’re beneficial for anybody. I know other players had issues [with Baalke] as well. I don’t view him as a good person. This is the first time, to my recollection, a 49ers player has gone on record about Baalke’s actual GM practices rather than how difficult he is to deal with . The closest we’ve gotten is reports and sources about what’s been going on in the front office. A good example is that during Chip Kelly’s single year as head coach , he wanted to draft now-Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott. Baalke said no—and provided zero reason why. Given that Baalke was fired from the Jacksonville Jaguars during their head coaching search because no candidate wanted to work with him, it suggests this behavior was a pattern, not an isolated incident. Baalke’s draft picks were laughably bad, so his refusal to let anyone help him make decisions is clearly a flex of power, but it could also stem from insecurity, based on what Kaepernick has said. This also checks out with Baalke’s refusal to want to draft a second quarterback after Harbaugh’s staff felt it was time to move on. We’re still waiting for the documentary of just how the 49ers crumbled. It’s well documented that Harbaugh is difficult to deal with, but it’s been made clear that Baalke is just as—if not more—difficult. I’d love just to know how that relationship was managed for four years and what exactly led to all this. Maybe Kaepernick’s biography will pull back the curtain just a bit more.

title: Dolphins offer 49ers a chance to build on their most surprising Week 1 strength
summary: That the 49ers are massive favorites over the Miami Dolphins in Week 2 will be absolutely no surprise to anybody. San Francisco is coming off a huge win over the Super Bowl favorites, while the Dolphins are likely to be in the conversation for the first overall pick and were beaten comfortably by the Las […]
full_text: Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect That the 49ers are massive favorites over the Miami Dolphins in Week 2 will be absolutely no surprise to anybody. San Francisco is coming off a huge win over the Super Bowl favorites, while the Dolphins are likely to be in the conversation for the first overall pick and were beaten comfortably by the Las Vegas Raiders in their opener. Still, given the 49ers have the added issue of recovering from their travel back from Australia, it’s not too much of a stretch to consider this a potential ‘trap game’ for the 49ers. But Kyle Shanahan and his staff are unlikely to feel the need to remind the team about taking the matchup seriously and, if the 49ers perform at anywhere close to the levels they produced in Melbourne, then the meeting with the Dolphins should offer a significant opportunity for them to have more success in what was a surprising area of strength in Week 1. Despite the concerns about the 49ers’ defensive line depth going into the season, the San Francisco pass rush impressed in the 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams, albeit without recording a sack of Matthew Stafford. Indeed, the 49ers racked up a 41 percent pressure rate against the Rams, with that number better than any single-game pressure rate they managed throughout 2025. And, going against the Dolphins’ offensive line, the 49ers’ defensive front has a clear opportunity to build on that performance and register some sacks, even in a game in which they will be going against a mobile quarterback in Malik Willis. Miami’s offensive line endured an extremely difficult Week 1 in the Dolphins’ loss to the Raiders, surrendering five sacks, with Willis pressured 17 times in a difficult debut for the former Green Bay Packers quarterback. While Maxx Crosby did the bulk of the damage with two sacks, all three of the Raiders top edge rushers were able to get impressive push against Miami, Crosby (3.58), Kwity Paye (3.84) and Malcolm Koonce (3.9) all had average separation from the quarterback on pass rushing plays that was well under the league average of 4.58 yards, per NextGen Stats. In other words, the Raiders’ top outside pass rushers each had consistent success shrinking the pocket for Willis, with their performances likely to offer encouragement to Niners defensive end Nick Bosa and the rest of a defensive line that produced an encouraging Week 1 showing. With doubts surrounding the depth on the interior and on the edge, the 49ers entered this season with plenty of concern externally about their defensive line. One game against the Rams will not allay those doubts and a strong performance versus Miami in Week 2 will not do so either. However, if the 49ers’ front can shake off the effects of their travel and take advantage of a very favorable matchup, it could be a confidence-boosting step towards this group exceeding expectations.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: NFL Week 2 power rankings: 49ers behind Rams despite Week 1 win
summary: We had a fun NFL slate wrap up in blowout fashion on Monday night, as the Kansas City Chiefs beat the Denver Broncos 31-10 to cap a memorable Week 1. There were some timely upsets, some close battles, and then some blowouts between good teams. Kansas City had one of those games. The San Francisco […]
full_text: (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) We had a fun NFL slate wrap up in blowout fashion on Monday night, as the Kansas City Chiefs beat the Denver Broncos 31-10 to cap a memorable Week 1. There were some timely upsets, some close battles, and then some blowouts between good teams. Kansas City had one of those games. The San Francisco 49ers had another when they beat the Los Angeles Rams 27-7 back on Thursday night in Australia, marking one of the best Week 1 wins on the slate (if not the best). Heading into the season, the 49ers were viewed as the clear No. 3 team in the NFC West. After one week, they arguably look the strongest, with the Seattle Seahawks dealing with an injury to quarterback Sam Darnold. Week 2 power rankings in the NFL were released by several publications on Tuesday morning. Let’s take a look at where the 49ers rank among the pack. ESPN: No. 5 San Francisco jumped up four spots from No. 9 to No. 5 in ESPN’s Week 2 power rankings, although they remained third in the NFC West. Here’s the top five teams on their poll: 1. Buffalo Bills 2. Seattle Seahawks 3. Baltimore Ravens 4. Los Angeles Rams 5. San Francisco 49ers Despite the win over the Rams, the 49ers remained one spot behind them in the rankings. They also remained behind the Bills, who beat the Houston Texans 36-31 on the road in a thriller, as well as the Seahawks and Baltimore Ravens. While the Seahawks (No. 2), Bills (No. 3), and Rams (No. 1) were all in the preseason top-five, the 49ers (No. 9) and Ravens (No. 8) both made considerable jumps after Week 1. The Athletic: No. 1 The Athletic’s Chad Graff and Josh Kendall wasted no time anointing the 49ers at No. 1, pointing to their offense after the 27-7 beatdown last Thursday. “After the franchise’s drama-filled offseason and with questions about the aging roster, the 49ers had no trouble moving the ball against the Rams. Brock Purdy threw for three touchdowns, the running game (including rookie Kaelon Black) looked good and Raheem Morris’ defense was great. It’d be hard to draw up a better start.” Here’s how the top five looked: 1. San Francisco 49ers 2. Seattle Seahawks 3. Buffalo Bills 4. Chicago Bears 5. Baltimore Ravens The Rams fell from No. 1 to No. 6 here, followed by the Kansas City Chiefs, who jumped from No. 14 to No. 7. FOX Sports: No. 7 Despite the marquee win, the 49ers didn’t move considerably here in FOX Sports’s power rankings, jumping just three spots from No. 10 to No. 7. Here’s all the teams ahead of them. 1. Baltimore Ravens 2. Chicago Bears 3. Seattle Seahawks 4. Buffalo Bills 5. Los Angeles Rams 6. Cincinnati Bengals All of these teams were ahead of the 49ers in FOX Sports’s preseason power rankings. “They heard all the talk about the dream team Rams and became L.A.’s worst nightmare. If the Niners stay healthy, they actually could end up the best team in the dangerous NFC West,” FOX Sports’s Ralph Vacciano wrote. USA Today: No. 2 The 49ers jumped up five spots in USA Today’s power rankings up to No. 2, trailing only the Seattle Seahawks, who beat the New England Patriots in the season opener without Sam Darnold. “Their “Sleep tight” tweet served as the mic drop of Week 1 after the Niners, who were at least close to full strength after juggling so many injuries in 2025, stuck it to the apparently jet-lagged Rams in Australia,” USA Today’s Nate Davis wrote. “The NFC West is already shaping up as a three-way heavyweight bout once again, and the Niners − if healthy − have certainly shown they’ve got the goods to be a Super Sunday threat.” Behind them were the Buffalo Bills, Chicago Bears, and Los Angeles Rams. The Niners definitely surprised most in Week 1, having strong play to go in the trenches to support their well-rounded team. Things are a lot different in Week 2, as they’ll host the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, where they’re already a massive 13.5-point favorite.

title: Titans must start Cedric Gray, Anthony Hill at LB in Week 2
summary: The only positive takeaway from the Tennessee Titans’ Week 1 blunder was the performance of rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. The 60th overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft recorded a team-high 16 tackles. The Titans need to start Hill and Cedric Gray at linebacker versus the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. Hill started in […]
full_text: Aug 4, 2026; Nashville, TN, USA; Tennessee Titans linebacker Anthony Hill (53) talks with the media during training camp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The only positive takeaway from the Tennessee Titans’ Week 1 blunder was the performance of rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. The 60th overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft recorded a team-high 16 tackles. The Titans need to start Hill and Cedric Gray at linebacker versus the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. Hill started in place of Gray, who failed to clear concussion protocol in time for Week 1 after suffering an off-field leisure accident . That put Hill in the starting lineup next to veteran Cody Barton. The rookie took full advantage of the opportunity. Head coach Robert Saleh confirmed that Gray has already cleared protocol during his Monday press conference. That opens up the possibility for the Titans to start Gray and Hill in Week 2. They must be bold enough to send Barton to the bench, especially versus an athletic Eagles offense. Hill didn’t just register 16 tackles. He appeared to have forced and recovered a fumble in Jets territory when he punched the ball loose from sophomore tight end Mason Taylor. The refs called an incomplete pass on the field, and surprisingly upheld that call once Saleh challenged it. Even with his takeaway confusingly stolen from him, Hill still made impact plays. The former Texas standout had a really nice pass breakup on a peanut-punch, breaking up a pass for a Jets running back on a wheel route. Hill also shoved Geno Smith out of bounds short of the sticks on a third-and-short, forcing a fourth down. The rebuilding Titans are still stacking young talent. They aggressively traded up for Hill, nabbing him with a second-round pick they initially didn’t have. That decision paid immediate dividends in Week 1. The Titans were terrible, but Hill was excellent. Hopefully he starts opposite Gray versus the Eagles in Week 2.

title: 3 OT prospects the Titans already have to know after brutal Week 1
summary: The Tennessee Titans could not protect quarterback Cam Ward in Week 1. The sophomore top overall selection was under routine pressure in Sunday’s 23-10 loss to the New York Jets. Ward was pressured on nearly 70 percent of his dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Ward actually did a pretty nice job navigating that pressure. […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - JANUARY 22: New General Manager Mike Borgonzi of the Tennessee Titans looks on during an introductory press conference at Ascension Saint Thomas Sports Park on January 22, 2025 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Tennessee Titans could not protect quarterback Cam Ward in Week 1. The sophomore top overall selection was under routine pressure in Sunday’s 23-10 loss to the New York Jets . Ward was pressured on nearly 70 percent of his dropbacks, according to Pro Football Focus. Ward actually did a pretty nice job navigating that pressure. He was only sacked on three occasions, and two of them were decisions to eat the football because nobody was open. Nonetheless, the Titans’ offensive line was putrid. The tackle play was especially bad from Dan Moore Jr. and JC Latham. They allowed two pressures apiece. Moore was beaten badly around the edge by Will McDonald IV for the third sack on Ward. The way-too-early indication is that the Titans will be in the market for at least one new starting offensive tackle next offseason. Possibly with a very early selection in the 2027 NFL Draft. With that in mind, we’ve identified the three offensive tackle prospects the Titans already need to be familiar with. Trevor Goosby, Texas Trevor Goosby was excellent at protecting Arch Manning in Texas’ Saturday’s stunning come-from-behind victory over Ohio State. Goosby possesses the prototypical length for an offensive tackle and displays incredible play strength on a snap-by-snap basis. He especially generates so much power as a run blocker, and effectively uses that power and length to keep the edge protected in the passing game. Jordan Seaton, LSU Jordan Seaton transferred to LSU this season from Colorado. Through two weeks, he’s handled the step up in competition in flawless fashion. Seaton looks like a natural in Lane Kiffin’s offense. He’s an extremely athletic blocker who thrives in space thanks to high-level foot quickness. Trevor Lauck, Iowa Death, taxes, and Iowa producing offensive lineman. Trevor Lauck is the next blocker in the Hawkeyes’ rich history. A mature tackle prospect, he’s technically sound and smart on tape. Think Peter Skoronski, but at tackle. Lauck isn’t an elite athlete, nor does he have elite length, but his skill set is just so technically advanced.

title: Commanders mailbag: Discussing Dan Quinn, Jayden Daniels, Mike Sainristil
summary: The Commanders showed well in Philadelphia but not well enough to beat the Eagles. That Week 1 affair proves that every snap counts, with but a few explosives allowed and offensive opportunities missed separating a win from a loss.   Washington’s intriguing to be sure, with plenty left to learn about this group as we […]
full_text: The Commanders showed well in Philadelphia but not well enough to beat the Eagles. That Week 1 affair proves that every snap counts, with but a few explosives allowed and offensive opportunities missed separating a win from a loss. Washington’s intriguing to be sure, with plenty left to learn about this group as we move forward. There are plenty of questions about the state of the franchise and what must be better heading into Week 2 in this Wednesday mailbag. That’s to everyone who suggested a discussion topic. Let’s get right to them, right now: “Let’s say the Commanders have a respectable season, but miss out on a Wildcard spot. Does DQ stay? Where is the line for Peters? I’m not asking this question to be inflammatory, and in general I’m in favor of keeping continuity and ideally keeping AP and DQ in that scenario. To me, even if our team was extremely good, it would be an uphill battle given our division and general NFC playoff picture. But the clock keeps ticking. Would love to hear the HH writers’ thoughts on this.” — “Evgeny Last Words?” I ponder this question a bit just before the season and it generally follows Evgeny’s logic. I think the Commanders want Dan Quinn and Adam Peters sticking together. They’re also on different timelines. I don’t think Adam Peters’ seat is even warm. He’ll be around another cycle at least, even if things go really bad in 2026 (which they won’t). It’s Quinn who might be in trouble . Anything close to a 2025 repeat and I think we’re covering a coaching search next year. If the Commander reach eight wins with this schedule – that’s a three-victory improvement – and DQ still has buy-in, he sticks. Six or possibly seven and things get murky. I believe continuity’s the goal here. Quinn’ the culture builder. If his coordinator hires develop and his game management is good, you stick with what you’ve got. If not, you’ll likely start all over with a new head and another new play caller for Daniels. “May be too early but does the FO plan to extend JD after this season or drag the process out through year 4 and into the option year (year 5). Personally, I think if they do it after this season, they will probably save money in the long run; ie the most lucrative contract in NFL history this year will be less than the most lucrative contract in NFL history next year.” — DGOLD510 One thing the NFL’s quarterback won’t do is go down. There’s only inflation on the horizon here, and the amount someone gets paid is far less about their ranking among the NFL’s best and far more about who’s next. While there is some merit-based pay involved here, there’s no way Jayden Daniels gets cheaper the farther we go from his next extension. The smart play here is to extend him when he’s first eligible , following this season. The team should have some leverage for that first season – even Daniels doesn’t want to play two more seasons without generational guarantees – but it makes sense to lock something down then. The Patriots, Bears and (possibly) Broncos will be thinking the same thing next offseason, so those salaries should be bunched together. If you’re Washington, you want Daniels done before Caleb Williams and maybe even Drake Maye, so those contracts don’t elevate costs. One situation where you may want to put the contract off a year: If Daniels has a 2025 repeat, where he can’t stay healthy. That might create some doubt in a long-term deal. If Daniels is healthy, he’ll play well and deserve the money given. I think it’s part of the front office plan to get it done next offseason. They’ve budgeted for it. I think they’re prepared to lock Daniels down. And as for a more game-oriented question, how has Caleb Downs looked so far and do they think he will be a major factor in this week’s game? — B&G Beatdown Caleb Downs looked pretty, pretty good in Week 1, to the tune of eight tackles, a sack and a forced fumble. The Dallas defense overall was putrid, but Downs can play. He’s a do-everything safety that must be accounted for and game-planned against. The Dallas defense, overall, looks exploitable. Who’s available at corner to replace Mikey? Me in Madden, he’s gone. — ComplainingIsAPayne Mark Tyler wrote about Mike Sainristil one in Tyler’s Take and advocated for a quick hook. Here’s what he wrote: “Mikey has to be benched. There is no other nice way to put this. Amik Robertson played a heck of a game against Philly on Sunday, but the worry is who plays outside opposite him until Trey Amos can return off injured reserve . What I would do is elevate Terell Smith , the 6-foot, 207-pound athletic corner from the practice squad and get him up to speed quickly. For now, Rasul Douglas showed enough against Philly to hold down that outside spot, but Smith may be the better long-term option if he’s finally back to health following a torn patellar during the 2025 preseason .” Adding more to Douglas’ plate sounds like the immediate option, with coaches keeping a close eye to see how Sainristil responds to a relative demotion. There are enough slot options to account for this move, especially with CeeDeeLamb and George Pickens looming on Sunday. I have covered Smith before and he’s a really good player. The Commanders will know how his knee is doing and whether he was the same player he was before the injury. It was an excellent practice-squad pickup that will pay off at some point this season. Dan Quinn is normally reserved regarding public player criticism, but he said Sainristil’s two big plays allowed were unacceptable. The Commanders simply can’t have that, when there are other options in wait while Amos gets healthy.

title: Commanders free agency: Washington reportedly signing veteran center/guard

full_text: The Commanders are reportedly signing veteran interior offensive lineman Lucas Patrick , who has extensive experience playing center and both guard spots. The knee injury might’ve necessitated the facility visit, allowing it to be examined before signing. As a matter of process, Patrick’s base salary is not guaranteed after signing post-Week 1. The addition’s corresponding move will be known later on Wednesday. The Commanders have struggled to find interior depth, especially at the center spot. Patrick is an established pro, but we’ll have to see how he fits and what he’s able to contribute once he works into the Commanders culture and position group. title: Commanders: No need for Jayden Daniels to be Superman…until there is
summary: The Daily Slop – 16 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Washington Sun The […]
full_text: Nov 14, 2024; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) runs with the football against the Philadelphia Eagles during the first quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Eric Hartline-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Daily Slop – 16 September 2026 Editor’s note: Each day, Hogs Haven compiles a collection of articles, podcasts & tweets from around the web to keep you in touch with the Commanders, the NFC East, the NFL and sports in general, with a sprinkling of other stuff. Enjoy! Commanders links Articles Washington Sun The Commanders’ Dilemma: Protect Jayden Daniels or Let Him Loose? In Week 1, Washington’s young quarterback stuck to a new script until his team needed a hero In a perfect world, the Commanders wouldn’t have to choose between keeping their franchise quarterback healthy and winning games. In a perfect world — such as the one they inhabited in 2024, when Daniels was a spectacular rookie and the Commanders were a 12-5 juggernaut — they can accomplish both objectives. But here, at the start of the 2026 season, it’s already feeling like something close to a binary choice. And for most of Sunday night’s entertaining game, it felt like the Commanders were unsure which side of that line they wanted to occupy. For the first three quarters Sunday night, the Commanders mostly stuck to that script. And what did that get them? A 17-9 deficit. Nine completions in 24 attempts for Daniels, for a total of 65 passing yards. No sacks, but no touchdown passes. Their longest play from scrimmage at that point was for 15 yards. They were 2 for 11 on third-down conversions. Terry McLaurin, their two-time Pro Bowl wideout, had two targets and no catches. They absolutely, positively, 100% don’t want Daniels to feel like he has to go out there and win games for them with his unique blend of athleticism, artistry and aerial acumen. Until they absolutely, positively, 100% need him to do exactly that. And then, it seems, they are willing to hold their breath and turn him loose. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE Jayden Daniels showing off the moves 😮‍💨 WASvsPHI on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/OEZovvBO38 — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Riggo’s Rag Joshua Josephs keeps turning limited Commanders chances into lasting impressions Josephs didn’t generate many headlines, certainly not compared to Styles, Williams, and even special-teams ace Tyler Owens . He played only 13 snaps on defense, but the Tennessee product stood out a couple of times. Just how much time Josephs will see on the field now that edge rusher Dorance Armstrong Jr. is back from his one-game suspension remains to be seen. But if the No. 147 overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft keeps making this kind of impact against elite-level tackles like Johnson, it’ll stay on the radar. At the very least. These Week 1 flashes weren’t without substance, either. Josephs was among the standout performers at training camp , displaying the speed, length, and dynamism that convinced the Commanders to take a chance. He backed this up in the preseason, even scoring a touchdown by bursting onto a loose football against the Detroit Lions. To read more of this article, CLICK HERE The Athletic (paywall) His stunning special teams effort went viral. To Tyler Owens, it was ‘just a normal football play’ It wasn’t the first time Tyler Owens ripped down the field to slam a returner to the ground. It wasn’t even the first time in that game. But in the second quarter of the Washington Commanders’ loss to the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, Owens’ play as a special-teams gunner made him a household name literally overnight. Facing a vise, or double-team, in punt coverage, Owens split Eagles jammers Jonathan Jones (a former Commander) and Darius Cooper by essentially tossing them to the side and leaving them in his wake as he pursued returner Britain Covey — whom he then lifted off the ground and body-slammed at Philadelphia’s 38-yard line. “I feel like it was just a normal football play out there,” Owens told The Athletic on Tuesday. Against the Eagles on Sunday, we saw that athleticism stand out in a number of different situations. As soon as the ball is snapped, Styles triggers and gets a full head of steam as he works up to Barkley. Barkley has to abandon the play-action fake because Styles covers the ground so quickly. title: Washington Commanders at the Cowboys in Week 2: Inside the Matchup
summary: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates […]
full_text: Back in June and early July, HH veteran writer Bill-in-Bangkok, offered a week-by-week preview via the 5 O’Clock Club of the Washington Commanders regular season schedule for 2026. As we roll into the actual games during the regular season, Hogs Haven will revisit each of these previews with John Portis adding additional thoughts and updates as we go inside the matchup to get you ready for every opponent the Commanders face in 2026. From John Portis: The Washington Commanders are coming off a tough 22-24 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles at Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday that was a golden opportunity to start a tough early schedule well. Unfortunately, head coach Dan Quinn and his team came up just short. The Commanders now head to Arlington, Texas, trying to avoid going 0-2 in the NFC East (and overall) to start the season. The Cowboys will look to do the same after a loss to John Harbaugh’s Giants, who got out to an early lead and never gave it back on the way to a 28-20 victory over Dallas Sunday night. The matchup between the NFC East rivals features two rookie coordinators on opposite sides of the ball in David Blough and Christian Parker, both of whom are looking to get things on track after a rough outing in Week 1. The Commanders’ offense looked out-of-sync and ineffective for the first three quarters versus a tough Eagles defense that was able to generate pressure with only a four-man rush while bracketing Washington’s wide receivers downfield. Blough finally switched to an up-tempo, shotgun-style approach late in the game, and Jayden Daniels will look to build off his 9-of-11, 100-yard, two-touchdown fourth-quarter performance in Sunday afternoon’s game. Dallas would appear to offer the perfect opportunity to do so. The Cowboys’ defensive overhaul was a complete disaster in Parker’s debut, which ranked 571 among 574 total defensive performances since Week 1 of 2025 based on EPA/drive and, at one point, the Giants successfully ran the same play four times in a row. The Giants ran the SAME PLAY 4x in a row and the Cowboys STILL can't stop them 😭 pic.twitter.com/cGidMoavhU — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) September 14, 2026 Parker’s defense showed more finesse than physicality, and New York’s offense dominated the Cowboys D to the tune of 394 yards of total offense, converting 9-of-11 third downs, which let the Giants maintain a chokehold on time of possession. Dallas failed to get much pressure on Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart and, unlike the Philadelphia Eagles, only generated two pressures on four-man rushes during the evening. Blough should have plenty of opportunities to get his offense on the right track, as the Cowboys’ defense also lost safety Malik Hooker and linebacker DeMarvion Overshown to injuries this week. Conversely, Washington’s defense looked vastly improved under Daronte Jones’ direction, but failed to limit the Philadelphia’s explosive playmaking ability, giving up 171 of the Eagles’ 318 total yards on just four plays. The secondary in particular struggled. Dallas’ two big wide receivers George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb will be going against last week’s starters, Amik Robertson and Mike Sainristil, making this a matchup to watch. As Bill noted in June , Brian Schottenheimer’s 2025 offense was one of the most prolific in the NFL, finishing second in the league in both total yards (6,663) and passing yards, but Dallas’ offense got off to a slow start in Week 1. Entering his 11th season, Dak Prescott completed 22 of 34 attempts for just 175 yards . The Cowboys, who had the fewest three-and-outs in 2025, opened Sunday with a three-and-out and Dallas failed to generate a play of more than 17 yards all game, with both George Pickens and CeeDee Lamb having opportunities go through their hands. Running back Javonte Williams also had a poor game, rushing for 41 yards on 12 attempts and drawing a momentum-stealing taunting penalty on his rushing touchdown. If Jones can dial up the pressure early, the Commanders’ defense should be able to set the tone versus the Cowboys. One of the bright spots for Dallas last week was first-round selection Caleb Downs. The safety was popularly mocked to the Commanders before the draft and played 61 total defensive snaps , with eight total tackles, one sack, one forced fumble and just two receptions allowed for seven yards. Washington’s offense will need to the keep their heads on swivels to avoid a play like this one happening to Jayden Daniels. CALEB DOWNS SACK FUMBLE pic.twitter.com/t8nwn7w07n — Underdog NFL (@UnderdogNFL) September 14, 2026 Downs recorded the fastest sack across all of Week 1, taking down Dart in 2.49 seconds. Betting Lines Point Spread : Dallas -3.5 Game Total (Over/Under) : 50.5 points Bill-in-Bangkok’s original preview published June 24th: Week 2 Preview: Washington Commanders at Dallas Cowboys Date: September 20, 2026, 4:25 p.m. ET Location: AT&T Stadium in Arlington, TX ( The two teams close the season when they play again at Northwest Stadium in Landover in Week 18 ) The Dallas Cowboys host the Washington Commanders in Week 2, on September 20, 2026, bringing a fierce and longstanding NFC East rivalry back to AT&T Stadium. Dallas enters the divisional game as a preseason 4.5-point home favorite, but both teams look different than they did last season due to changes in personnel and coaching staff. The All-Time Series Numbers Dallas holds a clear lead in the historic series between the two franchises. Entering this game, the Cowboys have an 81-49-2 all-time record against Washington. Recent history also favors Dallas, as the Cowboys have won 12 of the last 16 matchups. Washington has historically struggled when traveling to Texas. The Commanders are 17-43-2 all-time on the road against the Cowboys, though four of those Washington wins have come since 2014. Dallas Coaching Changes The Cowboys overhauled their defensive coaching staff during the offseason. After finishing with the worst defense in 2025 as measured by points surrendered, team owner Jerry Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer replaced the previous defensive coordinator, Matt Eberflus, with a new hire from another division rival. Christian Parker is the new defensive play-caller. He previously worked as the passing game coordinator/defensive backs coach for the Philadelphia Eagles. A former defensive backs coach under Fangio in Denver (2021) and passing game coordinator in Philadelphia (2024–2025), Parker will likely use foundational Fangio concepts to build his modern defensive schemes that rely on pre-snap 2-high safety alignments to obscure coverage intentions and limit big plays. Similar to Fangio, Parker’s defense is expected to focus on manipulating offenses by shifting coverages after the snap to confuse quarterbacks. He will probably utilize lighter boxes against the run in favor of coverage strength in the secondary, deploying both 3-4 and 4-2-5 alignments with versatile players, and favor rush efficiency (getting to the quarterback with a standard 4-man rush) rather than relying on heavy, exotic blitz packages. His background as a defensive backs coach should heavily influence his packages, expecting cornerbacks and safeties to take on dynamic responsibilities on third downs. Parker is also expected to mix up his front structures and introduce five-man fronts to create pressure and confuse blocking Offensively, Klayton Adams returns to serve as the offensive coordinator under head coach Brian Schottenheimer. The Cowboys kept their offensive coaching staff largely intact, making only a couple of minor tweaks to assistant roles, unlike their complete overhaul on the defensive side of the ball. The 2025 Dallas Cowboys offense was one of the most prolific in the NFL, finishing second in the league in both total yards (6,663) and passing yards. Despite this offensive success, the team finished with a 7-9-1 record because of its historically poor defensive play. Key statistical offensive rankings Total…

full_text: Commanders linebacker Frankie Luvu suffered a minor groin strain during a 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles, Commanders beat writer Ben Standig reported on Monday evening. Citing sources, Standig characterized the strain as mild and that his availability for a Week 2 clash with the host Dallas Cowboys is to be determined. Commanders LB Frankie Luvu's groin injury suffered in Sunday's game at Philadelphia is considered "mild," per source. Availability for Week2 in Dallas TBD. — Ben Standig (@BenStandig) September 15, 2026 Luvu played 29 snaps before suffering the injury, and was replaced by Leo Chenal. The veteran is a team captain and a green-dot-wearing defensive play caller. Rookie Sonny Styles took over as the defensive field general in that game and would do so again if Luvu is unavailable. Head coach Dan Quinn was asked for injury updates on Monday when he talked to reporters. He said the team would know more today, and would give any available updates at tomorrow’s presser, or when the team releases the first injury report of the week. TE Chig Okonkwo ( hamstring ), S Tyler Owens ( ankle ), and LB Jordan Magee ( hamstring ) also left Sunday’s game with injuries. Owens was injured when Jaylin Lane ran into him on a return, while Magee tweaked his hamstring chasing Jalen Hurts on a scramble. The Commanders return to practice Wednesday afternoon and will provide some injury updates. The same can be said about the network of SB Nation communities. We’ve been around for 20-plus years; that’s a lot of comments. The start of football season played a big role in that, of course, but our baseball communities grind it out every day as well. For 20 years we’ve built SB Nation around the idea of community, and that continues to bear itself out with millions of comments per month. There’s no site that exemplifies that more than Hogs Haven. Recently, we made an effort to make it easier to join and comment on our sites with the new SB Nation app . When someone signs up for the app, they can join any teams they want. So, you can merge all of your sports-fan interests into one spot. Let’s say you’re also into Washington Nationals, Capitals and Wizards. You can easily join those feeds to root for and comment on all D.C. sports. Now, let’s say, you’re just into the NFL. It’s fun to see everything that’s happening, especially on the NFL Feed on Sundays with fans of all 32 NFL teams. We made the app with community in mind: quicker to scroll to the comments, faster game day threads and easier to make your own feed post. So, check it out if you haven’t already.

title: Tyler’s Take: How Washington Commanders can fix what’s currently broken
summary: The Commanders opened their season on the road, in what is always a hostile environment in Philadelphia. Despite being heavy underdogs, Washington actually had a very competitive game against the 2025 NFC East champs, having a chance to tie the game in the final minutes. Ultimately, the Commanders fell 24-22 to the Eagles and fans […]
full_text: The Commanders opened their season on the road, in what is always a hostile environment in Philadelphia. Despite being heavy underdogs , Washington actually had a very competitive game against the 2025 NFC East champs, having a chance to tie the game in the final minutes. Ultimately, the Commanders fell 24-22 to the Eagles and fans had many questions about some of the decisions made by this staff after the game’s conclusion — with the majority of them being fair asks. So, what can Washington and head coach Dan Quinn do to fix the current issues on this team? Defensive Backs Cornerback Mike StandRealStill: Mikey is the wart on the toad, at the moment, on an otherwise promising defense. I stood up for the diminutive defender this offseason, but after seeing what I saw Sunday afternoon, my patience has disappeared. He can’t cover an 80-year-old in a Jazzy right now. His tackling and angles to the football leave a LOT to be desired. pic.twitter.com/DTtKpyfAaI — tj (@tballer061) September 14, 2026 This is ABSOLUTELY PATHETIC by Mike Sainristil!!! He’s in man coverage! What the HELL is he doing😡 pic.twitter.com/76vmK3jJbD — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Safety Jeremy Reaves: I love Jeremy Reaves . He’s a great person, leader and special teams player. That should be his role on this team; not as a starting free safety. He lacks the athleticism to make plays consistently in this defense and, although he leaves everything out on the field, that’s just not enough at this level. Washington has had a terrible time stopping opposing tight ends and I fear that trend will continue with Reaves in the lineup. This Reaves as a starting S may have to end very soon pic.twitter.com/1tqlJMaXs5 — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Tyler’s Take — Mikey has to be benched. There is no other nice way to put this. Amik Robertson played a heck of a game against Philly on Sunday, but the worry is who plays outside opposite him until Trey Amos can return off injured reserve . What I would do is elevate Terell Smith , the 6-foot, 207-pound athletic corner from the practice squad and get him up to speed quickly. For now, Rasul Douglas showed enough against Philly to hold down that outside spot, but Smith may be the better long-term option if he’s finally back to health following a torn patellar during the 2025 preseason . There is also the possibility that Fabian Moreau can handle some slot duties in nickel, however I would lean more towards Smith in this role, as he played in the slot a bit in Chicago. At free safety, I would take Reaves out of the starting lineup and give that duty back to Quan Martin. Martin had some bad gaffes last year in Joe Whitt’s horrible scheme, but he had a nice preseason and had earned an opportunity under Jones. I would also have Tyler Owens (who is the team’s best overall athlete) seeing more time in sub packages as that third safety. There can still be packages where Reavo sees some burn, but the snap count should flip to him at 38% or less (he played 100% of the defensive snaps against Philly) with Martin and Owens getting more. This may be getting a bit too aggressive but, if I’m Adam Peters, I’m having conversations with the Steelers for Joey Porter Jr. , following a contract impasse between the team and player. I have one problem with this scenario. The draft is in Washington in 2027 and this team needs to keep their top pick(s). The rumor is Pittsburgh wants two first round picks for Porter and, if that’s the case, I hope Peters hangs up the phone. But if there is a way to get him for, say, a second-rounder in 2027 and conditional pick in 2028 or a player, I may be interested. If Washington could somehow find a way to get Porter and eventually pair him with a healthy Trey Amos, the Commanders may have our secondary figured out for the foreseeable future. Great play by Quan Martin on the screen! pic.twitter.com/Bs3ckI28wh — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Tyler Owens with the big hit on special teams pic.twitter.com/WSDbTZlaOj — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Interior Offensive Line Center Nick Allegretti: Allegretti was extraordinarily bad against Philly, but is anyone really surprised? This is absolutely PATHETIC by Allegretti😡 Thankfully a penalty against Philly saved the play pic.twitter.com/01eLF6ma0l — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 The much talked about “center by default” was a human turnstile against the Eagles front. The issue here is that Adam Peters screwed up the situation so badly that there is really not a viable option to step in and take over center duties. Despite having better functional play-strength, rookie Matt Gulbin is likely not ready and very well could fare worse than Allegretti against the beasts Washington faces in the NFC East. Left guard Chris Paul: Chris Paul wasn’t quite as bad as his running mate to the right, but he remains a liability up front. He lacks the lateral athleticism to function adequately as both a zone run blocker and pass protector. Much like Allegretti, he’s currently the best of some bad options. My GOODNESS Chris Paul is absolutely destroyed by the swim move and Allegretti is too slow to even help pic.twitter.com/isUQBddixN — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 14, 2026 Tyler’s Take — Center and left guard are going to need a lot of help to get through the season. Sliding protection to the left side could help Paul, however that is not always an option based on what the defensive front is showing. One option is leaving a running back in to help pass protect, but that only works if he doesn’t have to pick up a free rusher elsewhere. Like I mentioned above, inserting the rookie Gulbin may result in more trouble than Washington currently has, so unless and until he’s both physically and mentally ready, the wait may have to continue. There is one other option for left guard, and that would result in elevating Esa Pole from the practice squat to play left tackle and moving Coleman back inside to guard. This seems a bit far-fetched, too, and I don’t think the staff would consider this route unless an injury were to occur. My conclusion would be to leave a running back in to help AND get some more designed rollouts in the passing game that allow Jayden Daniels to get outside the pocket and either have the option to run or throw. Quick passes and designed screens can also help in this regard — just don’t ask either Allegretti or Paul to get outside to block for them. Wide Receiver Dyami Brown: Quinn decided to have Dyami Brown active while keeping both Treylon Burks and Luke McCaffrey inactive. Brown was the only active receiver to not record a stat in the game. And let’s not act like his blocking in the run game was anything to laud. The Eagles corners are fast and physical, and they easily locked down Brown on most of his routes (as was evident from All-22 film). Tyler’s Take — I think this one is pretty easy. I would activate Burks and let him work the intermediate areas of the field with his outstanding play strength and big body. Tight end Chig Okonkwo and Burks would put a lot more pressure on linebackers and safeties, which could open up space for others. He also shows to be a much better blocker in the run game. I would also make sure rookie Antonio Williams sees MUCH more than 37% of the offensive snaps. Williams is the best Washington receiver on the day so far pic.twitter.com/NPy6yONjVv — Tiller56 (Hogs Haven) (@Tiller56) September 13, 2026 Offensive Play Calling David Blough: Blough had a rough debut against coordinator Vic Fangio and the Eagles much heralded defense. He and Daniels were not on the same page for the better part of three quarters, and it took a throwback effort in the fourth for Daniels to finally find his groove and get Washington’s passing game on track. Unfortunately, it was too-little, too-late for Washington. Tyler’s Take — I really liked Blough’s…
