title: Colts' D looked lost vs. Ravens, and Patrick Mahomes is next
summary: Communication problems hurt the Colts vs. Lamar Jackson, and that likely piqued Patrick Mahomes' curiosity.
full_text:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Quarterback Lamar Jackson casually broke the huddle and his Baltimore Ravens offense took its place in a tight, two-tight-end formation.

 Meanwhile, the  Indianapolis Colts ' defense across the line of scrimmage was in a state of chaos. Players were scrambling to get lined up, pointing, yelling. Confusion ruled.

 Jackson, likely taking notice, quickly called for the snap. He executed a hard play-action fake to running back Derrick Henry , then bootlegged to his left. Jackson found receiver Zay Flowers a couple of steps ahead of defender Justin Walley , hitting Flowers for a 49-yard gain that took the ball to the 2-yard line.

 Somewhere, Patrick Mahomes likely smiled.

 Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs host the Colts on Sunday night (8:20 ET, NBC), and it is not difficult to imagine Mahomes taking pleasure in seeing the Colts' many defensive miscues in Sunday's blowout loss to the Ravens. Indianapolis' defense looked lost, giving up its most total yards in nearly three seasons (506).

 Because, according to players, it was lost.

 "We're not getting the line right, being late to our alignments and just [not] executing the little details of the defense," defensive tackle DeForest Buckner said. "That was our biggest challenge."

 Embarrassing miscommunications that led to costly plays by Baltimore defined the Colts' 2026 debut, and it has left defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo to rectify things ahead of the team's Week 2 meeting with the crafty Mahomes.

 

 Among the things he'll be examining: Whether veteran safety Cam Bynum should continue to handle defensive communication, including wearing the helmet transmitter that allows Anarumo to share info with him from the sideline.

 The Colts are the rare team that has attempted to use a player other than a linebacker to handle sideline communication. Whether it was a good decision remains to be seen.

 "We make sure that it's certainly not just on Cam, but we've got to evaluate everything we do," Anarumo said, adding, "Cam did a phenomenal job for the first game, but I want to look at everything."

 The identity of the player wearing the helmet transmitter is not something fans typically obsess over, but the role is critical. Teams may designate one player to wear a helmet transmitter, denoted by the "green dot" on the helmet, to receive one-way communication from a coach. That is how Anarumo relays defensive calls and coverages to his unit, just as offensive coaches do with quarterbacks.

 In nearly all cases leaguewide, linebackers handle this responsibility because they are positioned in the middle of the defense. Rookie CJ Allen , the Colts' second-round pick, was projected to be the starting middle linebacker and was expected to wear the transmitter this season. But those plans fell through when Allen missed time with injuries in training camp and the preseason, leading coaches to determine he is not ready to be a starter. The Colts instead plan to use a rotation of linebackers, so it was not ideal to have one specific linebacker tasked with the job of sideline communication.

 So Anarumo turned to one of his trusted veterans instead. Bynum was caught off guard, to say the least.

 

 "I didn't even know defensive backs did that," Bynum said.

 But Bynum was up for the challenge. He now admits, however, that running the defensive huddle at the speed of a regular-season game proved challenging. Bynum is sometimes the deep safety in the Colts' system, meaning he has to travel a significant distance back to the huddle. Then, he oftentimes must return to the back end of the defense before the ball is snapped.

 "At the end of the day, communication has to be on point," Bynum said. "It's obviously my first time doing it, and I just want to make sure that everybody's always on the same page, and I have to take pride in being able to communicate and relay little messages."

 The Ravens made things even more challenging by using offensive tempo and snapping quickly on multiple occasions. It proved disastrous for the Colts. Anarumo said a majority of Baltimore's explosive plays were related to the Colts being misaligned or to communication issues.

 "You can never lose the explosive battle like we did," he said.

 But the problems could repeat themselves if the Colts aren't better prepared to deal with this issue in Week 2.

 "We were a little lackadaisical, man," cornerback Charvarius Ward said. "So, we can't allow that to happen again. It's, for sure, not the standard."

title: Njoku, Nwosu, Emmanwori, and more - 10 NFL players of Nigerian origin to watch this season
summary: The NFL has long had a significant African presence, but no country is represented quite like Nigeria.
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season is underway, and Nigerians will once again have plenty of reasons to pay attention, with players of Nigerian origin spread across the league, from defending Super Bowl champions to established starters, and former high draft picks looking for breakout seasons.

 The NFL has long had a significant African presence, but no country is represented quite like Nigeria. There are 137 players of African origin across NFL rosters and practice squads at the start of the 2026 season, representing 24 African countries, with Nigeria accounting for 93 of them, more than two-thirds of the total.

 Liberia is a distant second with nine players, followed by Côte d'Ivoire with seven, Cameroon with six and Ghana with five.

 Every NFL team has at least one player of African origin, while Nigerian representation stretches across 29 of the league's 32 teams. Only the Minnesota Vikings , New Orleans Saints and Arizona Cardinals do not have a player of Nigerian origin on their roster or practice squad.

 

 No team has more than the New York Jets . The Jets have eight players of Nigerian origin, including one on the practice squad, with Olu Fashanu , Joseph Ossai and Lagos-born veteran David Onyemata among the most recognizable.

 Those numbers help illustrate how dramatically Nigeria's footprint in American football has grown. The country's NFL connection is no longer represented by a handful of isolated success stories.

 Nigerian-born players and the children of Nigerian immigrants now occupy positions across the league, from quarterbacks and offensive linemen to linebackers, defensive backs and pass rushers.

 Some are already champions. Uchenna Nwosu and Nick Emmanwori helped the Seattle Seahawks win Super Bowl LX last season, while Moro Ojomo and Osa Odighizuwa enter this year on NFC teams with legitimate championship ambitions.

 Foye Oluokun remains one of the league's most productive linebackers, while former high draft picks Olu Fashanu and David Ojabo enter potentially important seasons in their development as potential breakout candidates.

 Jalen Milroe , whose playing time may be considerably more limited but whose position, Nigerian heritage and presence on the defending champions make his development particularly intriguing.

 Several others could have a significant say in who is still playing when Super Bowl LXI arrives in Los Angeles on Feb. 14.

 From the contenders to the challengers and potential breakout players, here are 10 NFL players of Nigerian origin to watch in 2026.

 

 SUPER BOWL CONTENDERS 
 Uchenna Nwosu, Edge, Seattle Seahawks 
 There is probably no better place to start than Nwosu. He is an established NFL veteran, a Super Bowl champion and a significant contributor on a Seattle team trying to win consecutive titles.

 Nwosu played 16 games last season and recorded seven sacks, his best total since registering 9.5 in 2022.

 He played 33 defensive snaps in Seattle's season-opening 13-10 victory over New England, finishing with five tackles and a pass defended as the Seahawks began their title defense by beating the team they defeated in Super Bowl LX.

 At 29, Nwosu is entering a stage where another strong season and another championship run would add considerably to an already successful NFL career.

 Why watch: An established Nigerian-American pass rusher playing significant snaps for the defending champions.

 Super Bowl chances : Excellent.

 Nick Emmanwori, Safety, Seattle Seahawks 
 Nwosu may be the established veteran, but Emmanwori could eventually become the bigger star. The young safety made an immediate impact as a rookie, finishing runner-up for AP Defensive Rookie of the Year and helping Seattle win the Super Bowl.

 At 6-foot-3, Emmanwori possesses unusual size and athleticism for a safety, allowing Seattle to deploy him in multiple roles rather than simply leaving him deep in the secondary.

 The challenge now is the second season. Opposing offenses have a full year of film on him, while expectations are considerably higher than when he arrived in the league. An offseason ankle problem also makes his health worth monitoring early in the season.

 If healthy, Emmanwori has an opportunity to establish himself among the league's emerging defensive stars.

 Why watch: He could make the jump from outstanding rookie to one of the NFL's better young defensive backs.

 Super Bowl chances: Excellent.

 

 Moro Ojomo, DT, Philadelphia Eagles 
 Ojomo has taken a very different route than usual to the NFL. Born in Lagos, he moved to California with his family when he was 8, eventually starred at Texas and was selected by the Philadelphia Eagles in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL draft.

 For players selected that late, simply sticking around is an achievement. Ojomo has done considerably more. He has developed into an increasingly important part of an Eagles defensive front featuring Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis , giving Philadelphia another source of interior pressure.

 That development makes 2026 particularly interesting. Ojomo has already gone from seventh-round project to legitimate NFL contributor. Another step Up the ladder could make him a much more recognizable name beyond Philadelphia.

 Why watch: One of the best development stories among Nigerian-born players in the NFL and now an important piece on a championship contender.

 Super Bowl chances: Very good.

 Osa Odighizuwa, DT, San Francisco 49ers 
 There are flashier names on this list, but few have been more dependable. Odighizuwa played all 17 games in each of his final four seasons with the Dallas Cowboys before moving to San Francisco, establishing himself as one of the league's more durable interior defensive linemen.

 Odighizuwa also comes from a football family. His older brother Owamagbe played in the NFL and now Osa arrives in San Francisco with an obvious assignment.

 The 49ers recorded an NFL-low 20 sacks last season and needed additional help for a defensive front that had lost some of its previous dominance. Odighizuwa provides an established interior presence alongside Nick Bosa .

 His first game suggested that the opportunity will be substantial this season. He started at defensive tackle and recorded two tackles as San Francisco's defense overwhelmed the Rams in a 27-7 season-opening victory in Melbourne. They limited the Rams to just seven points and 290 total yards, forced two turnovers, and limited Matthew Stafford to 155 passing yards

 With fellow starting tackle Alfred Collins lost for the season with a torn patellar tendon, Odighizuwa is now an even more important part of a 49ers defensive front attempting to return to its old standards.

 Why watch: Proven durability, substantial playing time and a new role on a team expecting to contend.

 Super Bowl chances: Very good.

 

 CHALLENGERS 
 Michael Onwenu, OL, New England Patriots 
 Onwenu already knows how close the Patriots came. New England's 2025 season carried them all the way to Super Bowl LX before Seattle ended the run with a 29-13 victory.

 Onwenu remains one of New England's most important offensive linemen and has provided valuable versatility throughout his career, playing both guard and tackle. His role becomes even more important with quarterback Drake Maye established as the centerpiece of the Patriots offense.

 Onwenu began 2026 where he left off, starting at right guard as New England's rebuilt offensive line allowed just two sacks against Seattle in its 13-10 opening-night loss.

 The Patriots still had problems dealing with Seattle's pressure, particularly late, but Onwenu remains the established presence on an offensive line charged with protecting Maye as New England attempts to return to the Super Bowl.

 Why watch: An established Nigerian-American starter protecting one of the AFC's leading young quarterbacks.

 Super Bowl chances: Very good.

title: Best and worst NFL teams' travel: 49ers, Seahawks, Steelers divulge it all
summary: ESPN spoke with several players and team executives about team travel and the feedback that serves as the basis for the latest NFLPA survey grades.
full_text:
As the NFL prepared for its first regular-season game in Australia to open the 2026 season, careful thought was put into how to get the Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers the nearly 8,000 miles from California to Melbourne.

 The league -- with help from the teams -- settled on a Qantas Airbus A380. The planes had 84 lie-flat seats, ensuring each player had a bed on the flight. Each charter flight flew with four pilots, 22 cabin crew and one traveling charter manager on board.

 In comparison, when the Pittsburgh Steelers flew to Dublin in September 2025, they flew on Aer Lingus as part of a partnership with the airline. A player, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, said Aer Lingus was "like Spirit," a low-cost carrier that shut down earlier this year. The player also said that only a handful of players had business class seats, which were allotted by seniority.

 There are no guidelines in the current NFL collective bargaining agreement on team travel, and there hasn't been much to show there's a correct way to do it. The last two times the Rams played internationally, they flew into the country the day before. The result didn't go their way this season against the 49ers, but it did last season in a blowout victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. Teams currently have the freedom to travel when they choose for international games.

 

 It is a topic that is especially important given the NFL's international expansion as the league will play a record nine international games in 2026. The NFL currently has the ability to play up to 11 games outside of North America, including a yearly contest at Wembley Stadium involving the Jaguars based on the current agreement with the NFLPA.

 What appears to matter to players is the accommodations teams dedicated to travel on domestic and international trips. In February, ESPN obtained the results of the NFLPA's 2026 report cards , which are anonymous surveys done annually that include grades on categories with everything from the team's facilities to treatment of families to head coach and general manager.

 In the newest NFLPA surveys, the 49ers received a C-plus in the team travel category and the Rams a B. The Steelers, Philadelphia Eagles and New England Patriots were the only three teams to receive an F. The Miami Dolphins received an A, the highest grade in the category. Among the top four teams in the category -- the Dolphins (A),  New Orleans Saints (A-minus), Seattle Seahawks (A-minus) and Denver Broncos  (A-minus) -- there were common themes about what makes for a positive team travel experience: having personal space and leg room on a flight (including the ability to recline seats to a laying position), the condition of the plane, the amenities available and advance notice given for the team travel schedule. 

 The report cards are based on a survey of 1,759 players (around 80% of the NFL) across the league, administered from Nov. 3 to Dec. 11, 2025.

 This is the fourth year the NFLPA has conducted these surveys. ESPN spoke with more than a dozen players, coaches and front office executives about "team travel" and the feedback that serves as the basis for the NFLPA's grades.

 Linebacker Kaden Elliss , who reunited with the Saints after three seasons with the  Atlanta Falcons , said he doesn't necessarily need "luxury all the time where you go" when traveling with the team, but that it's nice to feel taken care of by the organization on the road.

 "It is nice to know that you give everything you can, you put everything you can into it and it's nice to know and it's very apparent when you have an owner that's willing to do the same," Elliss said. "I think [Saints owner Gayle Benson] just has a really awesome track record of, like, we're going to make sure we want to be the best and we're going to be the best in everything we do, including travel."

 

 

 THE LIE-FLAT SEATS were not the reason Niners wide receiver Mike Evans decided to sign with the 49ers in free agency. But it certainly didn't hurt. In early March, Evans reached out to longtime Niners tight end George Kittle to learn more about how the team is run. Among the many topics that came up was plane seating and how the team travels.

 "He was a big fan of how we traveled with the lay down [seats] stuff and he's like, "Yep, I never had that,'" Kittle said. "And I was like, 'It's crazy, but welcome to the 49ers.'"

 Evans got an early taste of what travel with the Niners will look like when he and his teammates opened the season in Melbourne. Though the NFL began its international series in 2007, this trip required the longest flight NFL teams have ever taken for a regular-season game.

 The two teams handled it differently, with the 49ers landing a week before to practice there. Los Angeles spent almost the same amount of time in the air (29 hours) than on the ground (36 hours) in Melbourne. Although the teams made the final decisions, both head coaches said they talked to players about how they would handle the travel.

 While in Melbourne, 49ers running back Christian McCaffrey and fullback Kyle Juszczyk spent time at the Saint Haven Club, a spa less than a mile away from their hotel.

 There, the team arranged for players to have access to everything from hyperbaric chambers to red light to hot and cold plunge to massage to acupuncture -- "literally everything" the team needed to take care of their bodies almost 8,000 miles from home, Juszczyk said.

 "Honestly, we've had more out here than we usually have [at home]," 49ers defensive end Nick Bosa said.

 The setup was part of the work the NFL and the 49ers did for months in an attempt to make sure the athletes were as prepared as possible to spend their week of travel on the road.

 The 49ers are no strangers to a weeklong stay, as it is something they've done in recent years to acclimate to their travel schedules. In 2022, the Niners spent time in Colorado Springs, Colorado, before playing in Mexico City in an effort to adjust to the altitude. They'll do that again before their Mexico City game against the Vikings in Week 11. San Francisco has also done the same at IMG Academy in Florida (2019) and The Greenbrier Resort in West Virginia (2020, '21 and '22).

 

 When the Steelers flew to Dublin for their Week 4 game last season, they opted to fly on the overnight Thursday to arrive Friday morning before the Sunday game. In comparison, the Jaguars spent the week before they played the Rams last year at a hotel outside of London. 

 The Steelers went straight to the hotel from the airport with a brief window to settle in before practicing at the field on the property. 

 Steelers coaches, a player said, told the players not to fall asleep on the Friday after they landed, a task the player found challenging.

 That player had previously played in an international game with another team and spent the week in Europe. On that trip, the player said he had a lie-flat seat on the plane.

 "I think if they're going to have us travel to the other side of the [world] to produce them some money, then I think they should do us the common courtesy to letting us stay the whole week so we can at least experience the place that we're traveling to," he said. "Y'all want us to make so much money for y'all, but y'all don't care about us enough to say, 'OK, well we're going to take y'all out there, then guess what? We're going to take care of y'all.'

 "I don't know if it's the league owners or if it's the NFL as a whole, but the NFL's always been like that. It's more about how they're viewed outwardly than how we view them inwardly." 

 

 
 THOUGH INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL has been top of mind given the recent trip to Melbourne and the Dallas Cowboys ' Week 3 contest to Rio de Janeiro against the Baltimore Ravens , even domestic travel has its challenges.

title: Kwity Paye makes dream start to Las Vegas Raiders career in NFL opening week
summary: Kwity Paye had a dream debut for the Las Vegas Raiders in one of the standout performances of the first week of the NFL.
full_text:
Kwity Paye had a dream debut for the Las Vegas Raiders in one of the standout performances of the first week of the NFL.

 Paye - a Guinea-born Liberian defensive end - earns our Africa player of the Week nod for the first week of the new NFL season. There were plenty of other stars - either from the continent directly or with directly traceable lineage - who started with a bang.

 Kyle Monangai - a first-generation Cameroonian-American running back - scored a memorable touchdown for the Chicago Bears in their win over the Carolina Panthers .

 

 Jaxon Smith-Njigba - who is of Sierra Leonean descent through his grandparents - gave a timely reminder of why he is the reigning NFL Offensive Player of the Year in the Seattle Seahawks ' win over the New England Patriots .

 Africa Player of the Week: Kwity Paye (Las Vegas Raiders) 
 Paye was involved in three of the five sacks on Malik Willis in his first regular season game for the Raiders after joining from the Indianapolis Colts - ending with a personal tally of two (one sack and two split-sacks, counting for 0.5 each). He additionally notched four quarter-back hits among a total of six tackles.

 The 27-year-old played an integral part in a solid defensive performance as the Raiders beat the Miami Dolphins 27-13.

 Paye pinned the Dolphins back two yards with his very first tackle of the game on the first drive - made together with Taron Johnson on De'Von Achane .

 His first split-sack came on the second Dolphins drive as he and Folorunso Fatukasi - who is of Nigerian descent - brought down Willis.

 Paye picked up another split-sack on Willis with Maxx Crosby early in the fourth quarter to keep the lead at 14 points.

 The last sack of the game on Willis - with around three minutes remaining - was all Paye's and by that stage, it was effectively the cherry on the icing, topping off a tremendous debut.

 

 Africa Moment of the Week: Kyle Monangai (Chicago Bears) 
 Monangai scored a career best 61-yard running touchdown in the Bears' 59-37 win over the Carolina Panthers.

 While the Bears may eventually have won the game by a comfortable 22-point margin, the victory was far from settled at the time of Monangai's marauding run, which stretched the lead from seven to 14 points at the end of the third quarter.

 Monangai's Cameroonian parents grew up loving soccer, but in his second season in the NFL, their son continues to excel at a different type of football.

 Honorable Mentions 
 Jaxon Smith-Njigba gained 122 yards across eight receptions in the Seattle Seahawks' 13-10 win over the New England Patriots, picking up where he left off last season and scoring a touchdown.

 Boye Mafe , the proud son of Nigerian parents, brought down Baker Mayfield and forced a fumble in the Cincinnati Bengals ' 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .

 Foyesade Oluokun , another star with ties to Nigeria, made an interception in the Jacksonville Jaguars ' 34-10 win over the Cleveland Browns .

 Another compatriot, Kingsley Enagbare , made a sack in the New York Jets ' 23-10 over the Tennessee Titans . Elic Ayomanor , who is of Nigerian and Liberian descent, was on the losing side despite scoring a touchdown.

 

 Chuba Hubbard , like Ayomanor, is Canadian and of Nigerian descent. He, too, was on the scoreboard in a defeat in Week 1. Hubbard scored two touchdowns in the Panthers' defeat to the Bears.

 Bobby Okereke - a California-born star of proud Nigerian heritage forced a fumble despite ending up on the losing side. Nigeria-born Princely Umanmielen picked up a sack for the Panthers in defeat.

 Odafe Oweh (a first-generation American of Nigerian descent and a Washington Commanders star) made a sack in the narrow 24-22 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles .

 Donovan Ezeiruaku - also of Nigerian descent - had an impressive performance on defense for the Dallas Cowboys but also ended up on the losing side in a 28-20 defeat to the New York Giants .

 Felix Anudike-Uzomah - yet another player with roots in Nigeria - made a sack for the Kansas City Chiefs in their 31-10 Monday night win over the Denver Broncos .

 Africa-born Player Watch 
 The obvious winner among players born on the continent is Paye this week as he claims Africa Player of the Week honors even ahead of those from the diaspora not born directly in Africa.

 It is not every week that the continent gets to see a performance as spectacular as Paye's, but Africa has undoubtedly advanced in the development of homegrown talent.

 Paye's heroics and Umanmielen's sack for the Panthers aside, Zimbabwe's Nate Landman made eight tackles in the Rams' 27-7 loss to the San Francisco 49ers , though he was injured in the process.

 Landman will hope to be fit for the clash against the Giants - who gave homegrown Nigerian International Player Pathway (IPP) star Basil Chijioke 'CJ' Okoye his team debut in the 28-20 win over the Cowboys.

title: 49ers find needed balance in run game with McCaffrey, Black
summary: McCaffrey had four fewer carries in Week 1 than Black, San Francisco's rookie RB2. What should we expect from this backfield going forward?
full_text:
MELBOURNE, Australia -- More than halfway through the second quarter of Thursday's win over the Los Angeles Rams , San Francisco 49ers center Jake Brendel could feel things turning in his team's direction.

 The Niners were midway through an 86-yard scoring drive, and rookie running back Kaelon Black had just ripped off gains of 9 and 5 yards. From midfield, Brendel turned toward coach Kyle Shanahan on the sideline and waved his arms to suggest he wanted to run the ball, run it again and keep running it until the Rams showed they could at least slow it down.

 "After a few of those good chunk run plays hit, I'm looking right at Kyle, 'Let's go,'" Brendel said. "Let's just keep going. Let's keep dialing them up."

 Shanahan apparently agreed with Brendel's assessment. The success of those plays only yielded more runs, and by the end of San Francisco's 27-7 win, it had 30 attempts for a robust 5.8 yards per rush. That would've been the team's second-best outing for the 2025 season (behind its 5.9 against the Bears in Week 17 ).

 Perhaps more important was how the 49ers got back to their bread and butter. Since trading for Christian McCaffrey  in October 2022, Shanahan has explored finding a legitimate complement to the team's RB1 before either eschewing the idea completely or giving up after potential options failed to produce. Though the Niners only have a one-game sample size, the early returns indicate that Black might be the powerful complement they've long sought next to McCaffrey.

 "I thought they both ran really hard and really well," Shanahan said. "That was the goal for us coming into this, trying to balance it out more."

 

 When McCaffrey is healthy, balance has not been the word anyone would use to describe the 49ers' distribution of carries. The Melbourne game marked the first time a Niner had more rushing attempts (Black had 14) than McCaffrey (10) in a game he started and finished since the 2022 divisional playoffs against the Dallas Cowboys . Black had only one reception compared to McCaffrey's four, but that left them with an even split of 15 touches each for 70 and 88 yards, respectively.

 Black's extensive snaps came as a result of design and a bit because of McCaffrey dealing with cramps during the game, but Black earning such a role after missing a chunk of training camp with an adductor injury speaks volumes for the 24-year-old third-round pick. Especially given the 49ers' recent history of draft misses at the position in the middle rounds.

 "[Black is] a force and he's someone who's going to help our team a whole lot," McCaffrey said. "It was really cool to see him go out there and just do what he does."

 Equally encouraging for the 49ers was that the 1-2 punch got off to a strong start after a disappointing 2025 season on the ground. Last season, the 49ers averaged just 3.8 yards per carry (30th in the NFL), 106.9 yards per game (24th) and 2.04 yards before contact per carry (29th). The yards per carry and yards before contact marks were the worst in a single season since Shanahan took over in 2017 -- and that was with McCaffrey for all 17 games.

 In addition to a more balanced attack, the 49ers also showed creativity with their play design under new run game coordinator Joe Graves. San Francisco threw a variety of motions, including  some that allowed fullback Kyle Juszczyk  to lead block for McCaffrey or Black. The 49ers motioned players on 59% of their offensive plays, the highest rate in any game under Shanahan. They averaged 6.3 yards per rush on 20 attempts using any form of motion.

 San Francisco also took advantage of a schematic curveball from the Rams. According to Brendel, the Niners spent the week preparing for plenty of five-man fronts -- similar to what Los Angeles threw at them in recent matchups. Brendel was surprised when the Rams not only played four down linemen more frequently but were also often in nickel packages (five defensive backs).

 

 On 16 attempts against four or fewer man fronts, the Niners averaged 6.6 yards per attempt. Against nickel and dime (six DBs) looks, San Francisco averaged 6.5 yards per carry .

 "The way that they chose to play us on defense schematically we weren't really expecting," Brendel said. "Most teams are a little bit more scared of our wide zone and our run game."

 As the 49ers continued having rushing success in Melbourne, the offensive line could sense an opportunity to impose its will. In the third quarter, the team averaged 8.4 yards per attempt against the road-weary Rams.

 It was the perfect storm for what the 49ers hope is a reestablishment of their previous levels of dominance on the ground.

 "We felt it from the jump," right tackle Colton McKivitz said. "I definitely think our plan helped us being down here a week and getting our legs. ... We were kind of called out last year for not being a good running team. And this is a good start for us.

 "Obviously, it's Week 1 ... but when you can start with that number of rushing yards against a good defensive front, against a rival, it shows we're going in the right direction."
